papers.title: Gromov hyperbolicity and uniformity
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we first exhibit an example which answers negatively to a question posed by Herron et al. in 2008. That is, there is a rectifiably connected open set in a proper geodesic metric space so that it is Gromov hyperbolic with respect to the quasihyperbolic metric, and its Gromov boundary endowed with a visual metric is naturally bilipschitz equivalent to its metric boundary, but it is not uniform.
  Moreover, two positive answers are given under additional hypotheses. It is shown that a metric space is uniform if and only if it is Gromov hyperbolic and the natural map between its Gromov closure and its metric completion exists and satisfies a relatively quasisymmetric condition. Both bounded and unbounded cases are in our considerations via two different uniformization theorems developed recently by Bonk et al. and the first author, respectively. Finally, we characterize uniform metric spaces with uniformly perfect boundaries in terms of Gromov hyperbolicity and Teichm\"uller's displacement property.

papers.title: A normalization issue in a transmitted form of Bloch's diamond formula: anti-invariant subgroup versus regulator quotient
papers.abstract: Bloch's identity $\int_\gamma\eta(f,g)=D_E((f)\diamond(g))$, relating the regulator of a $K_2$-symbol on an elliptic curve $E/\mathbb{Q}$ to the elliptic dilogarithm of the diamond product of the divisors, is transmitted in the Mahler-measure literature with $\gamma$ generating the anti-invariant subgroup $H_1(E,\mathbb{Z})^-$ and factor $1$ (e.g. Lalin-Ramamonjisoa, Thm. 6). We observe that, when $E(\mathbb{R})$ has one connected component ($\Delta<0$), this reading is incompatible with the published intersection-product normalization (Brunault, Proposition 19): the anti-invariant subgroup then has index $2$ in the regulator quotient $H_1(E,\mathbb{Z})/H_1(E,\mathbb{Z})^+$. The correct statement -- factor $1$ for the quotient generator, hence factor $\iota(E)\in\{1,2\}$ for the subgroup generator, with $\iota(E)=1\iff\Delta>0$ -- follows from Brunault's formula by an elementary index computation. We document the phenomenon twice: on 11.a3 by proved values (a Siegel-unit anchor from [Zheng, arXiv:2609.26119]; the diamond side by Brunault and Bertin), and on 20.a4 by high-precision computation of both integrals against the $q$-series for $D_E$ (subgroup/quotient ratio $2$ to $13$ digits). We also show that Touafek's Theorem 2 (involving a $\Delta<0$ curve) mixes two independent normalizations (subgroup versus quotient, and a $(2\pi)^{-1}$ prefactor versus the bare diamond value), and we identify the two-part reinterpretation making its printed formulas mutually compatible. In the cases we have checked, no Mahler-measure or $D_E$-identity is affected: the main theorem of Lalin-Ramamonjisoa (conductor $17$, $\Delta>0$) and Bertin's proved exotic relations stand untouched, and Touafek's final $D_E$-relation is not contradicted and is numerically supported, though its printed derivation retains the gap described in the text. A systematic audit is beyond the scope of this note.

papers.title: Isosceles sets in Euclidean spaces of dimension nine to twenty-two
papers.abstract: A finite set of points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is isosceles if every three of its points form an isosceles triangle. Erd\H{o}s asked in 1946 for the largest size $\mathrm{iso}(d)$ of an isosceles set in $\mathbb{R}^d$. The answer was known for $d\le 8$, the last cases being due to Ionin. We prove that $\mathrm{iso}(d)=\binom{d+1}{2}+1$ for $9\le d\le 21$ and $\mathrm{iso}(22)=276$, and that the extremal set is unique: for $d\le21$ it is the set of midpoints of the edges of a regular simplex together with its centroid, and for $d=22$ it is the McLaughlin configuration together with its centre. For $10\le d\le22$ every isosceles set with more than $\binom d2+3$ points is a two-distance set or a spherical two-distance set together with its centre, and the number $\binom d2+3$ is attained. The proof combines Blokhuis' decomposition of isosceles sets into mutually orthogonal two-distance sets, for which we give a short self-contained proof (the key step is a special case of Gallai's theorem on edge colourings without rainbow triangles), with the recent determination of the maximum two-distance sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$ for $9\le d\le22$ and with the known maximum sizes of spherical two-distance sets. In dimension nine this gives only $\mathrm{iso}(9)\le47$, and the exact value $46$ requires an additional argument about eight-dimensional two-distance sets with at least $44$ points. We also show that $\mathrm{iso}(23)=\max\{g(23),278\}$, where $g(23)$ is the largest size of a two-distance set in $\mathbb{R}^{23}$, so that $278\le\mathrm{iso}(23)\le575$.

papers.title: The Borodin--Kostochka inequality from degree 750
papers.abstract: We prove that every finite simple graph $G$ with maximum degree at least $750$ satisfies $\chi(G)\le\max\{\omega(G),\Delta(G)-1\}$. The proof starts with a random partial colouring and completes it on large cliques using a list-colouring condition that remains valid as the rest of the graph is coloured. Disjoint stars provide the required colours. We estimate the number of stars that can be chosen after the clique colours have been exposed, while keeping their endpoint set fixed. A common exponential-moment argument reduces intervals of packing sizes to endpoint comparisons. More detailed neighbourhood estimates handle the remaining vertices. The final probability inequalities are verified by directed rational and interval arithmetic.

papers.title: Boundary phenomena for slow recurrences:finite and infinite critical sets
papers.abstract: For a second-order recurrence with positive integral coefficients, the slow length of an integer is the largest index at which it can occur when the initial terms range over positive integers. Spiro conjectured that, among a finite set of relatively prime recurrence pairs, a pair is slowest infinitely often precisely when its growth constant is strictly less than the square of the smallest growth constant. We study the equality case. For $T_m=\{(m-1,m),(m^2-1,m^2)\}$, the larger-growth pair attains the maximal slow length, with ties allowed, on $\Theta_m(\log x)$ integers up to $x$ whenever $m\ge3$, whereas for $m=2$ its complete set of slowest integers is $\{1,2,25\}$. We give certificates for the infinite examples and prove a bounded-seed theorem that limits the possible initial pairs at each critical index.

papers.title: Logarithmically Slim Polygons
papers.abstract:
We study the relationship between the large-scale geometry of a geodesic metric space and the slimness of its geodesic polygons. We show that if there is a uniform constant $\delta$ such that every geodesic polygon in an unbounded geodesic metric space is $\delta$-slim, then the space has asymptotic Assouad--Nagata dimension one.
  We further consider graphs of bounded valency and allow the slimness constant of an $n$-gon to grow logarithmically with $n$. More precisely, under an explicit logarithmic bound on the slimness of geodesic $n$-gons, we prove that the graph has asymptotic Assouad--Nagata dimension one. Thus, sufficiently strong logarithmic control on the slimness of geodesic polygons forces one-dimensional large-scale geometry.
  We also obtain two criteria for graphs, outside the hyperbolic setting, to have asymptotic Assouad--Nagata dimension one. In particular, these criteria show that one-dimensional large-scale geometry can be detected from quantitative restrictions on the slimness of geodesic polygons, without requiring the space to be hyperbolic.

papers.title: On the most informative Boolean function under noise
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a uniform random bit string and $Y$ be obtained by flipping each bit of $X$ independently with probability $p$. Let $C$ be a random bit obtained as a function of $Y$. We show that $\mathbf{I}(C:X)\le \mathbf{I}(Y_1:X)$ for all $p\in[0,1]$, which resolves a conjecture posed by Courtade and Kumar in 2013.

papers.title: Soft-confinement approximation of no-flux McKean-Vlasov dynamics
papers.authors: Geuntaek Seo, Yeoneung Kim, Beomjun Choi
papers.abstract: We study the approximation of the no-flux McKean-Vlasov equation on a bounded convex domain by a whole-space equation with quadratic confinement of strength $\lambda^{-1}$ outside the domain. For a smooth bounded interaction kernel and a common bounded initial density with square-integrable gradient, we establish an $O(\lambda^{1/4})$ approximation rate. The estimate controls the $L^2$ density error uniformly on every finite time interval and the gradient error in space-time $L^2$. Without interaction, a spectral gap independent of $\lambda$ yields the $O(\lambda^{1/4})$ rate uniformly in time for the density error and uniformly over all unit time intervals for the gradient error. With interaction, we construct a counterexample showing that even weak convergence can fail to be uniform in time.

papers.title: Extremal even-cycle-free subgraphs of the $k$-ary $n$-cube
papers.abstract: A graph is said to be $H$-free if it contains no subgraph isomorphic to $H$. The generalized Tur\'{a}n number $\mathrm{ex}(G, H)$, a natural extension of the classical Tur\'{a}n number, is defined as the maximum number of edges in an $H$-free spanning subgraph of $G$. For any integer $\ell\geq 2$, let $C_{2\ell}$ denote the even cycle of length $2\ell$. So far, extensive studies of the generalized Tur\'{a}n number for the hypercube $Q_{n}$ have been conducted. The $k$-ary $n$-cube is an important family of graphs with many favorable properties, such as regularity and vertex-transitivity. It generalizes the hypercube and reduces to the hypercube when $k=2$. In this paper, we investigate the generalized Tur\'{a}n number $\mathrm{ex}(Q^{k}_{n}, C_{2\ell})$ of $Q^{k}_{n}$ for all even integers $k\geq 4$ and integers $\ell\geq 2$, generalizing the result for $Q_{n}$ [J. Graph Theory 16 (1992) 273-286] from $k=2$ to $k\geq 4$.

papers.title: Construction, Enumeration and Duality of Perfectly Balanced Musical Sets of Order $2pq$
papers.authors: Paul Lascabettes, Sidney Ali, Alexandre Popoff, Moreno Andreatta
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present a comprehensive study of perfectly balanced musical sets, also known in the literature as vanishing sums of roots of unity, in the particular case of order $2pq$. Starting from the well-established result concerning the decomposition of such sets as an integer linear combination of regular polygons, we first provide an algebraic formalization that allows to explicitly construct all these sets. We then propose six different decompositions of each set into regular polygons. Moreover, by investigating their combinatorial enumeration, we derive a formula for the exact number of these sets for a given order $2pq$, and describe their distribution and cardinality for the particular case of order $6p$. One of the main results concerns the duality that can be established between these sets. In particular, we prove that every non-periodic minimal perfectly balanced set of order $2pq$ can be combined with another one to produce a self-complementary $2p$-periodic set, and the reciprocal also holds. Finally, we demonstrate that the modulus of the discrete Fourier transform coefficients of dual sets are related. All these results shed new light on the distribution of perfectly balanced sets of order $2pq$ and suggest new mathematical questions in a more general case.

papers.title: On Fujita's Advanced Generalized Mukai Conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove Fujita's advanced generalized Mukai conjecture for smooth complex Fano varieties. Our starting point is the existence of independent two-point Gromov--Witten correspondences. We show that there are finitely many unsplit families of rational curves whose chains connect $X$. We use these families to bound the anticanonical degrees throughout the successive minimal horizontal construction, so every family in that construction is unsplit. Fujita's contraction theorem and inductive classification then give the required list of varieties.

papers.title: Stabiliser codes over prime fields as weighted graphs and as quantum sets of lines
papers.authors: Simeon Ball, G\"ulizar G\"unay, Robin Simoens, Ricard Vilar
papers.abstract: We further develop the theory of quantum stabiliser codes and its links with graph theory and finite geometry. We prove that an [[n,k,d]]_p stabiliser code over a finite field with p elements, p prime, gives rise to a graph on n-k vertices together with two disjoint independent sets of size k. Its edges are weighted with elements of a finite field of size p. If k=0, such codes are known as graph states. Second, we view stabiliser codes as so-called quantum sets of lines in projective space, allowing us to determined their minimum distance geometrically. We describe two geometrical operations to obtain new quantum sets of lines from given quantum sets of lines. As an application, we list the number of stabiliser codes up to equivalence, for given small parameters.

papers.title: Representation theory and massive spectral zeta functions on spherical space forms
papers.authors: Victoria Martin, Allan Merino, Rahul Poddar, Simon Roby
papers.abstract:
We study the spectral theory of the massive scalar kinetic operator on spherical space forms $\Gamma \backslash S^{3}$, where $\Gamma$ is a finite subgroup of $\mathrm{SO}(4)$ acting freely on $S^{3}$. Using the Peter-Weyl theorem and Molien series we compute the spectrum of the Laplace-Beltrami operator on $\Gamma\backslash S^3$ directly from representation theory, obtaining the eigenvalues and their multiplicities for all lens spaces $L(p,q)$ and for each ADE-class of finite subgroups of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, which includes homogeneous lens spaces, prism spaces and quotients by the binary tetrahedral, octahedral and icosahedral groups, the last also known as the Poincar\'e homology sphere.
  For homogeneous quotients by subgroups of even order, we construct the meromorphic continuation of the spectral zeta function of the massive kinetic operator and obtain the general zeta-regularized determinant in closed form. The determinant is expressed as a finite sum of polylogarithms, valid for all real mass, and depends on $\Gamma$ only through its order and a finite set of parameters which we call twist coefficients fixed by the dimensions of the $\Gamma$-invariant subspaces.
  As a complementary approach, we express the heat trace of the kinetic operator on spherical space forms in terms of Jacobi theta functions, whose modular properties relate the spectral zeta function to geometric data, the volume and closed geodesic lengths of $\Gamma\backslash S^3$. We find that the spectral zeta function admits a rapidly convergent expansion in the heavy mass sector in terms of modified Bessel functions, and provides an independent check on the determinant.
  This framework extends to quotients of higher-dimensional manifolds directly, which we outline for future work.

papers.title: Low moments of sums of extended Rademacher random multiplicative functions
papers.authors: Christopher Atherfold, Maxim Gerspach, Jad Hamdan
papers.abstract:
Let $X^e \colon \mathbb{N} \to \{\pm 1\}$ be the random, completely multiplicative function whose values at the primes $(X^e(p))_{p \text{ prime}}$ are independent and uniformly distributed on $\{ \pm 1 \}$. Let $X=X^e\mu^2$. We determine the order of magnitude of
  \[
  \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \bigg| \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\sum_{n \le x} X^e(n) \bigg|^{2 q} \Bigg]\quad \text{ and }\quad \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \bigg|\sum_{n \le x} \frac{X(n)}{\sqrt{n}} \bigg|^{2 q} \Bigg]
  \]
  for $q\in [0,1]$, showing that a transition from better-than-square-root cancellation to growth like a power of $\log x$ occurs when $q$ crosses $1/2$. In particular, the first absolute moments are of order $(\log\log x)^{3/4}$.
  The proof proceeds by comparing these sums to integrals of random Euler products, which are then studied by analogy with Gaussian multiplicative chaos integrals. The main difficulty lies in proving the lower bound at $q=1/2$, for which we also adapt arguments from the study of random walks.

papers.title: Generalized Disjunctive Programming with Derivative-Free Configuration Search
papers.authors: Albert Joon Lee, Woosik Kim, David E. Bernal Neira
papers.abstract: Generalized disjunctive programming (GDP) describes process design alternatives with Boolean variables, disjunctions, and logical propositions, and fixing one configuration leaves a subproblem in the continuous variables. Conventional GDP methods require explicit equations, which a simulator may not expose, and mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) reformulations can be intractable for nonconvex models. The external-variable reformulation turns configuration choice into an optimization over an integer lattice whose objective is the subproblem value, which derivative-free optimization (DFO) can search while the GDP model continues describing the alternatives. We pair GDP models with surrogate DFO methods and the direct-search method NOMAD and compare them with discrete steepest descent (D-SDA), logic-based and MINLP solvers, and enumeration on nine process models, 21 test functions, a pharmaceutical flowsheet simulated in PharmaPy, and a catalytic distillation column with 100,947 configurations. On the largest reactor network, the surrogate methods MISO and RBFOpt reach the reference in nine or ten of ten runs with about 30 subproblem solves, whereas logic-based methods solve nearly one subproblem for each admissible configuration and most D-SDA descents end at one local minimum. In the flowsheet example, where GDP solvers do not apply, RBFOpt and MISO find the best of 36 simulated configurations in every run with 20 evaluations. For the catalytic column, D-SDA and MISO reach the best known design with 100 evaluations, whereas MINLP solvers find no design within 15% of it and global solvers return contradictory certificates. This search pays off when the configuration space is too large to enumerate, has deceptive local minima, or has MINLP reformulations that fail, and enumeration or a direct reformulation is simpler for small algebraic models.

papers.title: Filling Lipschitz spheres in metric spaces
papers.abstract: We prove a homotopical Euclidean isoperimetric inequality for Lipschitz maps from the unit n-sphere into metric spaces admitting a bounded bicombing, which includes CAT(0)-spaces and normed vector spaces. To do so, we first refine the second-named author's Euclidean isoperimetric inequality for singular Lipschitz chains to this setting. Then, we show that a singular Lipschitz chain filling induces a Lipschitz map filling of almost the same volume or less, by adapting a strategy seen in work of Gromov and others.

papers.title: Rough-to-frozen transition in non-integrable dimer models
papers.authors: Alessandro Giuliani, Vieri Mastropietro, Bruno Renzi, Fabio Toninelli
papers.abstract: The transition from rough to frozen phases in models of random surfaces is expected to be governed by the Pokrovsky-Talapov law, which predicts a $\varepsilon^{3/2}$-type singularity of the macroscopic height profile (limit shape), as the distance $\varepsilon$ from the frozen phase (facet) is sent to zero. This has been proved so far only in exactly solvable cases, notably the classical, determinantal, 2D dimer model. In this paper we prove the validity of the Pokrovsky-Talapov law for a non-integrable 2D dimer model on the hexagonal lattice, whose Gibbs weight depends upon a weak plaquette interaction among dimers. Our proof is based on a multiscale analysis (constructive fermionic Renormalization Group), which allows us to identify two different regimes with distinct scaling properties and to explain the universality of the Pokrovsky-Talapov exponent $3/2$, in contrast with the interaction-dependent critical exponents characterizing the rough phase. The first regime, corresponding to smaller distances, is characterized by an effective quadratic dispersion relation, while the second comes with an effective linear dispersion relation, typical of Luttinger liquid behavior. As a byproduct of our construction, we control the scaling limit of the interacting dimer model uniformly in the distance from the frozen phase.

papers.title: On Parallel Sums of Set-Valued Operators: Monotonicity, Paramonotonicity, and Decomposition Invariance
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate structural properties of the parallel sum of set-valued operators in a real Hilbert space, with particular emphasis on monotonicity, maximal monotonicity, and paramonotonicity. We examine the decomposition-invariance property of the parallel sum of two paramonotone operators and provide a direct proof based on monotonicity and the equality of admissible decompositions. This approach establishes the required orthogonality relations without invoking the Attouch--Th{\'e}ra Duality duality framework. We also revisit the classical maximal-monotonicity property of the parallel sum and present an alternative graph-based derivation involving an auxiliary shifted operator. Furthermore, we study the parallel sum of a set-valued operator and the normal cone operator associated with a closed linear subspace. Explicit characterizations of its values, domain, and range are presented, and a decomposition-independent representation is obtained under paramonotonicity through the orthogonality of the underlying subspaces. These results provide a unified and self-contained treatment of selected properties of parallel sums and clarify the role of paramonotonicity in their structural behavior.

papers.title: On symmetry and monotonicity of singular solutions to critical fractional Hartree equations
papers.authors: Guangze Gu, Aleks Jevnikar, Zhipeng Yang
papers.abstract: This paper continues the study initiated in \cite{GuJevnikarYang2026b} of fractional Hartree equations with zero capacity singular sets. We are concerned here with the critical case, i.e. \[ (-\Delta)^s u=\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^N\setminus\Gamma} \frac{u^{2_{\mu,s}^*}(y)}{|x-y|^\mu}\,d y\right)u^{2_{\mu,s}^*-1} \quad\text{in }\mathbb{R}^N\setminus\Gamma, \] where $N\ge2$, $s\in(0,1)$, $\mu\in(0,N)$ and $2_{\mu,s}^*$ is the critical exponent associated to this class of problems. We prove symmetry and monotonicity with respect to the singular set $\Gamma$. The Kelvin transforms centered at regular points provide sufficient decay at infinity for both the transformed solutions and their associated Hartree coefficients, without imposing global integrability assumptions. Combined with a moving plane argument and a comparison estimate in critical Lebesgue spaces, this allows the moving plane method to cover the full interaction range.

papers.title: Tight Lower Bounds under Matched High-Order H\"older Smoothness and Uniform Convexity
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we provide tight lower bounds for minimizing high-order H"older-smooth and uniformly convex functions when their orders match. Specifically, we consider functions whose $p^{th}$-order derivatives are H"older continuous with degree $
u$ and parameter $H$, and that are uniformly convex with degree $q$ and parameter $\sigma$. When these orders match, namely, $q = p + 
u$, we show that any deterministic algorithm with access to derivatives up to order $p$ requires $\Omega\left(\left( rac{H}{\sigma}ight)^{ rac{2}{3(p+
u)-2}}\log rac{\Delta_0}{\epsilon}ight)$ oracle calls to reduce an initial optimality gap of $\Delta_0$ to $\epsilon$. This matches the corresponding upper bound and establishes a higher-order uniformly convex counterpart to Nesterov's classical first-order lower bound for strongly convex functions. Rather than directly generalizing Nesterov's classical quadratic-chain construction, we develop a multiscale phase-wise construction that preserves previous oracle responses while maintaining global H"older smoothness and uniform convexity. Our result resolves the matched case left open by existing lower bounds for the two asymmetric regimes.

papers.title: Hamilton cycles in bicirculants with non-coprime connection sets
papers.abstract:
A bicirculant is a regular graph that admits an automorphism having two vertex-orbits of the same size. A bicirculant can be described as follows. Given an integer $m \ge 1$ and sets $R, S, T \subseteq \mathbb{Z}_m$ such that $R=-R$, $T=-T$, $0 \not\in R \cup T$ and $0 \in S$, the graph $B(m;R,S,T)$ has vertex set $V=\{u_0,\dots,u_{m-1},v_0,\dots,v_{m-1}\}$ and edge set $E=\{u_iu_{i+j}| \ i \in \mathbb{Z}_m, j \in R\} \cup \{v_iv_{i+j}| \ i \in \mathbb{Z}_m, j \in T\} \cup \{u_iv_{i+j}| \ i \in \mathbb{Z}_m, j \in S\}.$ Some of the well known bicirculants include the generalized Petersen graphs and Cayley graphs of dihedral groups.
  In 1983, Brian Alspach proved that the only non-hamiltonian generalized Petersen graphs are $G(m,2)$ where $m \equiv 5 \pmod 6$. In a recent paper we conjectured that this is the only exception among regular connected bicirculants of degree at least two, and we have verified the conjecture for bicirculants with $|S|\le 3$. Results of Alspach, Chen and Dean imply that the conjecture also holds for all bicirculants with $m$ even and $\gcd(m,S)=1$. In this paper, we show that the conjecture holds for all bicirculants with $|S| \geq 4$ and $\gcd(m,S)>1$ such that $R\cup T$ contains an element that is not coprime to $\gcd(m,S)$ and, if $m$ is odd, is also not divisibile by $\gcd(m, S)$ or $R \cap T$ contains an element that is coprime to $\gcd(m,S)$.

papers.title: Shotgun Assembly of the Non-Uniform Labeled Lattice Model
papers.authors: Julia Gaudio, Charlie K. Guan, Andrew Jin
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the graph shotgun assembly problem in the labeled lattice model, as introduced by Mossel and Ross (2019). We start with a $d$-dimensional lattice of length $n$, where the color of each vertex is sampled i.i.d. from a distribution $\pi$. Then, we ask whether it is possible to reconstruct the coloring of the lattice given the coloring of each subgrid of length $k$. While previous work by Ding and Liu (2023) and Demidovich, Panichkin, and Zhukovskii (2023) identified the reconstruction threshold when $\pi$ is uniform, we examine the non-uniform case. This paper establishes a sufficient condition for the impossibility of reconstruction for $d \geq 2$ using information-theoretic arguments. Our negative result matches the known threshold in the uniform case.

papers.title: One-third H\"older stability of optimal transport maps from log-concave sources
papers.abstract:
We prove quantitative stability of quadratic optimal transport maps from arbitrary log-concave sources to bounded targets. If the source $ho$ is isotropic on $\mathbb R^d$ and the targets $\mu$, $
u$ are supported in a common ball of radius $R$, their Brenier maps satisfy \[
  \lVert T_\mu-T_
uVert_{L^2(ho)}
  \leqslant 17d^{2/3}R^{2/3}W_2(\mu,
u)^{1/3}. \] The one-third exponent is optimal for $d\geqslant2$. The proof combines a linear stability estimate for Brenier potentials in a weighted norm with a matching weighted reverse Poincar'e inequality. The weight is chosen in terms of the negative log-density of the source to account for its tails. We also show that the best dimensional constant in map stability is at least of order $d^{1/3}$.

papers.title: On the existence of nonadmissible irreducible smooth representations of $p$-adic $\mathrm{GL}_n$
papers.abstract: Let $p>7$ be a prime, let $n>1$, and let $F$ be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic $p$ not equal to $\mathbb{Q}_p$. For every extension $E$ of the residue field of $F$, we construct an irreducible smooth $E$-representation of $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$ which is not admissible. When $E$ is countable, we also construct such representations without a central character and with nonscalar endomorphisms.

papers.title: Stroh--Hamiltonian Framework for Modeling Incompressible Poroelastic Materials
papers.abstract: The Stroh sextic formalism, developed by Stroh, offers a compelling framework for representing the equilibrium equations in anisotropic elasticity. This approach has proven particularly effective for studying multilayered structures and time-harmonic problems, owing to its ability to seamlessly integrate physical constraints into the analysis. By recognizing that the Stroh formalism aligns with the canonical Hamiltonian structure, this work extends its application to Biot's poroelasticity, focusing on scenarios where the solid material is incompressible and there is no fluid pressure gradient. The study introduces a novel Hamiltonian-based approach to analyze such systems, offering deeper insights into the interplay between solid incompressibility and fluid-solid coupling. A key novelty lies in the derivation of canonical equations under these constraints, enabling clearer interpretations of reversible poroelastic behavior. However, the framework assumes perfectly drained conditions and neglects dissipative effects, which limits its applicability to fully realistic scenarios involving energy loss or complex fluid dynamics. Despite this limitation, the work provides a foundational step toward understanding constrained poroelastic systems and paves the way for future extensions to more general cases, including dissipative and nonlinear regimes.

papers.title: Non-redundant Independence Atoms
papers.abstract: Independence atom is a key concept in relational database theory. In the present paper, we prove that the maximum possible size of a non-redundant set of independence atoms on $n$ attributes is asymptotically $(1+o(1))\binom{n}{\floor{n/2}}$. It turns out that this problem is closely related to two extremal set theory problems, the Katona-Tarj\'an question on ``V''-free families of subsets of $[n]$ for the lower bound, and Kleitman's bound on union-free families for the upper bound.

papers.title: A First Closed-Form Robin Parameter for Optimized Schwarz Waveform Relaxation as a Function of Iteration Count, Overlap, and Time Window Length
papers.authors: Alejandro Alfonso Rodriguez, Martin J. Gander, Felix Kwok
papers.abstract:
Schwarz waveform relaxation (SWR) is a parallel-in-time iterative method for the solution of evolution problems and belongs to the class of Parallel-in-Time algorithms that have received increasing attention over the past three decades. For parabolic problems, SWR converges linearly over long time intervals and exhibits superlinear convergence on short time intervals. Since the introduction of optimized variants (OSWR) nearly three decades ago, determining the optimized Robin parameter when OSWR is applied on bounded time windows has remained an open problem.
  We introduce here a new analytical approach that, for the first time, yields a closed-form expression for the optimal Robin parameter in the transmission conditions for the one-dimensional heat equation with two overlapping subdomains. The resulting formula explicitly characterizes the dependence of the optimal parameter on the iteration number, the overlap size, and the length of the time window. Beyond resolving this long-standing optimization problem, our analysis provides a framework that can be extended to more general settings, including higher-dimensional problems, multiple subdomains, and higher-order transmission conditions.

papers.title: The Zelevinsky involution, co-standard modules for quantum affine algebras and interval symmetric functions
papers.abstract:
Let $\mathscr{F}_n$ be the subcategory of finite-dimensional representations of the quantum loop algebra of $\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1}$ whose simple modules are indexed by multisegments consisting of intervals $[a,b]$, where $a,b$ are integers and $0<b-a\le n$. We define the co-standard module associated to a multisegment $\mathbf{s}$ to be the tensor product of the Kirillov--Reshetikhin modules, associated to the first node of the Dynkin diagram of $\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1}$, given by the segments of $\mathbf{s}$. Under a suitable (and necessary) restriction on $n$, we show that its socle is isomorphic to the simple module given by the Zelevinsky dual $\mathbf{s}^\dagger$ of $\mathbf{s}$. We then define an involution $\Phi$ of the Grothendieck ring $\mathcal{K}(\mathscr {F}_n)$ and prove that it maps the class of a simple module to the class of the simple module given by its Zelevinsky dual. We also show that on suitable subcategories $\Phi$ is induced by an exact autoequivalence reversing tensor products, and we give a $t$-analogue of the multiplicity identity in the quantum Grothendieck ring.
  Motivated by the determinantal formula for alternating snake modules, we realize $\mathcal{K}(\mathscr {F}_n)$ explicitly inside a polynomial ring in variables indexed by intervals, and, in the spirit of Macdonald's ninth variation of Schur functions, we show that the fundamental modules correspond to analogues of the elementary symmetric functions and the Kirillov--Reshetikhin modules to analogues of the complete homogeneous symmetric functions. This is compatible with $\Phi$ and the classical involution $\omega$, and we prove that alternating snake modules give a family of Schur positive symmetric functions extending the skew Schur functions.

papers.title: When light travels with infinite speed: the electromagnetic loop circuits
papers.abstract: Considering the ideal limit where the speed of light is infinite, or more precisely where the permittivity and permeability of the vaccuum are both zero, we construct a new type of electromagnetic circuit that we name an EM-loop circuit. These consist of wires having very high permittivity (E-wires) and wires having very high permeability (M-wires). These are threaded together by coils, the E-wire loops and M-wire loops. Some of the loops are terminal loops, pierced by an applied magnetic flux (for E-wire loops) or an applied displacement field (for M-wire loops) that are outside the vacuum since it does not support these fields. The response is the net flux of displacement field through a cross section of each E-wire terminal loop and the net magnetic flux through a cross section of each terminal M-wire loop. To calculate this response, the fields at the internal loops (those that are not terminal loops) are eliminated from the equations.It turns out that the response is governed by a new class of function pairs - dual Herglotz functions. Superpositions of a special class of EM-loop circuits, termed fundamental, allow us to realize any pair of dual Herglotz functions. Thus, we have obtained a complete characterization of the response functions of EM-loop circuits.

papers.title: IC-rigidity and generalizations of a theorem of Mahler
papers.abstract: Mahler showed that for every irrational $\alpha$ and every base ${b\geq 2}$, there is a single positive integer $n$ such that every digit in $\{0, \dots, b-1\}$ occurs infinitely often in the base-$b$ expansion of $n\alpha$. Furstenberg later observed that dynamical methods can be used to give a different proof. Building on this perspective, we give generalizations of Mahler's theorem in two directions: the multipliers are a syndetic subset of certain multiplicative semigroups, and analogous versions hold in higher dimensions. Our main tool is IC-rigidity, a type of rigidity which is a hybrid of topological and measurable constraints.

papers.title: Conjugator length of Bestvina-Brady groups
papers.abstract: We classify the conjugator length functions of Bestvina-Brady groups. We show that the conjugator length function, when non-trivial, grows as a linear or quadratic polynomial. In fact, we give explicit criteria on the defining graph to determine the precise degree of the polynomial. The proof generalises ideas of Bridson, Riley, and Sale by exploiting the framework developed by Chang and the authors to classify the Dehn functions of Bestvina-Brady groups.

papers.title: Pointfree convergence approach and pointfree index theory
papers.abstract: Given a category $\mathsf{C}$ of lattices, we introduce the category $\mathsf{C^{Cap}}$, a pointfree version of the category $\Cap$ of convergence approach spaces, that contains $\Cap$ coreflectively, as well as the category $\mathsf{C^{Conv}}$, of pointfree convergence spaces introduced by Goubault-Larrecq and Mynard, both reflectively and coreflectively. We investigate pointfree counterparts of pseudo-approach, pre-approach, and approach spaces along two natural axes---depth and adherence-determinedness---which coincide in the spatial case but diverge in general lattices, and we determine when the point--powerset adjunction restricts to these subcategories. Unlike in $\mathsf{C^{Conv}}$, the category $\mathsf{Ap}$ of approach spaces finds a natural analog $\mathsf{C^{Ap}}$ in $\mathsf{C^{Cap}}$ and "index theory" translating traditional topological or metric results into generalizing inequalities can be conducted. We illustrate this with a result involving measure of continuity and measure of compactness.

papers.title: Almost All 3-uniform Hypergraphs are Class 1
papers.authors: Arnab Chaterjee, Asaf Ferber, Marcelo Sales, Mason Shurman
papers.abstract: The chromatic index $\chi'(H)$ of a hypergraph $H$ is the smallest number of colors needed to color its edges so that no two adjacent edges share the same color. The chromatic index is trivially bounded below by the maximum degree $\Delta(H)$, and when $\chi'(H)= \Delta(H)$, we say that $H$ is Class 1. It is well known that almost every 2-graph is Class 1, and we extend this result to 3-graphs. We show for $n^{-2/3-1/200}\leq p \leq 0.99$ that the $3$-uniform binomial random hypergraph $H\sim H_{n,p}^{(3)}$ is Class 1 with high probability. We also show that this result doesn't hold for uniformities above $3$. For a broad range of $p$, when $k \geq 4$ and $k \nmid n$, the hypergraph $H \sim H_{n,p}^{(k)}$ is with high probability not Class 1.

papers.title: Partitions with designated summands: $k$-tuples and their congruences
papers.abstract: Let $A_k(n)$ and $B_k(n)$ be the numbers of ordered $k$-tuples of partitions with designated summands, respectively with designated summands and all parts odd, of total size $n$. Using an exact description of the generating function of designated partitions after a $3$-dissection, we classify for every $e$ the values of $k$ for which $A_k(3n+2)$ is divisible by $3^e$: this happens exactly when $k\equiv0$ or $-5\pmod{3^e}$ if $e\le4$, and when $3^e\mid k$ if $e\ge5$. We obtain the corresponding exact $3$-adic and several $2$-adic results for $B_k$ and for $A_k$ along the progressions $4n+3$, a recursion for the classes $3^b(3n+s)$, and for $k=2$ the congruences $A_2(12n+10)\equiv 27f_1^4f_6^3/f_2\pmod{81}$ in generating-function form. We relate the numbers $A_k(n)$ modulo $3$ and $9$ to overpartitions, sums of squares and triangular numbers, give group-action proofs of some of the congruences, and close with several conjectures supported by computation.

papers.title: Exact signal recovery from generative priors with sigmoid output activation
papers.authors: Matthew S. Scott, Yaniv Plan, \"Ozg\"ur Y{\i}lmaz
papers.abstract: We show exact signal recovery in generative compressed sensing for feedforward neural networks with piecewise-linear activations and a final sigmoid activation, with no assumption of expansivity. Consider a ReLU network of depth $d$ with a sigmoid final activation, whose input layer, of dimension $k$, is the narrowest, and let $K$ be the geometric mean of the widths of its layers. We show that, with high probability, all signals of the range whose entries lie in $[\delta, 1 - \delta]$ are uniformly recovered from $m \gtrsim k(d \log(K/k) + \log(1+\log(1/\delta)))$ measurements.

papers.title: Calder\'{o}n's complex interpolations of variable-exponent Fofana spaces
papers.authors: Nouffou Diarra, Pokou Nagacy, Sekou Coulibaly
papers.abstract: Fofana spaces, introduced in the framework of Wiener amalgam spaces, can be viewed as generalizations of Morrey spaces. These spaces have attracted considerable attention in recent years and have found applications in the study of partial differential equations. In this paper, we investigate their variable-exponent counterparts. More specifically, we describe Calder\'{o}n's, first and second, complex interpolations of Fofana spaces with variable exponent, as well as the corresponding interpolation spaces of their preduals. Our results recover, as special cases, those already known for (classical) Fofana and Morrey spaces.

papers.title: Lusztig sheaves, local systems, and the extended Springer resolution
papers.authors: William Graham, Martha Precup, Amber Russell
papers.abstract: The Springer resolution of the nilpotent cone is used to give a geometric construction of the Springer correspondence by applying tools in the derived category of perverse sheaves, particularly the decomposition theorem. In this paper we continue earlier work of the authors on the extended Springer resolution, a map introduced by the first author that factors through the Springer resolution. Our first main result shows that applying the decomposition theorem to this map yields a sum of Lusztig sheaves in all Lie types, each corresponding to a triple of so-called minimal cuspidal datum. We also study the simple perverse sheaves that occur as summands of the resulting sheaf. Our second main result proves that every simple perverse sheaf corresponding to orbits that are Levi-regular must occur, generalizing earlier work in the type A setting to all Lie types.

papers.title: On Diameter Graphs Problems: A proof of Brass's Conjecture
papers.abstract:
The diameter graph of a finite set $S\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ has vertex set $S$ and two points are adjacent when their distance equals $\operatorname{diam} S$. In this paper we study the following question: given $k$ and $d$, is there a constant $c=c(k,d)$ such that from every finite point set $S\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ one can remove at most $c$ points so that the subgraph of the diameter graph induced by the remaining points is $k$-colorable? Brass conjectured that such a constant exists for $d=3$ and $k=3$. We prove this conjecture by showing that at most one point needs to be removed.
  We also answer a question of Dol'nikov, showing that for every positive integer $m$, there exist a finite point set $S\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ in which every subset of smaller diameter has less than $(|S|-m)/2$ points.

papers.title: Linear-length cycles in the supercritical percolated hypercube
papers.abstract: Let $Q_p^d$ be the random subgraph of the $d$-dimensional binary hypercube obtained by retaining each edge independently with probability $p$. A long-standing folklore conjecture states that the emergence of the giant component in $Q_p^d$, at $p\approx 1/d$, is accompanied by the emergence of cycles of linear length. We confirm this conjecture and determine the order of the longest cycle near the phase transition. Specifically, for every sufficiently small constant $\varepsilon>0$, we show that if $p=(1+\varepsilon)/d$, then with high probability the longest cycle of $Q_p^d$ has length $\Theta(\varepsilon^2 2^d)$. The dependence on $\varepsilon$ is optimal up to constant factors.

papers.title: A liquid vapor phase transition in quantum statistical mechanics
papers.authors: Francesco Baffioni, Tobias Kuna, Immacolata Merola, Errico Presutti
papers.abstract: We prove a liquid vapor phase transition for a quantum system of particles in the continuum. The system is the quantum version with Boltzmann statistics of the point particles model introduced in by Lebowitz, Mazel and Presutti.

papers.title: Comparative analysis of numerical methods for X-ray 3D reconstruction from sparse views
papers.authors: Melitine N. Bardi, Konstantinos K. Delibasis
papers.abstract: Reconstruction of three-dimensional vascular structures from a limited number of X-ray projections is a severely underdetermined and ill-conditioned inverse problem. This work presents a unified matrix-free computational framework for evaluating iterative numerical methods for sparse-view cone-beam tomography. Forward and backprojection are implemented from ray-voxel intersection lengths computed with the Amanatides-Woo traversal algorithm, avoiding explicit construction of the large sparse system matrix. We systematically compare ART, SART, SIRT, gradient descent (GD), and Krylov subspace methods, including Conjugate Gradient, LSQR, and GMRES. The common matrix-free operators and geometry are used for all methods, allowing consistent comparisons under matched conditions. Particular emphasis is placed on gradient scaling using scalar step sizes, Jacobi preconditioning, and diagonal Hessian majorization, together with L1, Tikhonov, and total variation regularization. Numerical experiments use five three-dimensional coronary vessel models reconstructed from ten simulated X-ray projections under noise and scattering conditions, and are extended to real X-ray projections of a static thin-vessel phantom. Performance is evaluated in terms of convergence, computational cost, volumetric overlap, contrast-to-noise ratio, vessel diameter and centerline errors, and projection consistency at an unseen viewing angle. The results show that total-variation-regularized gradient descent with diagonal majorization provides the best overall reconstruction performance within the investigated computational budgets. By contrast, the tested Krylov implementations achieve limited geometric recovery despite higher computational cost. These findings emphasize the importance of appropriate gradient scaling and regularization for stable and computationally efficient sparse-view tomographic reconstruction.

papers.title: Linear Cotype Bounds for Nonlinear Spectral Gaps of Scalar Expanders
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite simple $d$-regular graph, $d\geq 3$, whose second largest adjacency eigenvalue satisfies $\lambda_2(G)\leq (1-\delta)d$, where $0<\delta\leq 1$. We prove that the Poincar\'e constant satisfies $$\gamma(G,\|\cdot\|_X)\lesssim \frac{qCK}{\delta}$$ whenever $X$ is a real Banach space with a $K$-unconditional Schauder basis and cotype $q$ with constant $C$. This constant compares the mean distance over all vertex pairs with the mean distance across edges. For real Banach lattices the bound is $O(qC/\delta)$. The proof estimates where a random walk first leaves each coordinate level set. As a consequence of the bound, if $n$-vertex graphs in a fixed-degree expander family embed with bounded distortion into spaces with bounded $C,K$, then $q$ must grow at least as fast as $\log n$. This order is attained in $\ell_q^n$.

papers.title: Infinitary real-valued logic and a refinement of the Kochen-Specker theorem
papers.abstract: For nearly sixty years, refinements of the Bell-Kochen-Specker theorem have concentrated on finite configurations, combinatorics and robustness; once a configuration is fixed, contextuality is witnessed by the inconsistency of a finite family of Boolean constraints. We study the theorem instead with infinitary real-valued logic and a model existence game. We axiomatize, in real-valued $L_{\omega_1\omega}$, the lattice of closed subspaces of a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space together with a quantum probability measure. In the standard models the theory recovers Gleason's theorem. Once the axiom that the measure is $\{0,1\}$-valued is adjoined, the theory has no models, standard or nonstandard, although every finite set of its axioms has one; a model existence game converts this infinitary inconsistency into finite inconsistent sets of interval commitments on the values of sentences. Over the standard models, the subsets of $[0,1]$ that formulas define through the values of the measure are exactly the $\sigma$-projective sets, the members of the least class containing the Borel sets and closed under complements, countable unions and projections along $\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$; the classification is proved in ZFC. For a specified strategy in the game, the plays that complete the parity argument for the eighteen-ray configuration of Cabello, Estebaranz and Garc\'ia-Alcaine record the geometric identities between the occurrences of a ray in different contexts, and the use that the measure makes of them. Probabilities are tracked up to rational tolerances, and $\sigma$-additivity along a named basis selects the four-dimensional block in which the argument takes place. The refinement is thus not a smaller Kochen-Specker set but a finer analysis of the logical form of the obstruction.

papers.title: A motivic Vojta inequality for non-CM elliptic curves with unbounded height
papers.abstract: We study a bounded-degree form of a motivic Vojta inequality for pure Andr\'e motives, arising from a question of Kato. We verify this inequality for infinitely many non-CM elliptic curves with unbounded stable Faltings height. The point is that ramification at the finite poles of the $j$-invariant gives the required discriminant bound.

papers.title: Orthogonal polynomials on two or more intervals: the Sprugnoli context
papers.abstract: We show how the group of Sprugnoli arrays on three elements can be used to define families of polynomials that are orthogonal on two intervals, and we indicate how the group can be extended in the hierarchy of Sprugnoli groups to yield families of orthogonal polynomials with more complex supports. In particular, we examine the defining three term recurrences and the Jacobi matrices of these families of orthogonal polynomials, while detailing the Sprugnoli matrix structure of the coefficient matrices of the polynomial families. We also consider integral representations of the principal moments on the defining intervals. Sprugnoli arrays are shown to relate to periodic recurrences where the parameters remain cyclically constant.

papers.title: The Galois actions on braided fusion categories
papers.abstract: This note harmonizes two classical topics: minimal modular extensions of braided fusion categories and the Galois action on modular fusion categories. Their common generalizations are Galois-modular extensions, which always exist when a braided fusion category $\mathcal{B}$ is pseudounitary. Each extension induces a Galois action on the simple objects of $\mathcal{B}$. Up to integral equivalence, the Galois-modular extensions of $\mathcal{B}$ form a torsor over an explicit group of homomorphisms from $\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})$ to the invertible objects of order dividing two in the symmetric center $\mathcal{E}$ of $\mathcal{B}$. If $\mathcal{E}$ is Tannakian and $\mathcal{B}$ has a minimal modular extension, all minimal modular extensions induce one canonical Galois action. We prove that many facts about the modular data of modular fusion categories extend to pseudounitary premodular fusion categories as well via the Galois action.

papers.title: Orbit Transversality for Projective Space
papers.abstract: Let $f\colon \mathbb{P}^n\to \mathbb{P}^n$ be a dominant endomorphism defined over a number field $K$. We show that there is a finite extension $L/K$ such that every proper closed subset of $\mathbb{P}^n$ misses at least one grand $(f,L)$-orbit. Equivalently, $(\mathbb{P}^n,f,K)$ is strongly dense orbit transversal (S-DOT): every set containing exactly one representative of each grand $(f,L)$-orbit is Zariski dense in $\mathbb{P}^n$.

papers.title: Dynamical Signatures of Selective Gap Closing in Multi-Dimensional Monotone Quasiperiodic Operators
papers.abstract: We translate the spectral gap-closing criterion for multi-dimensional monotone quasiperiodic Schr\"odinger operators into a concrete dynamical protocol and verify it by large-scale numerics. For a non-principal label we construct a sampling function whose leading eigenfunction weight at the origin vanishes; a local bump then drives the residual weight through zero. The height of a weighted oscillatory time average of the origin-to-localization-center correlator exhibits a deep minimum precisely at the closing, while the site-control label remains featureless and orders of magnitude larger. The signature is robust and maps directly onto superconducting-circuit and photonic platforms.

papers.title: Diophantine definability from addition and divisibility over rings of $S$-integers
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a number field, let $S$ be a finite set of places of $K$ containing the archimedean places, and let $\mathcal{O}_{K,S}$ denote the ring of $S$-integers of $K$. We prove that multiplication is positive-existentially definable in $(\mathcal{O}_{K,S},0,1,+,\mid)$ if and only if the unit group $\mathcal{O}_{K,S}^\times$ is infinite. This extends a 1977 theorem of Lipshitz for rings of integers to rings of $S$-integers. One of the key ingredients is a uniform bound for unit equations due to Evertse, Schlickewei and Schmidt, which we use to recover multiplication on the unit group.

papers.title: Quartic polynomial differential systems with three disjoint invariant circles
papers.abstract: We determine the normal forms of real planar polynomial differential systems of degree at most four with three prescribed pairwise disjoint invariant circles, covering all configurations of their centers. None of the prescribed circles is a limit cycle in the concentric case or in the coaxial case with three distinct centers, where the pairwise radical axes coincide. When exactly two centers coincide, or when the three centers are distinct and collinear and the circles are non-coaxial, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for all three circles to be algebraic limit cycles, which are necessarily hyperbolic. For non-collinear centers, we give explicit necessary and sufficient conditions for all three circles to be periodic orbits and for all three to be hyperbolic algebraic limit cycles. Each of the four configurations with non-collinear centers is realized by a coprime quartic polynomial differential system with three hyperbolic circular limit cycles.

papers.title: Discrete Poincar\'e and Bogovskii operators for higher order finite element de Rham complexes
papers.authors: Johnny Guzm\'an, Pratyush Potu, K. Olav Tyssvang
papers.abstract: We present discrete Poincar\'e and Bogovskii operators for the common finite element discretizations of the de Rham complex of arbitrary polynomial order. We first discuss how such operators arise from a decomposition of the finite element spaces into a lowest order component and a remainder. This results in a fast algorithm for computing grad, curl, and div potentials. We then introduce a nonlocal Poincar\'e operator on contractible domains, which generalizes existing constructions based on cone operators to arbitrary order by integrating over cones against extended test forms. This requires developing commuting extension operators, which turn out to be related to rational forms. We also show how the nonlocal construction is modified to obtain a discrete Bogovskii operator preserving homogeneous boundary conditions. We further discuss how the ideas of the construction fit into the theory of finite element systems.

papers.title: Equivariant elliptic cohomology via loop spaces
papers.abstract:
We construct a cohomology theory $H_A(-)$ canonically attached to any 1-dimensional commutative group scheme A over a connective $E_\infty$-ring. The additive group in characteristic zero gives 2-periodic de Rham cohomology, the multiplicative group gives topological periodic cyclic homology, and an elliptic curve gives elliptic cohomology. The construction extends to the G-equivariant setting for an algebraic group G, yielding in the elliptic case a theory of equivariant elliptic cohomology on algebraic varieties with G-action that takes values in sheaves on the stack of G-bundles. Over the complex numbers, and for G connected reductive, this lifts Grojnowski's theory from the moduli space of G-bundles to the stack.
  The key player is the category of perfect complexes on A with 0-dimensional support, equipped with the convolution product induced by the group law of A. It plays the role of a categorified circle and is used to define a loop space $L_A^G(X)$, whose structure sheaf gives rise to $H_A^G(X)$ after periodization. Sheaves on $L_A^G(X)$ equivariant under loop rotation provide a category of coefficients for $H_A^G(-)$ in the same way that D-modules provide coefficients for de Rham cohomology. At the point X = *, the theory also gives rise to an $E_\infty$-ring spectrum (or sheaf thereof) $K_A$, which recovers complex K-theory for $A = \mathbf{G}_m$, and the sheaf $\mathcal{O}^{top}$ of topological modular forms for the universal elliptic curve.

papers.title: Mixed-Integer Second-Order Cone Formulations for the Euclidean Bottleneck Steiner Tree Problem in $\mathbb{R}^d$
papers.authors: Gabriel P. Braun, Marcia Fampa, Nelson Maculan, Renan V. Pinto
papers.abstract: Given a set of terminals in $\mathbb{R}^d$ and an integer $k\ge0$, the Euclidean bottleneck Steiner tree problem (EBSTP) asks for a tree spanning the terminals with at most $k$ Steiner points that minimizes its longest edge. Although the planar case has been widely studied, exact optimization methods for arbitrary dimension remain scarce. We develop two exact mixed-integer second-order cone programming (MISOCP) formulations for the EBSTP: a single-commodity flow formulation and a formulation with connectivity cuts. Both formulations share a geometric core based on edge-conditional second-order cone constraints and are strengthened by problem-specific preprocessing, edge-dependent big-$M$ constants, symmetry-breaking constraints, constructive upper bounds, and new global lower bounds on the optimal value. We establish the correctness of the formulations and prove the validity of all strengthening techniques. Computational experiments on 1050 benchmark instances in dimensions $d\in\{2,3,4\}$, with up to $50$ terminals and $9$ Steiner points, show that the single-commodity flow formulation consistently outperforms the formulation with connectivity cuts, with an advantage { in solved instances} that grows with dimension. The proposed global lower bounds substantially strengthen the root relaxation, while the single-commodity flow formulation provides the most robust exact solution method across all test sets. These results establish the single-commodity flow formulation as an effective exact approach for the EBSTP in arbitrary fixed dimension.

papers.title: Translate, then decide: asymptotic optimality of latent-space control in bistable systems
papers.abstract: This paper asks whether an optimal decision can be separated from the physical dynamics on which it acts. It studies this question through minimum-energy barrier crossing in scalar bistable systems. It characterizes the finite-horizon optimal feedback and shows that, as the horizon grows, it converges to a law that doubles and reverses the drift while it opposes crossing, and switches off once the barrier is passed. In physical coordinates, this law inherits the plant's nonlinearity, entangling decision and dynamics. We show that a plant-specific translation of state, input, and time maps every double well in the considered class to the same unit-rate linear world model, allowing a downstream decision stage to use a single plant-independent control primitive. This separation generally loses optimality at finite horizons because the translation does not preserve the physical control energy. Nevertheless, we prove that the excess physical energy of the layered controller vanishes as the horizon grows and that its limiting feedback reproduces the asymptotic optimum exactly. Thus, translation and optimization generally do not commute at a finite horizon, but commute in the asymptotic limit.

papers.title: Conditions for Normality of Pontryagin's Maximum Principle in the Absence of State Constraints
papers.authors: Andr\'e Tits, Pierre-Antoine Absil, No\'e Tits
papers.abstract: Pontryagin's Maximum Principle is said to be "normal" for the problem at hand when it has a solution (maximizer u*) that explicitly involves the problem's cost function, making the maximum principle helpful (while in the opposite situation it is of no help). The aim of the present paper is, for Lagrange optimal control problems without state constraints, to identify classes of problems for which the Principle is normal. General conditions are introduced that guarantee normality, and classes of problems that satisfy these conditions are identified. Such classes include problems for which the constrained (by bounds on the control values) "augmented" reachable set, with cost along an upward vertical axis, has a convex lower-boundary function and the optimal terminal state lies in the relative interior of the reachable state set, with the terminal constraint within the affine hull of that set. Such classes include problems for which the constrained (by bounds on the values of the control signal) "augmented" (with the cost value along an upward "vertical axis") reachable set has a "convex" lower boundary for which the optimal terminal state lies in the relative interior of the set of reachable states. Special attention is given to Lagrange steering problems: sufficient conditions are obtained on a nested sequence of sub-classes of such problems, culminating with the class of steering problems with scalar control signal and linear time-invariant (LTI) state dynamics and objective integrand, for which normality is guaranteed whenever all eigenvalues of the state dynamics matrix A are real (e.g., if A is symmetric or triangular or the system is overdamped) or have small enough imaginary parts; simple 2 x 2 examples show that, in contrast with the situation in the finite-dimensional case, this property does not extend to arbitrary A matrices.

papers.title: A toric approach to social choice theory
papers.authors: Ata Poyraz Turna, Ben Y. Wormleighton
papers.abstract: This paper initiates a systematic study of objects in convex geometry and toric algebraic geometry arising from status quo systems in social choice theory. Our main application is to classify all cones arising from a large class of status quo systems that are smooth or simplicial.

papers.title: Assouad--Nagata dimension of systolic complexes with almost flat intervals
papers.authors: Mart\'in Blufstein, Victor Chepoi, Huaitao Gui, Damian Osajda
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of systolic complexes with almost flat intervals. They constitute a subclass of fit systolic complexes and arise naturally in the study of graphical C(3)--T(6) small cancellation complexes. We prove that their Assouad--Nagata dimension is bounded above by a universal constant. As consequences, we obtain universal bounds on the Assouad--Nagata dimension of tame simply connected graphical C(3)--T(6) small cancellation complexes and of finitely generated groups defined by graphical C(3)--T(6) small cancellation presentations. In the appendix, we observe that the proof of finiteness of asymptotic dimension for buildings due to Dymara and Schick also yields finiteness of their asymptotic Assouad--Nagata dimension.

papers.title: Second moment of incomplete Eisenstein series revisited
papers.abstract: We revisit Yu's second moment formula for incomplete Eisenstein series and give uniform bounds for secondary terms appearing in this formula. We use these bounds to improve results on distribution of integer points on the light cone corresponding to an indefinite quadratic form, as well as intrinsic Diophantine approximation on ellipsoids, and counting holonomy vectors of saddle connections of Veech surfaces.

papers.title: Continuity and Stability of the FitzHugh Nagumo System with Respect to the Diffusion
papers.abstract: Spatial heterogeneity in diffusion is a fundamental feature of excitable media, yet its effect on FitzHugh Nagumo dynamics remains mathematically challenging. We establish stability of solutions with respect to perturbations of the diffusion coefficient, providing a rigorous account of how changes in the medium affect the evolution of the system. Specifically, we prove a continuous dependence result ensuring that small perturbations in diffusion produce small variations in the corresponding solutions. The proof adapts the method of contracting rectangles to variable diffusion, yielding a framework for controlling and comparing solutions associated with different diffusion profiles. This result provides a rigorous link between heterogeneous and homogeneous FitzHugh Nagumo systems and justifies constant-diffusion approximations when the diffusion coefficient is close to a constant. Our analysis advances the understanding of FitzHugh Nagumo dynamics in heterogeneous media by establishing robustness with respect to spatial variations in diffusion.

papers.title: Hotplug Coded Caching: Embedding the YMA and Interference Elimination Schemes via Reed--Muller Codes
papers.abstract: In the hotplug coded caching model, $K$ users fill their caches of size $M$ as a function of $N$ files, but only an unknown subset of $A<K$ users is active in the delivery phase. We recently showed that (i) under uncoded placement, offline users cause a strict load penalty at intermediate memory sizes, so that coded placement is needed; and (ii) for $AM\leq N$, every classical scheme with row-wise placement, including the scheme of Gomez-Vilardebo (GV), can be embedded in a Reed-Solomon code, which removes the penalty. In this note, we show that every point of the scheme of Yu, Maddah-Ali and Avestimehr (YMA) for a classical system with $A$ users is achievable in the hotplug model for every $K\geq A$. Each user is associated with a hyperplane and each file with a homogeneous polynomial; each user caches the restriction of the polynomial to its hyperplane, and the subfiles seen by the active users are the values of the polynomial at the points where their hyperplanes meet. This is a projective Reed-Muller code, which reduces to the Reed-Solomon code when each subfile is cached by one user. We then show, by an existence argument, that every classical scheme whose cache is a linear compression of the Maddah-Ali-Niesen cache and whose correctness holds for generic coefficients can also be embedded over a sufficiently large field; this includes the interference elimination (IE) schemes of Tian and Chen. These embeddings complement the Reed-Solomon one, which allows any row-wise placement and any delivery. Together with past work, our results show that every point attained by a GV, YMA or IE scheme ($N\leq A$ for IE), and every corner point of the linear tradeoff for $A=N=3$, is achievable in the hotplug model with a load that does not depend on $K$. Whether the optimal hotplug tradeoff depends only on $A$ remains open, but these results support a positive answer.

papers.title: Collision Parameters in Higher-Dimensional Families of Polynomials
papers.abstract: Let $d\geq 3$ and consider the generic family of monic normalized polynomials $f_{\mathbf{t}}(z)=z^d+t_1z^{d-2}+t_2z^{d-3}+\cdots+t_{d-2}z+t_{d-1}$, where $\mathbf{t}=(t_1,\ldots,t_{d-1})$. Given pairwise distinct starting points $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_d\in\bar{\mathbb{Q}}$ and a target point $\beta\in\bar{\mathbb{Q}}$, we show that the set of parameters $\boldsymbol{\lambda}\in\mathbb{A}^{d-1}(\bar{\mathbb{Q}})$ for which $\beta$ belongs to the forward orbit of every $\alpha_i$ under $f_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}$ is not Zariski dense in $\mathbb{A}^{d-1}$.

papers.title: A topological Mundici representation theorem
papers.authors: Yifan Meng, Lili Shen, Dexue Zhang
papers.abstract: We lift Mundici's equivalence between MV-algebras and abelian $\ell$-groups with a strong unit to the topological setting. To this end, we prove that, for every topological MV-algebra, the associated Mundici group can be endowed with a topology that extends the topology of the MV-algebra and makes it into an abelian topological $\ell$-group. Among such topologies there is a finest one; we identify this topology as the topological-group reflection of the bounded-stage final topology, and construct an explicit zero-neighbourhood base in terms of the original MV-algebra topology. Using this topology, we establish a topological Mundici adjunction that restricts to an equivalence between topological MV-algebras and Mundici-fine abelian topological $\ell$-groups with a strong unit. Here, Mundici-fine means that the group topology is the finest $\ell$-group extension of its unit-interval topology. We also identify extremal $\ell$-group extensions under additional hypotheses, and establish a quasitopological correspondence clarifying the distinction between separate and joint continuity.

papers.title: Betti Sequences of Four-Generated Non-Almost-Symmetric Nearly Gorenstein Numerical Semigroup Rings
papers.abstract: Let $S$ be a minimally four-generated numerical semigroup that is nearly Gorenstein but not almost symmetric, and let $R=k[S]$ over an arbitrary field $k$. We prove that the defining ideal of $R$ has four or five minimal generators when $R$ has Cohen--Macaulay type two, and exactly six when it has type three. Thus the total Betti sequence over the four-variable polynomial presentation ring is one of $$(1,4,5,2),\quad (1,5,6,2),\quad (1,6,8,3),$$ and all three possibilities occur. The type-three argument uses a canonical-ideal exact sequence, a chain-level comparison on $\operatorname{Tor}$, and a codimension-three Gorenstein reduction. The resulting classification gives an affirmative answer, over every field, to Moscariello and Strazzanti's Question 4.3 on four-generated nearly Gorenstein numerical semigroups that are not almost symmetric.

papers.title: Near linear mixing of random-cluster Glauber dynamics on random regular graphs
papers.abstract:
We study the random-cluster model on locally treelike graphs at low temperatures. This is a model of dependent percolation parametrized by an edge probability $p \in (0,1)$ and a clustering weight $q \in [1,\infty)$, generalizing independent Bernoulli percolation ($q=1$) and closely related to the classical ferromagnetic Ising and Potts spin systems at integer $q$. For $q>2$, at parameter $p$ below the tree uniqueness threshold $p_{\mathsf u}(q,d)$, it is expected that sampling is easy and local Markov chains mix rapidly on all graphs with degree bounded by $d$. On typical graphs, the same is predicted at $p>p_{\mathsf s}(q,d)$, where $p_{\mathsf s}(q,d)$ is a second uniqueness transition point on the $d$-regular wired tree. Our result confirms this prediction for random regular graphs, showing that the random-cluster Glauber dynamics mix in time $O(n^{1+o(1)})$ on a random $d$-regular graph for all fixed $q>2$ and $p>p_{\mathsf s}$.
  For comparison, the best prior sampling results for these models that held for all $p>p_{\mathsf s}$ required $q\gtrsim \log d$ \cite{BGPZ26}. The key difficulty is that simply utilizing the contraction of cavity messages on $d$-regular trees does not suffice to cover the entire regime $q>2$. To address this issue, motivated by \cite{LS26}, we develop a careful bootstrap argument to show the shrinkage of disagreement under grand coupling. The core ideas of the proof were generated using GPT-6 and the Pharos system; the proof was then refined and simplified by the author.

papers.title: Non-Pseudo-Arithmetic Hyperbolic 4-Manifolds
papers.abstract:
We give three explicit finite-volume hyperbolic Coxeter lattices in dimension four whose adjoint trace fields are not totally real. They are the reflection groups of the Ma--Zheng polytopes $P_{11,6}$, $P_{11,7}$, $P_{11,8}$. The obstruction is contained in two cyclic products of the doubled unit-normal Gram matrix $A=2G$. Those products recover elements $s=\sqrt5$ and $u$ satisfying $$ (s-1)u^2+2(s-3)u+s-7=0. $$
  After the embedding $s\mapsto-\sqrt5$, this quadratic has discriminant $8(1-\sqrt5)<0$. The cyclic-product field therefore has a complex place. Vinberg's identification of that field with the adjoint trace field and the Emery--Mila total-reality obstruction imply that the three lattices are not pseudo-arithmetic. Torsion-free orientation-preserving finite-index subgroups yield orientable noncompact finite-volume hyperbolic $4$-manifolds with the same obstruction.
  Exact computations check the census data and provide independent field and finite-volume certificates. A pinned Lean~4 development verifies the radical identity and the number-field obstruction. It also checks the lattice and manifold implications conditional on explicit geometric and literature hypotheses.

papers.title: Existence of a Normalized Mountain Pass Solution for a Coupled Cubic Schr\"odinger System with Partial Confinement
papers.authors: Wan-Yue Tang, Hong-Rui Sun, Jianlun Liu
papers.abstract: This paper studies a mass supercritical Schr\"odinger system with partial confinement: $$ \begin{cases} -\Delta u_1+|y|^2u_1 =\lambda_1u_1+\mu_1u_1^3+2\beta u_1u_2^2,\qquad x\in\R^3,\\ -\Delta u_2+|y|^2u_2 =\lambda_2u_2+\mu_2u_2^3+2\beta u_1^2u_2,\qquad x\in\R^3, \end{cases} $$ subject to the mass constraints $ \int_{\R^3}u_1^2\dd x=a_1$, $\int_{\R^3}u_2^2\dd x=a_2,$ where $x=(y,z)\in\R^2\times\R$, the parameters $\mu_1,\mu_2,\beta$ are positive, and $\lambda_1,\lambda_2\in\R$ are unknown Lagrange multipliers. The masses satisfy $(a_1,a_2)=\eps(\rho_1,\rho_2)$ for a fixed vector $\rho=(\rho_1,\rho_2)\in (0,\infty)^2$. For all sufficiently small $\eps>0$, we establish the existence of a positive normalized solution $u_\eps^-$ at a mountain pass level on the full product mass sphere. This level coincides with the infimum of the energy over the negative part of the Pohozaev set. The main difficulty arises from the lack of compactness due to partial confinement. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a compactness argument that preserves the two independent mass constraints and show that every minimizing sequence for this infimum admits a strongly convergent subsequence after suitable common translations along the unconfined axial direction. We further establish the asymptotic relation $\eps E(u_\eps^-)\to m_0(\rho)$ as $\varepsilon\to0$, where $m_0(\rho)>0$ denotes the infimum of the free energy under the corresponding Pohozaev constraint. In addition, we derive the asymptotic behavior of the kinetic and potential energies. The solution obtained here is distinct from the normalized ground states constructed by Jia et al. [Discrete Contin. Dyn. Syst., 40(2020), 2739-2766] through local minimization for sufficiently small masses.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Complexity of Finding Approximate Local Minima of Nonconvex Finite Sums
papers.abstract: We study the component-oracle complexity of finding approximate local minima of nonconvex finite sums under mean-squared averaged smoothness with parameter $L$ and a $\rho$-Lipschitz average Hessian. Each query returns the value, gradient, and one Hessian-vector product of a component. We show that the complexity in the high-accuracy regime $\varepsilon\le c_0L^2/(n\rho)$ is $\tilde\Theta(n^{3/4}L^{1/2}\rho^{1/4}\Delta\varepsilon^{-7/4})$ for a sufficiently large initial gap $\Delta$. We attain the upper bound by adapting the inverse solver and eigenvector routine of FastCubic to averaged smoothness. Our lower bound assigns the bridge edges of a nested chain to random components; a replicated spectral construction gives the same bound for unrestricted randomized algorithms. Under individual smoothness, a factor of $n^{1/4}$ remains for $\varepsilon\le cL^2/(n^2\rho)$, up to logarithmic factors. In the complementary low-accuracy regime, we propose PathVR, which uses $\tilde O(n+\sqrt{n}L\Delta\varepsilon^{-2})$ queries and matches a lower bound from dense weak hiding.

papers.title: On rational curves relative to a divisor
papers.abstract:
Let $X$ be a smooth complex projective variety and $D$ a reduced simple normal crossings divisor. We prove that, given a complete curve of negative $(K_X+D)$-degree, through its general points there is a rational curve whose normalization meets $D$ in at most one point. The proof uses ordinary weighted jets of a smooth family constructed from $(X,D)$, a positive parameter line bundle, and an intersection calculation on a ruled surface. We obtain an explicit degree bound depending on a projective embedding.
  We apply this construction to a cyclic cover compactification associated with a smooth Campana orbifold $(X,\sum_i(1-1/m_i)D_i)$. If its anticanonical divisor is big, we show that there is a covering family of free divisible Campana rational curves with fixed numerical class and contact data. In Picard number one case, the orbifold is Campana rationally connected.

papers.title: Analysis of a Two Membrane Thermoelastic Problem
papers.authors: Nathaniel J. Fink-Humes, Carlos N. Rautenberg
papers.abstract: We formulate and study a mathematical model of a thermoforming process involving two interdependent thermoelastic membranes coupled with equations governing heat transfer. These membranes interact with each other through means of elastic forces and thermal transfer which determines changes in elastic properties and further deform the membranes. The two thermoelastic membranes lead to a pair of implicit obstacle problems which are modeled both as a 2-membrane problem or a pair of quasi-variational inequalities. Mathematically, the primary model couples an elliptic two membrane problem with associated nonlinear elliptic equations describing temperature distribution. We show, under physically relevant conditions, the existence of solutions via a fixed point approach that involves reformulation of the problem to improve regularity of solutions.

papers.title: Observability and stabilizability for Grushin-Type parabolic equations in the whole space
papers.authors: Shanlin Huang, Gengsheng Wang, Jiaqi Yu
papers.abstract:
We study observability and stabilization for the whole-space Grushin heat equation $$ \partial_t u-\Delta_\gamma u=0,\qquad \Delta_\gamma:=\Delta_x+|x|^{2\gamma}\Delta_y,\qquad (t,x,y)\in(0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m,\quad \gamma>0. $$ For product sets $E=E_1\times E_2$, we identify three observability regimes in which thickness, distance from the degeneracy set $\{x=0\}$, and local density near that set play different roles.
  (i) In the subcritical regime $0<\gamma<1$, the observability inequality holds for every $T>0$ if and only if both $E_1$ and $E_2$ are thick; hence $T_{\min}(E)=0$.
  (ii) At the critical exponent $\gamma=1$, if $E_2=\mathbb{R}^m$ and $E_1\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is thick, we determine the exact minimal observable time: $$ T_{\min}(E)=\frac{a_{\mathrm{ess}}(E_1)^2}{2n},\qquad a_{\mathrm{ess}}(E_1):=\operatorname*{ess\,inf}_{x\in E_1}|x|. $$ Thus, the threshold depends on the essential distance of $E_1$ from the degeneracy set.
  (iii) In the supercritical regime $\gamma>1$, we consider $n=1$, $E_2=\mathbb{R}^m$ and thick sets $E_1\subset\mathbb{R}$. If $a_{\mathrm{ess}}(E_1)>0$, observability fails for every $T>0$, so that $T_{\min}(E)=+\infty$. If $a_{\mathrm{ess}}(E_1)=0$, observability depends on the density of $E_1$ near $0$, measured by $$ D_{E_1}(r):=\log\!\left(\frac{2r}{|E_1\cap(-r,r)|}\right),\qquad L_{E_1}:=\limsup_{r\downarrow0}r^2D_{E_1}(r). $$ If $L_{E_1}=0$, then $T_{\min}(E)=0$; if $0<L_{E_1}<\infty$, a finite sufficient observation time exists. Moreover, observability at time $T$ requires $$ \limsup_{r\downarrow0}r^{2(1+\gamma)/(\gamma-1)}D_{E_1}(r)\le C_{T,\gamma}. $$
