  In contrast, for every $\gamma>0$, exponential and complete stabilizability hold if and only if both $E_1$ and $E_2$ are thick. The stabilization criterion is therefore independent of $\gamma$.

papers.title: A geometric proof of multivariate self-normalized moderate deviations via ridge regularization
papers.authors: Bing-Yi Jing, Yiming Liu, Shaochen Wang, Wang Zhou
papers.abstract:
Let $X,X_1,X_2,\ldots$ be i.i.d.\ random vectors in $\mathbb R^d$, where $d\ge1$ is fixed. Assume that $\mathbb{E} X=0$, $\mathbb{E} XX^\top=I_d$ and $\mathbb{E}\|X\|^3<\infty$. We prove a Cram\'er type moderate deviation theorem for a multivariate self-normalized radius statistic, that is, for every $a_n=o(n^{1/6})$, \[
  \sup_{0\le x\le a_n}
  \left|\frac{\mathbb{P}(U_{n,+}\ge x)}{\mathbb{P}(\chi_d\ge x)}-1\right|\to0, \] where $\chi_d$ is the Euclidean norm of a standard normal vector in $\mathbb{R}^d$ and \[
  U_{n,+}^2=S_n^\top A_n^+S_n,
  \qquad S_n=\sum_{j=1}^nX_j,
  \qquad A_n=\sum_{j=1}^nX_jX_j^\top. \] Here $A_n^+$ denotes the Moore--Penrose inverse. We further prove that the same result holds for the corresponding Hotelling $T^2$ statistic. This work closes the moment gap between the previously known finite $(3+\delta)$ moment condition for Hotelling moderate deviations and the finite third moment boundary. Our proof adopts a geometric approach. Truncation at the finite-third-moment scale yields a truncated covariance matrix whose concentration error is negligible relative to the target \(\chi_d\) tail. Uniform projected self-normalized moderate deviations are then averaged over directions and, after a whitening map with a ridge term, become a spherical cap transform of the radial distribution. A local Abel inversion recovers the radial tail, and deterministic comparison removes the ridge and the truncation.

papers.title: Twisted Diophantine approximation: asymptotic and uniform results
papers.abstract: Fix an $m\times n$ matrix $A$; twisted Diophantine approximation studies how well we can approximate the affine form $A {\bf q}-{\bf b}$ by an integer $m$-vector, depending on the choice of $m$-vector ${\bf b}$. We report on two companion papers in twisted Diophantine approximation, covering two setups: asymptotic and uniform. The asymptotic paper gives an exact Khintchine-type Lebesgue zero--one law, a null--conull criterion for badly approximable shifts, and Hausdorff-measure tests yielding exact power-law dimensions under a critical divergence condition. The uniform paper computes Hausdorff dimensions of sets of uniformly approximable vectors. It also gives Hausdorff zero--full laws, uniform-exponent spectra, and a sharp escape-of-mass bound. In both cases the results are established for arbitrary approximation functions from suitable regularity classes, and the arguments use a homogeneous lattice count involving all successive minima to record clustering in every independent direction.

papers.title: Variational exponential estimates and stationary large deviations for SPDEs
papers.authors: Rui Bai, Chunrong Feng, Huaizhong Zhao
papers.abstract:
We establish an abstract criterion for large deviations of invariant measures when the deterministic dynamics has a single globally attracting equilibrium. Deterministic regularisation and attraction yield an endpoint estimate for long controlled paths of bounded action, uniformly over each fixed bounded initial set. This allows the finite time Freidlin-Wentzell uniform LDP on bounded initial sets to be combined directly with stationary exponential norm estimates. The proof requires neither a separate exponential tightness argument nor a Dembo-Zeitouni uniform LDP, and imposes no decay condition on differences between controlled trajectories. Finite path approximation identifies the quasipotential as the good rate function. We also establish a variational criterion based on the Bou\'e-Dupuis representation that derives exponential estimates from bounds for controlled outputs, without requiring their convergence. Uniform controlled terminal moments yield estimates uniform in time, which pass to Krylov-Bogoliubov invariant measures.
  Together, these results establish stationary LDPs in four regimes: two-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations with possibly unbounded, globally Lipschitz, uniformly positive scalar amplitudes and vanishing noise correlation; reaction-diffusion systems without the additional restriction linking noise growth to reaction strength; Allen-Cahn equations with opposite boundary values and globally Lipschitz, uniformly nondegenerate multiplicative space-time white noise on intervals of arbitrary length; and Burgers equations with fixed covariance $(-\Delta)^\alpha$, $0\leq\alpha<1/2$. For Burgers, we also obtain Gaussian norm estimates.

papers.title: Functional inequalities from the fundamental limits of Bayesian estimation
papers.abstract:
We develop a Bayesian information-theoretic framework for proving functional inequalities for log-concave measures. Motivated by Klartag and Ordentlich, we establish a unified equivalence between $\Phi$-Sobolev inequalities and Bayesian estimation lower bounds: for a large class of smooth convex $\Phi$, a log-concave measure $\mu$ satisfies a $\Phi$-Sobolev inequality with constant $C>0$ if and only if for $X\sim\mu$, any $t>0$, and any real-valued measurable $f$, the Bayes risk of estimating $f(X)$ under the $\Phi$-Bregman loss from the Gaussian additive observation $Y_t=\sqrt tX+G, G\sim N(0,I_n)$ is at least a $1/(1+Ct)$-fraction of that of the trivial estimator.
  Combining it with direct information-theoretic arguments, such as testing-to-estimation reductions, we obtain old and new functional inequalities:
  - For the Poincar\'e inequality, corresponding to $\Phi(x)=(x-1)^2$, we give a simple static information-theoretic proof that the Poincar\'e constant of an isotropic log-concave measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$ is $O(n^{1/2})$, first proven via stochastic localization in the seminal work of Lee and Vempala.
  - For the log-Sobolev inequality, corresponding to $\Phi(x)=x\log x$, we prove that all smooth $K$-subgaussian log-concave measures $\mu$ satisfy $C_{\mathrm{LS}}(\mu)\lesssim K^2n^{1/4}$, surpassing the recent state-of-the-art bound of $O(K^2n^{1/2})$ by Bizeul. In parallel and independent work, OpenAI claimed the optimal bound $O(K^2)$ in their October 6, 2026 release of 722 papers.
  - Finally, we give a Bayesian reformulation of the common structure of the three recent proofs of the Kannan--Lov\'asz--Simonovits conjecture, a dimension-free Poincar\'e bound for isotropic log-concave measures [BK26; BKL26; SZ26]. Tools from the study of the "low-degree MMSE" in computational complexity of statistical inference motivate and recast key steps and quantities of these proofs.

papers.title: Learning Coarse Spaces for Two-Grid Methods from Smoothed Errors with Applications to High-Contrast Porous Media Flow
papers.authors: Chenglong Bao, Chen Cui, Ruohua Li
papers.abstract: Efficient two-grid solvers for high-contrast parametric elliptic problems require coarse spaces that capture error components poorly reduced by local smoothing. As these components vary with the problem parameters, repeatedly constructing parameter-adaptive coarse spaces can be computationally expensive. We propose a coarse-space learning method based on finite-step errors generated by additive Schwarz smoothing. For each training parameter, proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) of smoothed-error snapshots in the discrete energy inner product defines a reference coarse space. A continuous-coordinate neural generator is then trained using a basis-invariant, whitened subspace loss, enabling the prediction of parameter-adaptive coarse spaces on unseen grids. We establish discrete perturbation estimates relating coarse-space discrepancies to the associated nonsymmetric two-grid operators and derive conditional finite-step Krylov residual-polynomial bounds without assuming stationary energy contraction. Numerical experiments on high-contrast interface problems, moving-interface Darcy flow, and nonlinear Forchheimer flow demonstrate effective solver performance across varying parameters and grid resolutions. On the finest static test grid, with approximately 264 times as many degrees of freedom as the training grid, the learned spaces achieve FGMRES iteration counts close to those of parameter-specific POD references and comparable to GenEO spaces, while substantially reducing repeated coarse-space construction costs.

papers.title: Effect of a fourth-order diffusion term on the robustness of the transfer function stability for hyperbolic systems
papers.abstract: We study a $2\times2$ hyperbolic system with anti-located control and observation. It is well known that the system can be stabilized with a delayed output-feedback control and that, unfortunately, this design is arbitrarily sensitive to small errors in the transport velocity. It was recently proved that adding a second-order diffusion term to the system restores robustness. We show that the same phenomenon occurs with a fourth-order diffusion term: the maximal spectral abscissa of the closed-loop system converges, as the diffusion parameter goes to zero, to the explicit value $-\ln(2)$, and the resulting stability margin is robust to small perturbations of the transport velocity. This additional term leads to a quartic characteristic equation whose roots have no tractable closed-form expression. We develop an asymptotic classification of its four roots and use it to obtain a first-order expansion of the transfer function with an explicit error bound. Combining this expansion with a topological degree argument, we show that $-\ln(2)$ is in fact the exact limiting value of the spectral abscissa, extending to the fourth-order case the sharpness result previously available only for second-order diffusive terms.

papers.title: Cyclotomic factorization and fixed-point insertion in colored permutation groups
papers.abstract: We extend cyclotomic Euler--Mahonian factorization to colored permutation groups for two inversion statistics: Biagioli--Zeng length and the inversion number of the underlying unsigned permutation. At a primitive $m$th root and rank $n=mk+i$, each normalized enumerator is a Hadamard product of a rank-$i$ colored enumerator and a weighted rank-$k$ type-B enumerator. Separate color variables are retained. The type-B factors agree for the two statistics, yielding equidistribution modulo the rank jointly with descent number, major index and negative-entry number. We also determine their exact changes under positive fixed-point insertion and obtain rational kernels retaining descent and major index. These kernels mark arbitrary fixed-point numbers and give derangement expansions at every inversion weight. Signed specializations recover type-A and type-B identities and give colored flag-major refinements. Inverse statistics and color-sum subgroups admit related insertion formulas.

papers.title: Gaussian free field limit for the Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble
papers.abstract: We prove that the centered height function of the Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble converges for each $\beta>0$, under rescaling of space and time variables, towards the Gaussian free field in the half-plane. The conformal structure for GFF involves the spatial change of coordinate $x\mapsto \sqrt{-x}$. The $\beta$--dependence is isolated in the field rescaling by $\sqrt{\beta}$. For the proofs we study the asymptotic expansions of the moments of Laplace transforms of the Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble developed in our previous work with Xu.

papers.title: A Rankin-Selberg Integral for $SU_{2,2}$
papers.abstract: We construct a Rankin-Selberg integral for the non-split quasi-split unitary group $SU_{2,2}$ and prove that it is Eulerian. We then compute the local integral at inert places where all data are unramified, and show that it represents the local adjoint $L$-function of $SU_{2,2}$.

papers.title: Root vector localization and minimal nilpotent finite $W$-algebras
papers.abstract:
Let \(\mathfrak{g}\) be any finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebra, let $h^\vee$ be its dual Coxeter number, and let \(e\) be its highest-root vector which is a minimal nilpotent element. In this paper, using a result of Bavula on invariants of commuting locally nilpotent derivations, we show that \[
  U(\mathfrak{g})_f
  \cong \mathcal{D}^+_{h^\vee-2}\otimes \mathcal{D}_1\otimes U(\mathfrak{g},e), \]
  where the first factor is a polynomial Weyl algebra of rank $h^\vee-2$, the second factor is a Laurent Weyl algebra of rank one, and $U(\mathfrak{g},e)$ is the finite $W$-algebra associated with $\mathfrak{g}$ and $e$. As an application, we prove that if $M$ is a simple infinite-dimensional $\mathfrak{g}$-module with the minimal GK dimension on which $f-1$ acts locally nilpotently, then $M\cong P\otimes V$ for some simple $\mathcal{D}^+_{h^\vee-2}\otimes \mathcal{D}_1$-module $P$ and some finite-dimensional simple $U(\mathfrak{g},e)$-module $V$. We also give a new proof of the Skryabine quivalence and Petukhov's birational decomposition of the quotient division ring of $U(\mathfrak{g})$.

papers.title: A Complete Characterization of $q$-Ary $2$-Designs in Doubly-Extended Reed-Solomon Codes
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}_k$ be the doubly-extended Reed--Solomon code with parameters $[q+1, k, q-k+2]_q$. We give a complete characterization of when its codewords of a fixed weight form $q$-ary 2-designs. The main ingredient is an exact criterion showing that the number of $r$-subsets of $\mathbb{F}_q^*$ with a prescribed product is independent of that product if and only if $\gcd(r, q-1)=1$. Applying this criterion to the minimum-weight codewords of $\mathcal{C}_k$, we prove that they form a $q$-ary 2-design if and only if $\gcd(k-1, q-1)=1$. We further establish a propagation result for MDS codes showing that the $q$-ary 2-design property at minimum weight implies the same property at every nonzero weight. Consequently, $\mathcal{C}_k$ holds $q$-ary 2-designs at all nonzero weights if and only if $\gcd(k-1, q-1)=1$.

papers.title: Sharp Hausdorff--Young inequalities for some locally compact quantum groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that the usual Hausdorff--Young inequalities for locally compact quantum groups such as the quantum \(E_q(2)\), the real quantum \(az+b\), and the extended quantum \(SU_q(1,1)\), where \(0<q<1\), are sharp. Moreover, there are no group-like projections with finite Haar weight in these locally compact quantum groups. We obtain a sharp Hausdorff--Young inequality for Kahng's skew-matrix quantum groups; the optimal constant is strictly less than one for \(1<p<2\); at \(p=2\), Plancherel gives equality, and these quantum groups have no nonzero group-like projections with finite Haar weight.

papers.title: The Invocation Bottleneck in LLM-Based Lossless Compression: What Can Be Removed and What Must Be Traded
papers.authors: Zhe Yan, Yihao Liu, Antonio Boffa, Huanchen Zhang
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) compress text far better than classical compressors, but LLM-based compressors are slow, particularly during decompression. We argue that their decoding time has two fundamentally different sources. Execution redundancy, such as per-token host transfers, CPU-side coding, and token-by-token encoding, is work that the coded output does not require and can be removed without changing a single output bit. Sequential dependency, one model call per decoded token, is inherent to lossless decoding and cannot be removed by better execution, only traded for more calls or for more bits. We remove execution redundancy with a GPU-resident pipeline whose block-parallel encoding is made lossless in half precision by batch-invariant kernels, speeding up arithmetic coding by up to 5.8x in encoding and 3.0x in decoding without changing its compression rate. We then study the two ways of trading sequential dependency, speculative dual-model coding (SDMC) and multi-token single-model coding (MSMC), characterize the compression cost of predicting several tokens from a shared prefix, and identify the workloads in which fewer model calls are worth that cost.

papers.title: BMV conjecture and positivity of spectral shift for relatively Schatten perturbations
papers.abstract: We establish BMV-type results and prove the positivity-preserving property and uniqueness of support-normalized spectral shift functions of arbitrary order for semibounded operators with relatively Schatten-von Neumann perturbations. We also derive correlation inequalities in the relative Hilbert-Schmidt case. These results build on a new positivity-preserving property for the trace of a higher-order operator derivative along a relatively Schatten direction and are obtained using methods of multilinear operator integration and approximation.

papers.title: Weak and strong convergence of a general splitting approach for monotone multioperator inclusions
papers.authors: Minh N. Dao, Matthew K. Tam, Thang D. Truong
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a general forward-backward splitting approach for monotone inclusion problems that simultaneously accommodate set-valued, monotone Lipschitz continuous, and cocoercive operators. Weak convergence is established under a general setting. Strong convergence is obtained when both the maximally monotone operators are linear relations and the monotone Lipschitz continuous and cocoercive operators are linear. When the set-valued operators are normal cones to closed linear subspaces, we derive an explicit characterization of limit points of generated sequences using a new technique. Numerical experiments on a quadratic minimization problem with multiple-set split feasibility constraints are presented to illustrate the theoretical results.

papers.title: Maximal Unipotent Monodromy and $p$-adic Eigenvalue Formulas
papers.authors: Alan Adolphson, Steven Sperber, Hao Zhang
papers.abstract: We establish p-adic formulas for the eigenvalues of Frobenius in the case of the family of hyperkloosterman sums. The deformation equation in this case has maximal unipotent monodromy, and the interplay of Frobenius and the differential equation plays an important role in establishing p-adic analytic formulas for the eigenvalues.

papers.title: Stable equivalence of quadratic monomial algebras
papers.abstract: It is well known that gentle algebras are closed under derived equivalence. However, it is easy to verify that they are not closed under stable equivalence. We prove that the classes of quadratic monomial, almost gentle and string almost gentle algebras are closed under stable equivalence. In fact, in each of these cases, stable equivalence is characterized by isomorphism after deleting all nodes and removing semisimple direct summands. The underlying isomorphism theorem gives a positive answer to Mart\'inez-Villa's question on selfinjective-free algebras for these classes. We also prove that the nonprojective simple modules form the unique weakly simple-minded system of a quadratic monomial algebra. Consequently, every stable equivalence of Morita type involving such an algebra lifts to a Morita equivalence when neither algebra has semisimple direct summands. Finally, we describe the effect of node deletion on stable categories of Gorenstein-projective modules and singularity categories, and give combinatorial descriptions of the equivalences for almost gentle algebras using marked configurations.

papers.title: A sharp Bernstein theorem for affine maximal type surfaces
papers.authors: Yalin Sun, Cheng Xing, Ruiwei Xu
papers.abstract: We investigate Bernstein theorem for the affine maximal type equation \begin{equation*} \sum_{i,j=1}^nf^{ij}(D^a)_{ij}=0,\qquad D=\det(f_{ij}),\qquad a\neq0, \end{equation*} under completeness of the Calabi metric. In dimension two, we prove that every smooth strictly convex solution on a convex domain is a quadratic polynomial whenever $a\notin[-\tfrac23,-\tfrac13]$, resolving a conjecture of Sun and Xu [25]. For every $n\geq2$, we also construct explicit non-quadratic Calabi complete solutions on convex domains for all $a\in[-\tfrac n{n+1},-\tfrac1{n+1}]$. These examples show that the rigidity range is sharp in dimension two.

papers.title: An Asymptotic for E. P. Stein Numbers
papers.abstract:
Epstein's put-or-take-a-square game is an impartial combinatorial game in which a player may, in each turn, add or subtract the largest square not exceeding the current integer. We study E. P. Stein numbers, the positions from which both legal moves lead directly to positive squares, and prove the following asymptotic formula for the counting function $S_2(X)$ of these positions: \[
  S_2(X)=\frac{1}{\pi^2}X^{1/4}\log X+O(X^{1/4}). \]

papers.title: Large orbits of $p$-groups on conjugacy classes
papers.abstract: Let $P$ be a $p$-group that acts faithfully and coprimely on a finite group $H$. A classical result of D.\ S.\ Passman, in the form proved by I.\ M.\ Isaacs, asserts that there exists an element $x\in H$ such that $|C_P(x)|\le (|P|/p)^{1/p}$. In this paper, we study the corresponding question for the action of $P$ on the conjugacy classes of $H$. We show that for every odd prime $p$ the analogue of Isaacs' bound fails for classes. On the other hand, we prove that if $H$ is solvable, then there always exists a conjugacy class $c$ of $H$ whose stabilizer in $P$ has order at most $|P|^{1/2}$, and that this bound is best possible for every prime $p$. As a consequence, there always exists an irreducible character of $H$ whose inertia group in $P$ has order at most $|P|^{1/2}$. The proof proceeds via a result on linear actions of $p$-nilpotent groups, and in the quasiprimitive case it relies on a classification of Holt and Yang and on computer calculations.

papers.title: Holomorphic flexibility properties of strongly commuting varieties
papers.abstract: We study holomorphic flexibility properties of the strongly commuting variety of a complex semisimple algebraic group $G$. We prove that the smooth locus of the strongly commuting variety of $G$ is Oka-$1$. We also prove that the smooth locus of the commuting variety of a semisimple complex Lie algebra is Oka-$1$, and that it contains a Zariski dense open subset which is algebraically elliptic.

papers.title: Uniform comparison of multiplier and test ideals for polynomials with affinely independent support
papers.abstract: Let $f\in\Q[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ have affinely independent exponent vectors. We prove that its test ideals agree with the reductions of its multiplier ideals at all nonnegative real exponents for every sufficiently large prime in one arithmetic progression. The progression depends only on the support of $f$.

papers.title: Categorical Torelli and Fourier-Mukai partners of hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: Let $X\subset\PP^{M-1}$ be a smooth hypersurface of degree $d<M$, and let $\Ku(X)$ be its Kuznetsov component, the orthogonal complement of the line bundles $\OO_X,\dots,\OO_X(M-d-1)$ in the derived category. We prove that $\Ku(X)$ determines $X$ for every smooth quartic in $\PP^{4k+1}$, $k\geq1$; together with earlier work, this gives categorical Torelli for every smooth hypersurface of degree $d<M$ with $d\nmid M$. The same algebraic reconstruction proves the classical generic Torelli theorem for these quartics, which completes generic Torelli for smooth hypersurfaces whose degree does not divide $M$, cubic surfaces excepted. When $d$ divides $M$, the Kuznetsov component is a Calabi--Yau category, as for cubic fourfolds, where categorical Torelli is known to fail. We show that, apart from cubic fourfolds, such a hypersurface has a number of Fourier--Mukai partners bounded by a constant depending only on $d$ and $M$, and that categorical Torelli holds in sufficiently large degree, in every dimension. The main tool is a deformation theorem: when geometric deformations surject onto the second Hochschild cohomology of the Kuznetsov components, an equivalence deforms together with the hypersurfaces, so statements proved for general hypersurfaces extend to all smooth ones.

papers.title: Occupation Measures in the ODE Method: Wasserstein Convergence and Rates
papers.abstract: We study occupation measures associated with stochastic approximation recursions within the ordinary differential equation (ODE) method. Under Lyapunov conditions ensuring that the limiting ODE has a globally exponentially stable equilibrium, we establish that the continuous-time occupation measures associated with the piecewise linear interpolation of the iterates converge almost surely in the $2$-Wasserstein topology to the Dirac mass at the equilibrium, the unique invariant probability measure of the limiting semiflow. The choice of the $2$-Wasserstein distance is naturally aligned with our continuous- and discrete-time Lyapunov drift analysis. We also consider two discrete-time sequences of occupation measures, induced by the algorithmic time scale and the iteration count, respectively, and we establish their almost sure convergence to the same invariant measure in the $2$-Wasserstein distance. We then derive corresponding convergence rates in expectation, providing a nonasymptotic complement to the almost sure results. These expectation bounds also imply some tail probability estimates. Finally, we verify that our results apply to a canonical class of linear recursions.

papers.title: Dimensionally absolutely stable but non-diagonalizable $T$-meshes
papers.abstract: We construct an infinite family of rectangular \(T\)-meshes whose conformality-vector-space dimension is constant over all structurally similar geometric realizations, although the meshes are not diagonalizable. For every integer \(d\ge 2\), the construction has \(2(d+2)\) \(\Tl\)-edges and intersection graph \(K_{d+2,d+2}\). Every \(\Tl\)-edge contains at least \(d+2\) vertices, so no edge is vanishable under the usual vertex-count criterion for bidegree \((d,d)\) and smoothness \((d-1,d-1)\). We prove that the conformality-vector space is one-dimensional throughout the structural similarity class. Its generator is the outer product of two vectors of barycentric interpolation weights, extended by four zero coordinates. Non-diagonalizability follows by examining the last edge in any proposed diagonalizing ordering. Thus, for the geometric structural similarity class specified here, diagonalizability is not a necessary condition for dimensional absolute stability.

papers.title: How to prove equations using diagrams: A categorical and operational semantics for e-graphs
papers.abstract: E-graphs are a powerful algorithmic technique for automated equational reasoning but have resisted a conceptual understanding independent of issues of presentation and implementation. We propose an operational semantics for e-graphs based on the fundamental category-theoretic concepts of diagrams, limits, and initial functors. We illustrate the formalism through numerous example calculations and establish its soundness and completeness. Technical prerequisites are kept to a minimum in the main text; less standard elements of the mathematical theory are developed in two appendices.

papers.title: Rule extensions of the implication--negation fragment of intuitionistic logic
papers.abstract:
We present an algebraic study of extensions of the implication--negation fragment $\mathrm{IPC}_{	o,
eg}$ of intuitionistic propositional logic. Such extensions by inference rules correspond to subquasivarieties of the variety $\var{Ho}$ of Hilbert algebras with zero. We describe the lattice of such extensions of $\mathrm{IPC}_{	o,
eg}$ by means of its generators: it is isomorphic to the lattice of upsets of a countable poset, and in particular it is completely distributive. Consequently, $\var{Ho}$ is not Q-universal, in contrast to several other varieties related to $\mathrm{IPC}$. Nevertheless, this lattice is very complex: at each suitably defined height it has intervals containing continuum many quasivarieties which are not varieties. To the best of our knowledge $\mathrm{IPC}_{	o,
eg}$ is the only natural fragment of intuitionistic logic known to combine a completely distributive lattice of extensions with continuum many non-axiomatic extensions.

papers.title: Empirical approximation of $L^p$ norms for $p\in (1, 2)$
papers.abstract: For $p\in[1,2]$, we prove uniform moment estimates for weighted sums \[ \sum_{j=1}^m\zeta_jw_j|\langle{\bf v}_j,y\rangle|^p \] of independent subgaussian random variables $\zeta_j$, where the unit vectors $\{{\bf v}_j\}_{j=1}^m$ and nonnegative weights $\{w_j\}_{j=1}^m$ form an isotropic frame. This allows us to obtain optimal sampling discretization of $L_p$ norms for each fixed $p\in[1,2]$. Namely, for an $N$-dimensional space $X_N$ of bounded functions satisfying $\|f\|_\infty\le\sqrt {KN}\,\|f\|_{L_2}$ for every $f\in X_N$, we show that $m\ge C\varepsilon^{-2}KN\log(2N)$ independent samples $\xi^1,\ldots,\xi^m$ provide the discretization \[ (1-\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p}^p \le\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m|f(\xi^j)|^p \le(1+\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p}^p \quad\forall f\in X_N \] with probability at least $1-\exp(-c\frac{m\varepsilon^2}{KN})$. This implies a corresponding weighted discretization result that, for $1<p<2$, improves Talagrand's bound on the dimension $m$ needed to embed $N$-dimensional subspaces of $L_p$ into $\ell_p^m$ with distortion at most $1+\varepsilon$, giving $m\le C\varepsilon^{-2}N\log(2N)$.

papers.title: Homogeneous Polynomial Carleson Operators Along the Paraboloid
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove boundedness on $L^p(\mathbb{R}^{n+1})$, $1<p<\infty$, of polynomial Carleson operators along the paraboloid with phase belonging to a class $Y$ of homogeneous polynomials. For $n,d\ge 2$, let $\mathcal{P}^{n,d}$ denote the class of all real-valued homogeneous polynomials in $n$ variables of degree $d$. We may take the class $Y$ to be an arbitrary linear subspace $Y \subseteq \mathcal{P}^{n,d}$ such that $\dim Y \le M_{n , d}$, where $M_{n , d}$ is a constant depending only on $n$ and $d$. The main novelty of our result is that we may allow a large collection of homogeneous polynomials of the same degree, in contrast to earlier results that relied on distinct degree assumptions. The heart of our proof is a $TT^*$ method, and the derivation of new estimates for oscillatory integral kernels involving interactions between homogeneous polynomial phases and the paraboloid.

papers.title: Parabolic Extrapolation of Compactness with Applications to Characterizations of the Parabolic CMO Space via Parabolic Fractional Commutators
papers.authors: Mingming Cao, Weiyi Kong, Dachun Yang, Wen Yuan, Chenfeng Zhu
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove two compactness parabolic extrapolation theorems for linear operators and their commutators on parabolic weighted Lebesgue spaces. As applications, we show that $b\in\mathrm{PCMO}$ (parabolic CMO space) if and only if $b\in L_\mathrm{loc}^1$ and the commutator $[b,I_\alpha^{\gamma+}]_k$ is compact from $L^r(\omega^r)$ to $L^q(\omega^q)$ for any $k\in\mathbb{N}$, $1<r<q<\infty$ with $\frac{1}{r}-\frac{1}{q}=\alpha\in(0,1)$, and $\omega\in A_{r,q}^+(\gamma)$ (parabolic Muckenhoupt class), where $I_\alpha^{\gamma+}$ is the parabolic fractional integral. Several other equivalent characterizations of the space $\mathrm{PCMO}$ are also given. Our approach combines the unweighted compactness for mixed commutators, a local lower estimate for $[b,I_\alpha^{\gamma+}]_k$, and both a quantitative Uchiyama-type description and the equivalence with $\inf_T\{\|[\cdot,I_\alpha^{\gamma+}]_k-T\|_{L^r\to L^q}^\frac{1}{k}\}$ of $\mathrm{dist}_{\mathrm{PBMO}}(\cdot,\mathrm{PCMO})$, where the infimum is taken over all compact operators $T:L^r\to L^q$. Finally, we establish two parabolic weighted Fr\'echet--Kolmogorov compactness criteria, which further induce a parabolic interpolation theorem of compactness.

papers.title: Wandering continua, renormalization, and Lebesgue measure on Julia sets
papers.abstract: We study the Lebesgue measure of wandering continua and related invariant sets in Julia sets, using the hyperbolic area method recently developed by Ye. For entire functions of finite type, we show that a wandering continuum of positive area must escape to infinity uniformly. For infinitely renormalizable unicritical polynomials, we show that almost every point in the renormalization core (the intersection of the orbits of little Julia sets) is recurrent and contained in the postcritical set. The main tool is a conservativity theorem: if $f$ is injective on a forward invariant measurable subset $E$ of the Julia set, then $f|_E$ is conservative and almost every point of $E$ is recurrent and contained in the postsingular set.

papers.title: Magnetic Bloch eigenvalue problems in nonuniform periodic magnetic fields: a Fourier-finite difference approach
papers.abstract: We study magnetic Bloch eigenvalue problems for two-dimensional magnetic Schr\"odinger operators with nonuniform periodic magnetic fields and periodic scalar potentials, and develop a hybrid Fourier-finite difference discretization. A Landau-type gauge is constructed by solving a periodic Poisson equation. Under the integer magnetic flux condition, the magnetic Bloch boundary conditions are incorporated through shifts of Fourier-mode indices. The method combines link-variable-based covariant central differences in the $x$-direction with a Fourier pseudospectral discretization in the $y$-direction, yielding a Hermitian discrete Hamiltonian. The resulting eigenvalue problems are solved using a LOBPCG method. Under appropriate regularity assumptions, we establish a fully discrete consistency residual estimate of order $O(h_1^2+N_2^{-s})$. With suitable spectral separation and eigenspace dimension-preserving conditions, error estimates of the same order are derived for isolated eigenvalues and their associated eigenspaces. Numerical experiments show second-order convergence in the finite difference direction and rapid error reduction with increasing Fourier resolution, and illustrate band degeneracies and eigenstate distributions in nonuniform periodic magnetic fields.

papers.title: Scaling Limits and Fractal Dimensions of $\omega$-Substitution Graph Systems
papers.authors: Qingcheng Zeng, Yumei Xue, Cheng Zeng
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a class of non-homogeneous self-similar constructions, called $\omega $-substitution graph system, in which the interface vertices are determined by an infinite sequence $\omega .$ The associated graph sequences naturally form compact metric measure spaces, and under suitable assumptions on $\omega$, we establish their convergence in the Gromov-Hausdorff-Prokhorov sense. We determine the Hausdorff and box-counting dimensions of the limiting space. We further prove that the discrete Hausdorff dimension of the graph sequence coincides with the Hausdorff dimension of its scaling limit. As a direct application of the scaling limit, asymptotic formulas are derived for a class of generalized Wiener indices, which include the classical Wiener index and Kirchhoff index as special cases. Finally, closed-form expressions for these indices are also obtained.

papers.title: One-Vertex Lifts of Looped Circle Graphs: Obstructions and Interlace Polynomials
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be the adjacency matrix of a looped simple graph over $\mathbb{F}_2$ and let $t=\operatorname{diag} M$. We study the one-vertex lift with adjacency matrix $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}M+tt^T&t\\t^T&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. A looped circle graph is called stable if its lift is a circle graph. We prove that stability is equivalent to the existence of a pseudo-orientable bouquet realizing the given looped circle graph. We then obtain a finite excluded toggle-minor characterization by applying two rooted constructions to the known excluded pivot-minors for circle graphs. An exact enumeration yields $22$ minimal toggle-equivalence classes: one of order $5$, twelve of order $6$, and nine of order $7$. The enumeration is accompanied by independently checkable linear-algebra and minor certificates. Finally, we prove $q(G^\dagger;y)=yq(G;y)$ for the vertex-nullity interlace polynomial of every looped simple graph, and derive quasi-tree counting and real determinant formulas.

papers.title: Exact $3$-Adic Periods of Symmetric Dellac Numbers and Their Polynomial Extensions
papers.abstract: The odd and even symmetric Dellac numbers are the specializations $a_n=f_n(0)$ and $e_n=f_n(1)$ of the Randrianarivony--Zeng family $f_n(s)=2^{-n}D_n(s)$. Using a finite Stieltjes-fraction truncation, we establish the sharp congruence $v_3(a_n)=1$ for $n\ge2$ and obtain explicit congruences modulo $81$ for both sequences. We also establish universal eventual periodicity modulo arbitrary positive integers. For every integer $s\ge0$ and $k\ge1$, we give and analyse formulas for the \emph{least} eventual period of $f_n(s)$ modulo $3^k$ and its \emph{least starting index}. The period is governed by five linear factors in $s$; the onset follows a nine-class formula modulo $9$. In particular, for $k\ge3$ the even symmetric Dellac period is three times the odd period and begins one index earlier. The proofs combine a finite Stieltjes-fraction certificate, a graded $3$-adic pole expansion, and an explicit finite top-degree certificate over $\F_3$. Finite integer-arithmetic checks supplement the proofs. We also record the connection with the type-$B$ homogenized Linial arrangement.

papers.title: Ray-Tracing-Based Dynamic Channel Sounding With Autoregressive Wi-Fi CSI Prediction
papers.authors: Lyutianyang Zhang, Yixin Ying, Liu Cao, Vanlin Sathya, Jinke Ren, Shuguang Cui
papers.abstract: Channel sounding in Wi-Fi multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems must balance channel state information (CSI) accuracy against CSI acquisition overhead. Device mobility causes channel aging, while autoregressive CSI prediction introduces errors that accumulate over sounding intervals. However, standardized statistical channel models cannot fully capture the environment-specific channel dynamics encountered in physical artificial intelligence (AI) applications, motivating the use of Sionna-based ray tracing to evaluate CSI prediction under device mobility and evolving propagation geometry. This paper develops a dynamic sounding framework that integrates autoregressive CSI prediction with signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR)-constrained interval selection. A Transformer with rotary position embedding that converts device positions into CSI sequences predicts CSI across multiple subcarriers for beamforming updates between sounding exchanges. We formulate sounding-interval selection as a predicted average-throughput maximization problem under per-stream SINR lower-bound constraints, including CSI acquisition and processing overhead. A prediction-error perturbation analysis provides the SINR bounds, and cumulative-sum enumeration globally solves the finite single-variable problem. Actual SINR feasibility holds whenever the prediction errors satisfy the bounds. Ray-tracing experiments assess channel prediction, trajectory transfer, and autoregressive prediction errors. In single-STA Wi-Fi 7 link-level simulations, predicted-CSI beamforming improves mean goodput by 67.3%, 112.7%, and 119.1% over stale CSI for linear, circular, and cosine trajectories, respectively.

papers.title: Magnitude, path and coarse homology
papers.abstract:
In this article, we introduce Borel--Moore and uniformly finite versions of magnitude homology and path homology for locally finite graphs by allowing possibly infinite chains subject to local finiteness and boundedness conditions. In both settings, we construct magnitude--path spectral sequences extending the spectral sequence studied by the author. Their E^1-pages are given by the corresponding magnitude homologies, their E^2-pages contain the corresponding path homologies on the p-axis, and they converge to coarse homology and uniformly finite homology, respectively, in the sense of Nowak--Yu. Moreover, the E^{r+1}-page is invariant under r- homotopy, whereas the homology to which the spectral sequence converges is invariant under coarse equivalence. Thus the spectral sequences interpolate between small-scale and large-scale geometry.
  We also show that the Borel--Moore and uniformly finite magnitude homologies are products and restricted products, respectively, of ordinary magnitude homology groups with a fixed initial point. Hence the E^1-page is assembled from pointwise magnitude-homological data, providing a mechanism for combining local information into global large-scale invariants. As applications, we establish Mayer--Vietoris sequences for magnitude homology, path homology, the associated spectral-sequence pages, and coarse and uniformly finite homology. We also show that diagonality of ordinary magnitude homology implies degeneration at the E^2-page, yielding isomorphisms between path homology and the corresponding coarse homology. Finally, we discuss applications to Cayley graphs of graph products, including right-angled Artin groups and right-angled Coxeter groups.

papers.title: Linear adaptive variable time step schemes for the anisotropic phase field dendritic crystal growth model
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a class of efficient, linear and decoupled adaptive variable time step schemes for the anisotropic phase field dendritic crystal growth model. The main difficulty is twofold: the gradient dependent anisotropic coefficient and the strongly nonlinear terms make unconditional energy stability difficult to achieve, and on nonuniform meshes the discrete energy dissipation law, which is straightforward to establish on uniform meshes, has to be reestablished under varying step sizes. To overcome these difficulties, two linear stabilizers and a time dependent auxiliary variable with relaxation are introduced and incorporated into a second-order generalized BDF-type operator, with the spatial derivatives discretized by the Fourier spectral method. The proposed schemes are energy stable for arbitrary positive adjacent step ratios, so that no restriction on the step ratio is imposed, and only two linear equations together with a few algebraic equations, which are solved independently in Fourier space, need to be solved at each time step. Moreover, the schemes are naturally compatible with energy based time adaptive strategies. The associated adaptive strategy reduces the number of time steps by $24.6\%$--$86.6\%$ in comparison with uniform time stepping, and numerical experiments on fourfold and sixfold dendritic growth in two dimensions and on three-dimensional growth confirm the accuracy, efficiency and stability of the proposed schemes.

papers.title: Coherent configuration on 3-uniform hypergraph over strongly regular graph
papers.abstract: This paper investigates coherent configurations on 3-uniform hypergraphs constructed from strongly regular graphs. We establish that the hypergraph preserves the automorphism group of the original graph and induces a nonhomogeneous Schurian coherent configuration. Using the case of Petersen graph, we obtain a configuration with two fibers and thirteen basic relations. We further determine their valencies and nonzero intersection numbers, together with the corresponding adjacency matrix multiplication identities.

papers.title: Failure of superharmonicity near an isolated singularity of the critical biharmonic equation
papers.authors: Juncheng Wei, Hui Yang, Ronghao Yang
papers.abstract: Let $n\ge5$ and $u$ be a positive singular solution of $\Delta^2u=u^{(n+4)/(n-4)}$ in a punctured ball. A long-standing question is where or not $ -\Delta u>0$ in the punctured ball. In this paper we show that the answer is negative. More precisely we construct a positive singular solution whose singularity at the origin is nonremovable, while its lower limit there is zero. On a normal subspace, $-\Delta u$ converges to a strictly negative constant. The spherical minimum has order $r^\beta$, where $2<\beta<4$, and the spherical Harnack ratio is unbounded. The proof uses balanced planar polygons, finitely many exterior parameters and a countable gluing construction.

papers.title: The enhanced polylogarithm conjecture in weight two for imaginary quadratic fields
papers.abstract: Zagier's polylogarithm conjecture predicts that special values of Dedekind zeta functions can be expressed in terms of polylogarithms at algebraic arguments. For imaginary quadratic fields, Zagier and Gangl refined it by lifting both sides to complex values modulo rational multiples of a power of $2\pi i$. In previous work, the author extended their enhanced zeta values from ideal classes to ray classes by means of the Shintani $L$-function of two variables and formulated the enhanced polylogarithm conjecture for ray classes. In this article, we prove this conjecture in weight two. More precisely, we establish a Galois-equivariant equality between the enhanced partial zeta values of ray classes and the enhanced dilogarithms of elements of the rational Bloch groups of the corresponding ray class fields. These elements are constructed explicitly, starting from the Eisenstein class of Doran and Kerr on the square of a CM elliptic curve and contracting it with the graphs of complex multiplication.

papers.title: Long-memory Hermite functional processes in functional time series spectral asymptotics
papers.authors: M. C. D\"uker, P. Zoubouloglou, M. D. Ruiz-Medina
papers.abstract: Functional Non-Central Limit Theorems (NCLTs) are derived, in the functional spectral domain (see RuizMedina, 2022), for square integrable transformations, mapping an H_{1}-valued Gaussian stationary functional sequence into a nonlinear H_{2}-valued sequence, where H_{1} and H_{2} are separable Hilbert spaces. Linear and nonlinear operator-based scalings are considered, leading to different limit LRD Hermite functional processes. Under bounded linear operator scalings, an infinite-dimensional version of Theorem 5.3.1 in Pipiras and Taqqu (2017) is obtained, involving a functional reduction theorem, extending Theorem 5.3.3 in Pipiras and Taqqu (2017). Alternatively, when an operator-valued exponent based nonlinear scaling is applied, we pay attention to the LRD dominant set at each active output direction, in the leading chaos. Both scaling scenarios allow the derivation of NCLTs under similar settings of conditions.

papers.title: Geometric Multigrid Preconditioners for conforming Finite Element Methods on Arbitrarily Agglomerated Meshes
papers.abstract: Geometric multigrid methods for conforming finite element discretisations classically require a nested mesh hierarchy, forcing coarse meshes to be conforming, which is unsuitable for general domains. In order to eliminate this geometric constraint, we introduce and analyse a family of multilevel auxiliary space preconditioners. At the first level, a conforming Lagrangian discretisation on a fine simplicial mesh is preconditioned by a non-conforming polytopal discretisation posed on an arbitrarily agglomerated coarse mesh. At the subsequent levels, the coarse problem is solved by a geometric multigrid method for that polytopal discretisation on further agglomerated meshes, so that the whole hierarchy is generated from the fine mesh by agglomeration alone. We consider two polytopal discretisations, a symmetric interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin method and a hybrid high-order method. The prolongation operator at the first level is an element-wise interpolation onto the fine mesh followed by nodal averaging, preceded in the hybrid high-order case by a local potential reconstruction. For point-Jacobi and vertex-star patch additive Schwarz smoothers, we prove that the condition number of the preconditioned system is bounded by $O((H/h)^3)$, where $H/h$ is the coarsening ratio, and by $O((H/h)^2)$ for the DG variant with penalty proportional to $H/h$. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions, on structured and unstructured meshes with agglomerates generated by automatic clustering algorithms, confirm the robustness of the preconditioners.

papers.title: The integral Chow rings of $\mathcal A_3$ and $\mathcal M_3$
papers.abstract: Over $\mathbb C$, we compute the integral Chow ring of $\mathcal A_3$, the moduli stack of principally polarized abelian threefolds. Along the way, we compute the integral Chow ring of $\mathcal M_3$, the moduli stack of smooth genus-three curves. The ring $\CH(\mathcal A_3)$ is generated by the Chern classes of the Hodge bundle, along with three classes supported on the locus of decomposable abelian varieties, subject to 16 relations. The ring $\CH(\mathcal M_3)$ is generated by the Chern classes of the Hodge bundle, with five relations. In particular, we find that the top Chern class of the Hodge bundle, $\lambda_3$, has order 504 on $\mathcal A_3$ and 252 on $\mathcal M_3$. For $\mathcal A_3$, this removes the factor of 4 from the bound $252\mid\operatorname{ord}(\lambda_3)\mid 1008$ of Ekedahl and van der Geer.

papers.title: The Maximum Principle and Optimal Gradient Estimates of Solutions to the Insulated Conductivity Problem
papers.abstract: We study the insulated conductivity problem with two unit spherical inclusions embedded in a bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $n\ge3$. The gradient of solutions may blow up as the distance between the two inclusions goes to zero. We introduce bispherical coordinates and expand the solution in spherical harmonics. Then we use the maximum principle to give a new proof of the optimal gradient estimate obtained by Dong-Li-Yang.

papers.title: Finiteness of Non-decomposable Critically Frustrated Signed Graphs
papers.abstract: A signed graph $(G,\sigma)$ is a graph $G$ with a signature $\sigma$ labeling each edge with a positive or negative sign. Two signatures of $G$ are switching equivalent if one is obtained from the other by sequentially changing the signs of all edges in an edge-cut. The frustration index of a signed graph $(G, \sigma)$ is the minimum number of negative edges among all signatures switching equivalent to $\sigma$. A signed graph is critically $k$-frustrated if it has frustration index $k$, and the removal of any edge decreases its frustration index. A critically $k$-frustrated signed graph is prime if it is irreducible and contains no two edge-disjoint negative cycles. Steffen and Naserasr et al. asked if there are only finitely many prime critically $k$-frustrated signed graphs for any positive integer $k$. The cases $k\leq 3$ were proved to be true by Cappello et al., and later, the cases $k=4$ and $5$ were verified by Z. Wang. In this paper, the author proves the conjecture by a topological argument.

papers.title: Quantum Adiabatic Theorem under Wiener Noise:Maximal Mean-SquareEstimates
papers.authors: A. M. H. H. Caldera, R. P. K. DeSilva, K. K. W. A. S. Kumara, B. P. W. Fernando
papers.abstract: We derive maximal mean-square adiabatic estimates for finite-dimensional stochastic Schr\"odinger equations with Hamiltonian-proportional Wiener noise. For deterministic $C^2$ Hamiltonians whose eigenvalues have constant multiplicities and do not cross on $[0,1]$, we construct a unitary stochastic adiabatic intertwiner driven by the same Wiener process as the exact propagator. A commutator argument, It\^o calculus, and Doob's maximal inequality yield an explicit bound for the expected supremum of their squared operator-norm difference on a selected initial eigenspace. Under uniform coefficient bounds, the physical noise scaling $\alpha=\sigma T^{-\gamma}$, where $T$ is the total evolution time and $\sigma\geq0$ and $\gamma\geq0$ are fixed, gives maximal mean-square error $O(T^{-2}+\sigma^4T^{-4\gamma}+\sigma^2T^{-(2\gamma+1)})$. Consequently, adiabatic convergence holds for every $\gamma>0$ as $T\to\infty$, while $\gamma\geq1/2$ recovers the deterministic $O(T^{-1})$ bound for the root-mean-square maximal error. For fixed nonzero physical noise amplitude, the estimate leaves convergence unresolved.

papers.title: Capelli Operators and the Bernstein-Sato polynomials of Minors
papers.abstract:
For every ideal of minors of a generic complex matrix, we determine all roots and their multiplicities in the Bernstein-Sato polynomial. These roots lie in explicit rational intervals indexed by the rank strata. Every nonintegral root is simple, whereas the multiplicity of each integral root equals the number of labels producing that root. We deduce the strong motivic monodromy conjecture, including the inequality relating pole orders to root multiplicities; for minors of size $r$, the largest possible root multiplicity over all matrix dimensions is $\lfloor\sqrt{4r-1}\rfloor$.
  Keywords. Bernstein-Sato polynomial, determinantal ideal, root multiplicities, strong monodromy conjecture.

papers.title: Toward Shifted symplectic Chiralization: Deformation of Courant Algebroids
papers.abstract: We study the chiralization of Poisson--Lie theory through graded symplectic geometry. We compare Courant deformations and classical $r$- and $R$-matrix constructions, obtaining integrable hierarchies and free field realizations. We give a variational description of the obstruction to Lie conformal bialgebra compatibility and recover Liberati's obstruction in the Virasoro case. We also introduce a vertex bialgebra analogue of quantized universal enveloping algebras and construct explicit quantizations to all orders of Cartan type Lie conformal bialgebra structures on $\operatorname{Cur}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$. These results contribute to the first author's broader programme of developing shifted symplectic chiralization as a geometric method for constructing chiral analogues of Poisson-Lie structures via $n$-shifted symplectic geometry, and exploring its connections with AKSZ theory and quantization.

papers.title: The Cone Fixing the Reals of $\mathrm{HOD}^{M_{2n}(x)}
papers.abstract: For a cone of reals $x$, the reals of $\mathrm{HOD}^{L[x]}$ are precisely the reals in $Q_3$, or equivalently, the set of reals in $M_1$, the minimal proper class mouse with a Woodin cardinal. We show that if $z$ is any real coding $M_1|\delta^{+M_1}$, then $z$ is the base of such a cone (so $M_1^{\#}$ is such a base). We also establish a kind of optimality for this result, by identifying a real $x$ such that $M_1\subseteq L[x]$ but $\mathbb{R}\cap\mathrm{HOD}^{L[x]}\not\subseteq M_1$, although there is a base for the cone in a generic extension of $L[x]$. We prove analogous results for $M_{2n}(x)$ for all $n$, with the optimality result holding for all $n$.

papers.title: Poissonian Pair Correlation and Discrepancy Rates
papers.authors: Bo Tan, Zhen Zhang, Qing-Long Zhou
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of a sequence in $[0,1)$ with Poissonian pair correlation (PPC) and optimal-order star discrepancy $D_N^*=O((\log N)/N)$, and further give a deterministic construction by applying a conditional-expectation rule to a nested dyadic random model. We also show that PPC imposes no universal discrepancy decay rate: for every positive sequence $\rho_N\to0$, there exists a PPC sequence with $D_N^*/\rho_N\to\infty$. Under suitable regularity and growth assumptions, we realize prescribed discrepancy asymptotics, including $D_N^*\sim c_\beta N^{-\beta}$ for every $0<\beta<1$, with $c_\beta>0$. We further construct a PPC sequence satisfying $D_N^*\asymp(\log N)/N$ for all sufficiently large $N$.

papers.title: Galois's lost proof on $PSL(2,p)$
papers.abstract: In his famous ``testamentary letter'' Galois formulated several results without proof. Among them he claimed --- here we express it in modern terms --- that the projective special linear group $PSL(2,p)$ has a subgroup of index $p$ only for $p\le 11$. Nowadays this result is seen as a corollary of the complete enumeration of all subgroups of $PSL(2,p)$ obtained by Gierster in 1881. In this paper we attempt to give a proof that uses only methods available to Galois.

papers.title: Non-admissible smooth irreducible representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ for totally ramified extensions $F/\mathbb{Q}_p$
papers.abstract: Let $p\geq 5$, and let $F/\mathbb{Q}_p$ be a nontrivial finite totally ramified extension. We construct a non-admissible smooth irreducible representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$. The construction uses representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathcal{O}_F)$ on which the first principal congruence subgroup acts nontrivially, together with a deformation of a diagram indexed by $\mathbb{Z}$.

papers.title: Exact Transport-Information Correspondence for Distribution-Adaptive Discretization
papers.abstract: Discretization of continuous probability distributions is an operation on the sample space, and the structure induced by this operation cannot generally be determined solely from information geometry. In our recent work on unavoidable canonical nonlinearity (UCN), we established a non-arbitrary connection between the transport cost associated with discretization and the information-geometric indistinguishability of continuous probability distributions. Through the transport-information correspondence, the UCN quantify the information-theoretic cost due to discretization as the expected Kullback-Leibler divergence between nearby continuous distributions associated with the discretization geometry. In the original UCN construction, discretization is implemented by transporting the probability mass within each cell to its geometric centroid. The resulting transport-information correspondence, however, is derived under specific conditions involving the cell geometry, spatial coverage, and the vanishing-cell-scale limit. In this work, we introduce an alternative local-map discretization scheme in which the probability mass within each cell is transported to its own probability-weighted centroid. This change in the representative-point selection enables an exact expression for the transport cost of each cell in terms of the covariance matrix of its conditional probability distribution and the Fisher metric of the underlying continuous family. We establish an exact correspondence between the resulting transport cost and the expectation of the associated Fisher-induced quadratic form, without requiring uniform cell geometry, complete coverage of the sample space, or an infinitesimal cell-scale limit. The proposed construction thus generalizes the transport-information correspondence to finite-scale discretization using arbitrary collections of non-overlapping bounded convex sets.

papers.title: On Wilker-Type Properties
papers.abstract: Wilker-type properties record how a compact set can be split along a binary open cover, and they are precisely the continuity conditions for the union operation on open lattices, governing the topology of power and function spaces. We give a unified treatment of the four properties $\W$, $\Ww$, $\Wi$ and $\Win$. We prove that $\Wi$ and $\Win$ are hereditary for arbitrary subspaces, whereas $\W$ and $\Ww$ are hereditary only for closed subspaces; all four are preserved by continuous retracts, and $\Ww$, $\Wi$, $\Win$ are finitely additive over topological sums. For KC-spaces $\Ww$ and $\Wi$ coincide, and spaces whose compact subspaces are Hausdorff belong to $\Win$. Using Kov\'ar's compact KC-space $M_0$ and its variant $\QQ^{+}$, we obtain countably infinite compact KC-spaces in $\Wi\setminus\W$, showing $\Wi$ is strictly weaker than $\W$. Conversely, we construct compact $T_1$ spaces whose product fails $\Ww$, proving the classes $\Ww$ and $\Wi$ are not reflective. We further show Vietoris constructions need not preserve $\Wi$, and prove that $\Ok(M_0)\cong \Ck(M_0,\Sier)$ is not sober and fails property~$S$. Open problems are collected at the end.

papers.title: The Minimal excludant of $\ell$-regular partition
papers.abstract: Andrews and Newman \cite{andrewsnewmanI} introduced and studied ``mex,'' function for an integer partition $\lambda$ of a positive integer $n$. The related function $\sigma^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ was subsequently defined, and its generating function and other properties have been studied by several authors. In this article, for a positive integer $\ell \geq 2$, we define the minimal excludant of an $\ell$-regular partition $\lambda$ of a positive integer $n$. We then define $\sigma_\ell^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$, the sum of the minimal excludants over all $\ell$-regular partitions of $n$, and obtain explicit generating functions for $\sigma_\ell^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ in the cases $\ell = 2$ and $\ell = 3$, expressed as eta-quotients. We prove that the sequence $\sigma_\ell^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ is weakly increasing for every $\ell$, and we obtain Hardy--Ramanujan type asymptotic formulas for $\sigma_2^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ and $\sigma_3^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ as $n \to \infty$. Additionally, we completely determine the parity of $\sigma_2^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$, showing that it is odd precisely at generalized pentagonal numbers, and we use this characterization to compute the density of $n$ for which $\sigma_2^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ is odd versus even. Finally, for $\sigma_3^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$, we prove that it is odd infinitely often, and we establish a quantitative lower bound, showing that the number of such $n$ up to $X$ grows at least like $\log \log X$.

papers.title: Odd and even fake quadrics isogenous to a product
papers.authors: Fabrizio Catanese, JongHae Keum, Do Geun Kim, Kyoung-Seog Lee
papers.abstract: A $\mathbb{Q}$-homology quadric is a smooth compact complex surface which has the same $\mathbb{Q}$-homology as a quadric surface, that is, the product of two $2$-dimensional spheres. It is called fake if it is minimal and not rational. Among them are the fake quadrics which are isogenous to a product of complex curves. In this paper, we determine the parity of the intersection forms of all fake quadrics isogenous to a product of unmixed type. In particular, we show that there are fake quadrics with odd intersection forms.

papers.title: Descriptor representations of geometric port-Hamiltonian systems on Hilbert spaces
papers.abstract: We establish conversions in both directions between geometric and descriptor representations of linear port-Hamiltonian systems on infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. For the geometric-to-descriptor conversion, we represent the possibly multivalued inverse Dirac relation by a skew-adjoint operator on enlarged Hilbert spaces, retaining the original operator-domain restrictions. The construction accommodates internal and external ports. We show that the conversions preserve trajectories and the power balance. An incompressible Kelvin--Voigt solid illustrates the results.

papers.title: On the Cameron-Praeger conjecture for Steiner 6-designs
papers.authors: Ximin Wang, Zheng Huang, Weijun Liu
papers.abstract: A long-standing and far-reaching conjecture of Cameron and Praeger (1993) asserts that no non-trivial block-transitive $6$-$(v,k,\lambda)$ designs exist. Huber (2010) reduced the Steiner case ($\lambda=1$) to a single infinite family of possible exceptions, where the automorphism group is $G=\PGaL(2,p^e)$ acting on the points of the projective line, with $p\in\{2,3\}$ and $e$ an odd prime power. In this paper, we resolve this final case. By combining orbit-stabiliser analysis for the action of specific involutions in $\PGaL(2,p^e)$ with the modular arithmetic constraints derived from the design parameters, we prove that no such Steiner 6-designs can exist for any admissible $q$. This completes the proof that the Cameron-Praeger conjecture is true for the important case of non-trivial Steiner 6-designs.

papers.title: Iterated minimal Darboux transformations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the superposition of two minimal Darboux transformations in Euclidean three-space. A four-dimensional permutability diagram for transformations of isothermic surfaces yields the common minimal transform for distinct nonzero parameters and an explicit formula for its Gauss map. This formula determines the planar ends over regular umbilic-free points of the seed: an end is embedded when the two transformed Gauss maps coincide away from the seed value and has multiplicity 3 when all three values coincide. We illustrate this criterion with the Enneper surface and the catenoid. For the catenoid, suitable parameters give complete surfaces of finite total curvature, and we determine the numbers and multiplicities of their planar ends from the parameters and initial values. In the family with multiplicity-3 ends, the remaining initial-value parameter realizes, up to rotation, the L\'opez--Ros deformation.

papers.title: Neighbourhood second Zagreb matrix of graphs: spectral radius bounds and extremal graphs
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a connected graph on at least two vertices, and let $\delta(i)$ be the sum of the degrees of the neighbours of a vertex $i$. The \emph{neighbourhood second Zagreb matrix} $\NF(G)$ has $(i,j)$-entry $\delta(i)\delta(j)$ if $i\sim j$ and $0$ otherwise; its spectral radius is denoted by $\rNF(G)$. We prove that $\rNF(G)\ge\rho(G)^{5}$, where $\rho(G)$ is the adjacency spectral radius, with equality if and only if $G$ is regular or bipartite semiregular, and we use this to show that the same graphs are exactly the extremal graphs of a Berman--Zhang--type upper bound. We sharpen the estimates $\demin^{2}\rho(G)\le\rNF(G)\le\demax^{2}\rho(G)$ by means of the extreme edge weights of $\NF(G)$, give sharp upper bounds in terms of the maximum degree $\dmax$, the maximum neighbourhood degree sum $\demax$, the size $m$ and the clique number $\omega(G)$, and determine the extremal graphs for bipartite graphs and trees. For every connected unicyclic graph $G$ of order $n\ge3$ we prove $32=\rNF(C_n)\le\rNF(G)\le\rNF(\Sp n)$, where $\Sp n$ is the triangle with $n-3$ pendant edges at one vertex, with equality only for $C_n$ and only for $\Sp n$, respectively. Finally, we give bounds in terms of the first Zagreb index and for the neighbourhood second Zagreb energy; for lower energy bounds, the extremal graphs are described completely.

papers.title: Constrained minimization problem and unbounded dynamics for the four-dimensional Klein-Gordon-Schr\"{o}dinger System
papers.authors: Masaru Hamano, Hiroaki Kikuchi, Kenta Tomioka
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the Klein-Gordon-Schrodinger system in four spatial dimensions. We consider a constrained minimization problem associated with the corresponding stationary system and establish the existence of a positive radial minimizer. We further investigate the asymptotic behavior and qualitative properties of minimizers. As an application, we analyze the dynamics of solutions with initial data in a potential well and prove that such solutions either blow up in finite time or exhibit unbounded growth in the energy norm as time tends to infinity. Since the minimizers lie on the boundary of the potential well, we also establish the strong instability of the associated standing waves.

papers.title: Compatible Condensation and Generalized Gauging: Marked Transport and Wall Interchange
papers.abstract: We formulate condensation compatible with a specified separable generalized gauging operation in a unitary (2 + 1)-dimensional defect realization. Compatibility is a coherent reversible crossing of the full condensate algebra, retaining charged channels and the marked condensation interface. The resulting composite network determines the transported condensate, the induced operation, and a commuting square of specified walls. For connected gauging data, compatibility admits a central matching description that retains the transported condensate and its algebra identification on the specified wall. The specified unit may absorb a nontrivial parent anyon algebra; strong connectedness appears only as the transparent-unit specialization. We distinguish original vacuum insertions, vacuum branches after unit absorption, and the full vacuum algebra of the final phase, and we prove a complete Higgs criterion that incorporates the parent algebra absorbed by the specified unit. In the toric-code example of a non-invertible subgroup gauging we classify the compatible condensations for the fixed operation, exhibit two inequivalent crossings of the same parent condensate that lead to different final phases, and analyse a pure condensation operation in which the specified unit absorbs the parent electric condensate and produces additional final vacuum operators. The transparent-unit case recovers reverse-condensation transport and the vacuum-overlap formula, and the three complete Higgs conditions appear as a corollary of the general criterion.

papers.title: PCF All The Way Down
papers.authors: Taylor Dupuy, Alon Levy, Thomas Tucker, Zhouran Wang
papers.abstract:
We prove that a finite surjective post-critically finite self-map of a variety in characteristic zero remains post-critically finite on every preperiodic integral effective divisor after passing to its periodic image with its return map. Iterating this result proves PCF all the way down.
  A detailed report on AI usage is contained in the manuscript.

papers.title: Geodesic Transversal of Hypercube and Butterfly networks
papers.authors: R. Prabha, B. Sandhiya, Paul Manuel
papers.abstract: A geodesic $P$ of a connected graph $G(V,E)$ is called a maximal geodesic if there exists no geodesic $P'$ in $G$ that contains $P$ as its sub-path. The geodesic transversal problem determines a subset $S\subseteq V(G)$ such that every possible maximal geodesic of $G$ includes at least one vertex of $S$. Such a set with minimum number of elements is called a gt-set and its cardinality is the gt-number of $G$. In this paper, we establish a general result, called the Geodesic Transversal lemma which provides a lower bound for the gt-number of an arbitrary graph $G$ in terms of the gt-number of its induced subgraphs. Using this lemma, we determine the gt-number of Butterfly and Hypercube networks.

papers.title: Reconstruction and well-posedness of an inverse coefficient problem for a diffusion equation
papers.authors: Siyu Cen, Bangti Jin, Yavar Kian, Zhi Zhou
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate the inverse coefficient problem of determining an unknown coefficient in a diffusion equation from a single boundary flux measurement. More precisely, assuming that the domain is cylindrical, we develop a unified theoretical and numerical framework for the stable reconstruction of a space-time-dependent coefficient, by reformulating the inverse problem as a nonlinear equation. The inherent nonlinearity of the problem is transferred to an auxiliary nonlinear equation, enabling the application of techniques and concepts from nonlinear analysis. By combining representation formulas with regularity properties of solutions to diffusion equations, we extend to nonlinear inverse problems an approach that has so far been restricted to linear ones. The theoretical reconstruction procedure is complemented by a numerical analysis of the proposed method, including convergence and error estimates, as well as numerical experiments. The proposed reconstruction algorithm is directly inspired by the theoretical framework.

papers.title: A Viscous Cascade Construction of Nonunique Leray--Hopf Solutions to the Unforced 3D Navier--Stokes Equations
papers.authors: Thomas Y. Hou, Xiang Qin, Peicong Song, Wenhan Zhang
papers.abstract:
We construct a nonzero divergence-free initial velocity on $\mathbb{R}^3$ and a continuum of pairwise distinct suitable Leray--Hopf solutions of the unforced three-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations on a common time interval. The initial datum is axisymmetric, smooth away from the origin, and belongs to every $L^{\mathfrak q}$ with $1\leq \mathfrak q<3$, but not to $L^3$. All the solutions attain this datum strongly in $L^2$, are smooth at positive times, and satisfy both the global and local energy equalities through time zero. The same family belongs simultaneously to every $L^{\mathfrak p}_tL^{\mathfrak q}_x$ with $1\leq \mathfrak p\leq\infty$, $2\leq \mathfrak q\leq\infty$, and $2/\mathfrak p+3/\mathfrak q>1$. The same solutions also belong to the critical Lorentz space $L^\infty_tL^{3,\infty}_x$. This endpoint is sharp for uniqueness in the Leray--Hopf class within the Lorentz scale.
  The proof is entirely analytic and uses a cascade through geometrically separated Gaussian swirls. We establish growth for the time-dependent viscous linearization and determine the sign of its complete quadratic stress, including the interaction of the reference velocity with the second variation. The integrated stress generates a controlled perturbation at the next larger spatial scale. At each finite cutoff, a prescribed terminal coordinate selects an initial perturbation whose physical $L^2$ norm tends to zero as the cutoff is removed. Uniform energy, moment, and transfer estimates yield the common strong initial trace while preserving a nonzero observable at a fixed positive time.

papers.title: The Convergence Rate of Accelerated Proximal Gradient Methods with General Inertia Term for Convex Composite Multiobjective Optimization
papers.abstract: We study accelerated proximal gradient methods with general stepsizes for convex composite multiobjective optimization, in which every objective is the sum of a smooth convex term and a proper closed convex extended-valued term, and the proximal subproblem retains a separate offset for each objective. The momentum coefficient may depend on the computed trajectory. For a two-parameter root momentum rule we prove boundedness, weighted square summability of the displacements, a merit-function rate of $o(k^{-2})$, and displacement decay of $o(k^{-1})$ whenever the first parameter converges to a value in $(0,1)$; the second parameter need not converge or have bounded total variation. The analysis is organized as a chain of basic estimates, an energy identity, coefficient asymptotics, and auxiliary lemmas that are reused in every regime. For the critical parameter $\alpha=3$ we establish the finite bound $u_0(x^N)\le 2\ell R/[N(N+3)]$, square summability of the displacements, displacement decay $O(1/N)$, and convergence of the full sequence to a weak Pareto point. The remaining little-o question at $\alpha=3$ is shown to be exactly the vanishing of a nonnegative critical energy, so it is separated from the large-$O$ estimate rather than left as a missing step. For $1<\alpha<3$ we give the rate $O(N^{-(\alpha-1)})$ and for every $\alpha>0$ the qualitative conclusion $u_0(x^k)\to0$, $F_i(x^k)\to c_i$, and $\sum_k D_k/k<\infty$. A table summarizes the rate picture over the whole positive range of $\alpha$, and a JOS1 experiment illustrates the predicted little-$o$ separation.

papers.title: Highly connected uniquely $k$-linked digraphs
papers.abstract: Extending a result of Thomassen, we prove that for every choice of positive integers $K\geq k$ there exist a $K$-strong digraph which has two disjoint sets $S,T$ each of size $k$ so that the only linkage from $S$ to $T$ in $D$ is the one whose existence follows from Menger's theorem.

papers.title: Hadamard configurations and sharp cubic-period bounds for stealth in dimensions 10, 11, and 12
papers.abstract: We construct explicit, nonlattice periodic point configurations in dimensions $10$, $11$ and $12$ with stealth center density $1/24$ and unit-density stealth radius $2\cdot24^{-1/n}$. These values exceed those of duals of the current record lattice packings, without claiming to exceed all possible lattices. The construction uses the $24$ sign rows of an order-$12$ Hadamard matrix and their antipodes, projected onto $n$ coordinates. For an arbitrary, not necessarily binary, equally weighted motif with marked period $2\mathbb{Z}^n$, we prove a sharp $2n$-point lower bound for a raw stealth radius at least one and classify equality by antipodal Hadamard configurations. We deduce bounded-complexity optimality, sharp optimality among binary motifs in dimensions $10$--$12$, and local maximality under simultaneous perturbations of the motif and the marked period shape. A divisibility argument excludes ordinary equally weighted periodic formal duals. Statements are confined to their indicated classes; no global optimality among arbitrary-period configurations is asserted.

papers.title: Flux-Matched Poisson Iteration for Generated Jacobian Equations: Local Convergence and Spectral Galerkin Approximation
papers.abstract: We develop a flux-matched Poisson iteration for solving generated Jacobian equations with second boundary conditions. In each step, it solves a fixed shifted Poisson problem with a Neumann-type boundary condition. Near a smooth regular solution with positive $C^{1,1}$ densities, we prove that the iteration has local geometric convergence in $C^{2,\alpha}$ on smooth connected Riemannian domains. The iteration is then discretized using a spectral Galerkin method, with local convergence proved for the Fourier-Jacobi scheme on spherical caps. Optical numerical experiments support these estimates and demonstrate useful imaging performance beyond the local convergence theory.

papers.title: Koszul duality and homotopy algebras for operads over quivers
papers.abstract: For a quiver $Q$, we introduce and study $Q$-operads (or operads over $Q$), defined as a special sort of $\mathbf{fc}$-multicategories or virtual double categories, in which the directions of the arrows of $Q$ encode the permitted input orderings. In this higher operadic framework, we construct the bar--cobar adjunction and develop a theory of Koszul duality and homotopy algebras, together with compatibility results under changes of quiver. We treat dg categories and their left modules, right modules, and bimodules as algebras over quiver-operads. We prove that these operads are Koszul and that their resolutions govern the corresponding $A_\infty$ categories and modules. We also categorify Sagave's notion of derived $A_\infty$ algebras and introduce modules over derived $A_\infty$ algebras and categories. Finally, we explain that restriction along a folding of quivers constructs diagonal $A_\infty$ bimodules, while extension along an inclusion of quivers realizes two-sided bar models of derived tensor products.

papers.title: Optimal Error Estimates With Polynomial Dependence on $\epsilon^{-1}$ for Mixed Finite Element Methods of the Cahn-Hilliard-Navier-Stokes System
papers.authors: Haijun Gao, Xi Li, Xiaoli Li
papers.abstract: In this paper, we analyze a first-order convex-splitting mixed finite element scheme for the Cahn--Hilliard--Navier--Stokes system, tracking explicitly how the error constants depend on the interface width $\epsilon$. Due to the strong nonlinear coupling inherent in the CHNS system and the singular dependence of the Cahn--Hilliard equation on $\epsilon$, conventional energy-based analyzes often lead to severe dependence of the error constants on $\epsilon^{-1}$, and may even result in exponential growth. Such dependence significantly limits the applicability of the resulting error estimates in the small-interfacial-thickness regime. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a robust parameter error analysis framework with respect to interfacial thickness $\epsilon$.
