For $p \in (1, \infty)$, the spectrum is independent of $p$, consists entirely of eigenvalues and exhibits a spectral gap. For $p=1$, the spectrum is instead the left half-plane. Furthermore, we discuss ultracontractivity and hypercontractivity properties of the semigroup.

papers.title: Independent Backward Preimages and Algebraic Radial Decompositions of Operators
papers.authors: Zakariae Aznay, Fadil Chabbabi, Hassan Zariouh
papers.abstract: Let $T\in\mathcal{B}(X)$, where $X$ is a complex Banach space. We introduce the spaces $\mathcal{I}_s(T)$, defined by independently chosen preimages under the powers of $T$ with exponential growth bounds, and study algebraic radial decompositions involving $\mathcal{H}_r(T)$, $\mathcal{K}_s(T)$, and $\mathcal{I}_s(T)$. We prove that every algebraic decomposition $X=\mathcal{H}_r(T)\oplus\mathcal{I}_s(T)$ is topological and that $\mathcal{I}_s(T)=\mathcal{K}_s(T)$. This removes the closedness assumption in the radial decomposition theorem of Koliha and Poon. We also prove that, for $0\leq a\leq b$, the closedness of $\mathcal{I}_b(T)$ and $\mathcal{H}_a(T)+\mathcal{I}_b(T)$ implies $\mathcal{I}_b(T)=\mathcal{K}_b(T)$. We establish finite-defect and circular spectral criteria and characterize the Cantor--Bendixson derivatives of the spectrum, Browder spectrum, and Drazin spectrum in terms of radial decompositions and quotient restrictions. As applications, we obtain new characterizations of generalized Drazin, generalized Drazin--Riesz, generalized Drazin--meromorphic, and $g_z$-invertible operators in terms of radial subspaces.

papers.title: Delay-induced multirhythmicity in a 3-cell inhibitory network
papers.authors: Xinxin Qie, Morten Gram Pedersen, Jian Song, Shenquan Liu, Andrey L. Shilnikov
papers.abstract: We study the dynamics of a delayed three-cell central pattern generator network using return-map analysis and a phase-reduced description derived from generalized FitzHugh-Nagumo oscillators. The phase model captures the emergence and stability of synchronous, pacemaker, and traveling-wave rhythms and provides a systematic, computationally efficient framework for characterizing the network dynamics beyond direct return-map calculations. We conduct extensive two-parameter analyses of both the full and phase-reduced models, revealing rich multi-rhythmic dynamics and transitions among coexisting rhythmic states. The close agreement between the two descriptions establishes phase reduction as an efficient and reliable framework for characterizing the dynamical organization of delayed neural oscillator networks.

papers.title: Matching Random Point Sets with Minimum Distortion
papers.authors: Itai Benjamini, Mark Braverman, Elad Tzalik, Georgii Zakharov
papers.abstract:
How well can two independent random samples from a metric measure space be matched while preserving pairwise distances? Concretely, given two independent copies, each of $n$ points sampled from the space, what is their typical metric distortion as finite $n$-point metric spaces? We prove that the space $[0,1]$ equipped with the uniform measure already exhibits a rich behavior. We show that with high probability the distortion of the two independent samples is $n^{2/3}$ up to polylogarithmic factors.
  The lower bound reflects two competing obstructions. A bijection that maps points close to their original positions or their reflections in $[0,1]$ must expand the smallest gaps, in both directions. On the other hand, we show that large displacement from both the identity and reflection itself forces large distortion. Balancing these obstructions yields the lower-bound exponent $2/3$. For the upper bound, we construct a partial matching of the points that maps each gap between consecutive points of length $d\lesssim n^{-4/3}$ to a pair at distance $\widetilde{O}(dn^{1/3})$, with analogous control in the reverse direction. We then use a delicate multiscale oscillation construction to extend this partial matching to a low-distortion bijection.

papers.title: Morphisms of $A_\infty$-algebras and modules
papers.abstract: $A_\infty$-algebra is a chain complex equipped with a coherent multiplicative structure, i.e. a multiplication which is commutative up to (higher) chain homotopy. Similarly $A_\infty$-module over such algebra is equipped with its coherent action. These notions are used to represent cohomological information contained in topological multiplicative structures. One of the key tools of the theory are minimal models, which are useful in cohomological computations. In this thesis author presents certain sufficient conditions for a morphism of $A_\infty$-modules to induce a morphism of their minimal models.

papers.title: Hessenberg character
papers.authors: Patrick Brosnan, Jaehyun Hong, Donggun Lee
papers.abstract:
Let $G$ be a connected reductive group with Borel subgroup $B$, flag variety $\mathcal B=G/B$, and Weyl group $W$. We define the \emph{Hessenberg functor} on the geometric Hecke category by microlocalizing along the diagonal in $\mathcal B\times\mathcal B$ and pushing forward along the Springer map. It induces the \emph{Hessenberg character} of the Iwahori--Hecke algebra, with values in graded $W$-representations. On Kazhdan--Lusztig basis elements indexed by smooth elements of $W$, this character recovers the cohomology of the associated regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties. We identify the Hessenberg functor with the microlocalization of Lusztig's character functor and compute the Hessenberg character using Lusztig's nonabelian Fourier pairing.
  More generally, for families of Hessenberg schemes defined by pure-dimensional $B$-stable closed cones in the tangent space $T_{eB}\mathcal B$, we show that monodromy on the intersection cohomology of regular semisimple fibers factors through $W$. When the cone is the tangent cone of a Schubert variety, we give a local condition at $eB$ under which the same character formula computes the graded $W$-character of this intersection cohomology.
  Combined with the methods of Precup and Sommers, our character formula can be used to compute the graded $W$-characters of all regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties in all Lie types of rank at most ten, including all exceptional types. These computations also motivate positivity and unimodality conjectures for Hessenberg varieties and Lusztig varieties in types $B$, $C$, and $D$, together with positivity conjectures for their partial flag versions.

papers.title: Largest Sperner families with bounded VC-dimension
papers.authors: Gennian Ge, Hanyu Wang, Zixiang Xu, Yixuan Zhang
papers.abstract: A conjecture of Frankl proposed in the 1980s states that for $n\ge2d$, every Sperner family $\mathcal{F}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ of VC-dimension at most $d$ has at most $\binom{n}{d}$ members. We prove this conjecture for every fixed $d$ and large $n$, and show that equality holds only when $\mathcal{F}$ is $\binom{[n]}{d}$ or $\binom{[n]}{n-d}$.

papers.title: The pliability of del Pezzo surfaces
papers.abstract: We study $G$-Mori fibre space models of $G$-del Pezzo surfaces, focusing on surfaces over non-closed fields. We construct explicit examples of birationally rigid sextic del Pezzo surfaces and give a negative answer to a generalization of Koll\'ar's question on birational rigidity and field extensions: a sextic del Pezzo surface of Picard rank $1$ can fail to be birationally rigid over its ground field but become birationally rigid after an algebraic field extension. We interpret this phenomenon in terms of the failure of injectivity of natural maps in nonabelian Galois cohomology induced by the inclusion of automorphism groups into birational automorphism groups. We also show that finite pliability is unbounded: for every integer $d\geqslant2$, we construct a sextic del Pezzo surface of index $3$ over a field of characteristic zero whose pliability is exactly $3^d+1$.

papers.title: Heavy-Light Wall Crossings and Motivic Asymptotics of Moduli Spaces of Curves. Part I: Stabilization Graphs and Euler Characteristics
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we develop an explicit calculation of ordinary topological Euler characteristics of the coarse moduli spaces underlying Hassett spaces in the minimal all-light chamber and the Deligne-Mumford compactification. For genus $g\ge2$, we organize the calculation through a decomposition indexed by stabilization graphs and their decorations. The Burnside-Lefschetz formula allows us to compute the resulting contributions, taking into account graph symmetries and their fixed loci.
  The calculation in genus two illustrates the method explicitly and, in the Deligne-Mumford case, recovers the generating function of G. Bini, G. Gaiffi, and M. Polito (arXiv:math/9806048), with the corrections of G. Bini and J. Harer (arXiv:math/0506083), providing a check on the construction. We also carry out the calculation in genus three in an appendix. Together with an elementary genus-one calculation based on collision partitions and rational necklaces, these formulas yield complete asymptotic expansions as the number of labeled markings tends to infinity. The passage from all-light to ordinary Euler characteristics is governed by the universal change of variables $\Phi(z)=(2-z)e^z-2$, which we derive by a direct wall-crossing argument.
  For arbitrary fixed genus $g\ge2$, the same framework identifies the leading contribution of rational trivalent graphs and gives the ordinary asymptotic scale $n!(e-2)^{-n}n^{(3g-5)/2}$. The leading constants are the symmetry weights of these graphs; we derive their generating function, recurrence, and large-genus behavior. We also determine the asymptotic ratio of all-light to ordinary Euler characteristics, answering a question of S. Kannan, S. Serpente, and C. H. Yun (arXiv:2207.02800).

papers.title: Finite-Time Blowup for Navier-Stokes with Smooth Forcing, Part II: Residual Correction via Oscillatory Pulses
papers.abstract: This paper is a companion to Part I: Construction of Self-Similar Solutions with Admissible Stress and Flat Remainder (arXiv:2609.35406). Part I constructs approximately self-similar flow profiles with a singular stress in divergence form. The associated velocity becomes unbounded as $t\uparrow 1$. Here, localized oscillatory pulses cancel this stress contribution through their averaged quadratic momentum flux. Successive corrections preserve the velocity growth and leave a smooth external force $f\in C^\infty$. This gives a local solution of the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with forcing $f$. Its velocity satisfies $\limsup_{t\uparrow 1}\|u(t)\|_{L^\infty}=\infty$. Together, the two papers present a readable and accessible account of OpenAI's Finite Time Blowup for Navier-Stokes. We claim no original mathematical contribution.

papers.title: A property of boundary extensions of atomic singular inner functions
papers.authors: Iason Efraimidis, Adrian Llinares, Sullivan MacDonald, Ignacio Uriarte-Tuero, Dragan Vukotic
papers.abstract: Using a property of the Hilbert transform, we prove a measure theoretic result concerning the extensions of atomic singular inner functions to the circle. Various alternative proofs are presented using the mean value theorem for harmonic functions and a well-known property of Blaschke products. Using the main result, we establish several facts concerning atomic singular inner functions and their logarithms.

papers.title: The full Kolakoski shift is topologically transitive
papers.authors: Andrew C. Mitchell, James J. Walton, Michael F. Whittaker
papers.abstract: We prove that the full Kolakoski shift---namely, the subshift of all smooth sequences over the alphabet $\{1,2\}$---is topologically transitive. Consequently, we demonstrate the existence of a smooth sequence whose factors are invariant under both reversal and bitwise complementation. As a further application, we prove the existence of arbitrarily long smooth words containing an equal number of occurrences of the symbols $1$ and $2$, providing evidence in support of Keane's conjecture. Our approach leverages the hierarchical structure of the full Kolakoski shift to reimagine the shift action in terms of a self-similar semigroup, which allows techniques from group theory and combinatorics to be applied.

papers.title: On Natural Exponential Families with Log-Affine Generalized Variance
papers.abstract: We study natural exponential families whose generalized variance, the determinant of the covariance matrix, is log-affine in the natural parameter. Without any assumption on the natural parameter domain, we show that every such family is regular and that it is Gaussian when its generalized variance is constant. Consequently, a sample of size $n>d$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ comes from a non-degenerate normal law exactly when the conditional expectation of the sample generalized variance given the sample mean is a positive constant. Every non-Gaussian family puts mass on a facet of its convex support, and, as for a Poisson count, its height above that facet takes only integer multiples of a fixed step. More generally, its displacement away from any exposed face that carries mass has nonnegative integer coordinates in a suitable basis. A local inequality between third and fourth cumulants singles out the Poisson--Gaussian families and yields a complete classification of the infinitely divisible ones. Geometrically, a semi-flat K\"ahler tube, whose potential has constant Hessian determinant, is flat if some multiple of its metric is projectively induced near a point.

papers.title: Off-Diagonal Induced Ramsey Numbers
papers.authors: Bruno Andrades, Marcelo Campos, Rafael Filipe, Anastasiia Kats
papers.abstract: Given graphs $F$ and $H$, the induced Ramsey number $r_{\mathrm{ind}}(F,H)$ is the smallest integer $n$ for which there exists a graph $G$ on $n$ vertices such that every red-blue colouring of $E(G)$ contains either a blue induced copy of $F$ or a red induced copy of $H$. A conjecture of Kohayakawa, Pr\"omel and R\"odl asserts that, for every fixed graph $F$, this number is polynomial in $v(H)$. We prove this conjecture, showing that there is an absolute constant $C > 0$ such that $$r_{\mathrm{ind}}(F,H) \leq v(H)^{Cv(F)^2}$$ for all graphs $F$ and $H$. The proof combines a variant of a random geometric construction of Kohayakawa, Pr\"omel and R\"odl with the hypergraph container method.

papers.title: Risk-Sensitive Stochastic Optimal Control on Positive Cones
papers.abstract: We consider stochastic optimal control problems in which the state is constrained to a proper cone. Specifically, we consider risk-neutral, risk-averse, and risk-seeking formulations within a single entropic-risk framework. We investigate classes of problems whose Bellman operator preserves affine functions and characterize their optimal value functions and feedback policies for both finite-horizon and time-average infinite-horizon problems. Additionally, we establish convergence and state-bound results under finite-step cost observability. Moreover, we demonstrate an exact connection between entropic-risk optimal control on proper cones and deterministic infsup control for systems whose dynamics and stage costs are affine in the disturbances. In addition, we provide examples of classes of systems for which explicit solutions can be obtained.

papers.title: $\omega$-limit sets of triangular maps over periodic orbits of the base
papers.abstract: Let $F(x,y)=(f(x),g(x,y))$ be a continuous triangular map of the unit square and let $z=(x_0,y_0)$ be a point such that $\omega_f(x_0)$ is a periodic orbit $\{p_0,\dots,p_{m-1}\}$ of $f$. Then $\omega_F(z)=\bigcup_{i}\{p_i\}\times M_i$ for nonempty compact sets $M_i$, and we ask which $m$-tuples $(M_0,\dots,M_{m-1})$ occur. For $m=1$ the answer is a theorem of Kolyada and Snoha. We show that a tuple occurs if and only if there are continuous surjections $M_i\to M_{i+1}$, indices modulo $m$, whose composition around the cycle is chain transitive. This is a cyclic version of classical facts due to Dowker and Friedlander, Sharkovsky, Hirsch, Smith and Zhao, and Kolyada and Snoha. It yields two necessary conditions: no $M_i$ is one of the exceptional sets of Kolyada and Snoha, and there are continuous surjections $M_0\to M_1\to\dots\to M_{m-1}\to M_0$. We prove that these conditions are also sufficient when every $M_i$ has uncountably many connected components, and when every $M_i$ has countably many components of which only finitely many are nondegenerate. In particular the sections of one $\omega$-limit set need not be homeomorphic. Every tuple satisfying the two conditions falls into one of these cases or into a single remaining class, in which the sections have countably many components and infinitely many of them are nondegenerate; that class is studied in a companion paper.

papers.title: Uniform Central Limit Theorems for Degree Distributions of Sparse Graphon Models
papers.abstract: The degree distribution is among the most basic summaries of a network, yet no functional limit theorem for the empirical degree distribution of graphon models has been available, even for dense, bounded graphons, for which only finite-dimensional results were known. We study the empirical degree distribution of sparse $L^p$ graphon models, allowing unbounded kernels and hence heavy-tailed degrees. For graphons whose latent expected degrees have a density, we prove a finite-dimensional central limit theorem whenever $n\rho_n/\log n\to\infty$ and $n\rho_n^{2+\beta}\to0$, where $\rho_n$ is the sparsity level and the kernel has $2+\beta$ moments for some $\beta>0$; the limiting covariance coincides with that of the dense case. Under additional local regularity, we establish a functional central limit theorem on compact intervals in the interior of the support. Under tail regularity and a stronger sparsity condition, we prove that uniformity extends to unbounded intervals. We also show that uniform limits fail at atoms of the degree distribution, for instance in stochastic block models. The analysis rests on an exact multilinear representation of the conditional degree distribution, which identifies its Hoeffding decomposition without Edgeworth expansions, combined with a lattice version of Billingsley's tightness criterion and moment inequalities of Efron-Stein type.

papers.title: Lifts of Brauer characters and vertex pairs for odd primes
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $G$ be a finite $p$-solvable group, and let $\varphi\in\IBr_p(G)$ have vertex $Q$. We prove that $\varphi$ has at most $|Q:Q'|$ lifts to ordinary irreducible characters, establishing Cossey's conjecture for odd primes.

papers.title: Sublinear multi-type preferential attachment
papers.authors: Anna Ben-Hamou, Nicolas Broutin, Camille Cazaux
papers.abstract: We consider a random growing graph model with two \emph{types}, or \emph{communities}, that belongs to the class of preferential attachment models. Starting from an initial graph $G_0$ in which each node has a type, the graph $G_{n+1}$ is generated by addition of a new node, which attaches through an edge to a node $v$ of $G_n$. The probability of attaching to $v$ depends on the communities of both the new node and $v$, and is proportional to $\operatorname{deg}_n(v)^\gamma$, where $\gamma\in[0, 1]$. We establish a convergence result for the limiting proportion of vertices of each degree and in each community in a certain regime of the parameter $\gamma$. To this end, we first use stochastic approximation techniques to reduce the convergence problem to the study of a non-linear evolution equation. We then use a probabilistic coupling approach to investigate the long-time behavior of the unique solution to this evolution equation. We emphasize that the techniques previously used to handle the single-community case cannot be extended directly to our setting. Indeed, the associated continuous-time embedding is not a multitype branching process in the usual sense, since the transition rates at any given time $t$ depend on the entire graph structure at that time.

papers.title: Representations of 3D Rotations: Mathematical Foundations and Comparative Analysis
papers.authors: Aizierjiang Aiersilan, Haochen Liu, James Hahn
papers.abstract: Rotation representations are foundational in fields such as computer graphics, robotics, and machine learning, where precise and efficient modeling of 3D orientations is critical. This paper comprehensively investigates diverse representations of the special orthogonal group $SO(3)$, such as Euler angles, axis-angle vectors, quaternions, rotation matrices, exponential maps, and emerging continuous and probabilistic methods, evaluating their mathematical formulations, continuity, susceptibility to gimbal lock, computational efficiency, storage requirements, interpolation properties, and composition operations, while integrating detailed algebraic insights with practical applications in fields like animation, pose estimation, inertial navigation, 3D shape registration, and neural networks. Empirical evidence highlights quaternions' dominance due to their compactness and computational efficiency, while alternatives like 6D continuous representations and matrix Fisher distributions provide enhanced continuity and uncertainty modeling. Future research could explore hybrid methods and thorough large-scale evaluations to help build a solid foundation for improving rotation representation techniques.

papers.title: Pauli Supported Invariants for Periodic Graphs-Derived Hamiltonians
papers.authors: Sarah Chehade, Andrew Vlasic, Rebekah Herrman, Rick Mukherjee
papers.abstract: We introduce a graph invariant obtained from Pauli decompositions of Hamiltonians derived from local graph neighborhoods. Given a rooted h-hop neighborhood, we construct a local adjacency operator, embed it into a common Hilbert space dimension, and define its Pauli-support set as the collection of Pauli strings appearing with nonzero coefficients. For periodic graphs, we prove invariance under lattice-compatible graph equivalence and establish converse results under root-separation hypothesis. The framework naturally extends to Lie closures, commutants, and Cartan-type structures generated by the associated Pauli supports. We further discuss extensions to aperiodic graphs with finite local complexity and make connections to cut-and-project models of quasicrystals and notably, Penrose tilings. From a quantum information perspective, the resulting invariants provide a operator-theoretic description of graph-based Hamiltonians and offer a new mechanism for comparing graph-based quantum systems through Pauli-support data.

papers.title: A Sharp Dynamic Haussler Lemma
papers.abstract:
Haussler's covering lemma (JCTA 1995) gives the sharp $(C/\delta)^d$ metric-entropy bound for binary VC classes under normalized $\ell_1$ distance. We prove a sharp global dynamic analogue for bounded real-valued classes in normalized $\ell_p$, for every $1\le p<\infty$. Writing $d=\operatorname{sfat}_{\varepsilon/32}(\mathcal F)$, we obtain a global dynamic cover of size at most $(C/\varepsilon^p)^d$ for every horizon and $0<\varepsilon<1/2$. Here a single family of deterministic causal experts, fixed independently of the instance sequence, covers every target on every sequence. For $0<\varepsilon<1/4$, a matching worst-case lower bound $(c/\varepsilon)^{pd}$ holds already for binary classes on one fixed sequence, even with real-valued experts. The constants are universal, independent of $p$.
  For $p=2$, this resolves the horizon-independent sequential $\ell_2$ covering problem of Rakhlin, Sridharan, and Tewari (PTRF 2015) in a stronger global form. For $p=1$, it gives the sharp $(C/\delta)^{\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal H)}$ global dynamic covering bound for binary classes, resolving questions of Alon, Ben-Eliezer, Dagan, Moran, Naor, and Yogev (STOC 2021) and Malliaris and Moran (Trans. AMS 2024). Our proof combines rank-decreasing correction schedules and accurate sampled prefixes with exact continuations after target identification. Shared-parent routing distributes these continuations among eligible prefixes, eliminating the logarithmic overhead.

papers.title: The Liouville property for geometric graphs in the plane
papers.authors: Kuijun Liu, Feng Luo, Yanwen Luo, Zhenghao Rao
papers.abstract: We show that every bounded discrete harmonic function with respect to the cotangent Laplacian on a Delaunay triangulation of the Euclidean plane is constant; equivalently, the cotangent-weighted triangulation has the Liouville property. Our main theorem establishes this property for a more general class of connected weighted geometric graphs in the plane. Furthermore, we show that a planar Delaunay triangulation with cotangent weights could be transient but is recurrent if edge lengths are uniformly bounded.

papers.title: Scaly: an Optimizing Compiler for Optimal Control
papers.authors: Tudor A. Oancea, Colin N. Jones
papers.abstract: We present Scaly, an open-source optimizing compiler for optimal control, written in Python, that generates fast C code. Scaly provides a modeling language embedded in Python for the parametric optimization problems that arise in model predictive control and moving horizon estimation, and computes the sparse derivatives that standard optimization solvers need. Scaly accepts general nonlinear programs but applies optimizations specific to optimal control, which preserve the repeated structure of a problem, such as the stages of a horizon, through differentiation down to the generated loops. The generated C depends only on the C math library and never allocates memory dynamically. On three benchmark problems, Scaly evaluates the Hessian of the Lagrangian up to 26 times faster than CasADi, with smaller binaries and build times that stay nearly constant with the horizon. With the same solver, Scaly shortens the solver time per control step on every benchmark, by a factor of up to 9.

papers.title: Applying Changes to LDPC Codes by Using 3-Induced Matchings and Eigenvalues
papers.authors: Alireza Eshraghi Dehaghani, Sara Saeedi Madani, Dariush Kiani
papers.abstract: The 2-switch operation for reducing the number of short cycles in Tanner graphs of LDPC codes has been utilized in some works. If this operation is appropriately applied to a 2-induced matching in a bipartite graph, then it surely preserves the bipartiteness of the graph. With a 2-induced matching, we have only one choice for applying this type of change to the graph. Using 3-induced matchings creates more potential and flexibility to apply certain changes to the Tanner graph. We present a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of a 3-induced matching in bipartite graphs with girth at least 6. A 3-induced matching helps us to have more choices for applying a change to a bipartite graph while surely preserving the bipartiteness of the graph and keeping the degree sequences unchanged. Among all changes that we consider, we select the best change for reducing the number of cycles of length 6. The eigenvalues of subgraphs are used to reach a 3-induced matching, and a condition in some steps can be checked to ensure that the subgraph has at least one 3-induced matching. We present some numerical results regarding the steps at which the condition that guarantees the existence of a 3-induced matching is checked.

papers.title: Improving the performance of regularized Stokeslet simulations using Rosenbrock time integration methods
papers.authors: Moslem Uddin, Lisa J. Fauci, Ricardo Cortez, Tommaso Buvoli
papers.abstract: The method of regularized Stokeslets (MRS) is widely used to model fluid-structure interactions of microscopic bodies in viscous environments. Specifically, MRS computes the fluid velocity generated by regularized forces distributed on an immersed body, which in turn defines a system of ordinary differential equations with which to evolve the body so that the no-slip condition is enforced. To accurately model material properties such as elasticity and bending rigidity, the resulting ODE system is often stiff and, therefore, computationally expensive to solve with explicit time-integration methods. Here we demonstrate the potential of linearly implicit Rosenbrock (ROS) time integration methods to greatly reduce the computational time required to solve such ODE systems. We focus on the classic model problem of the swimming of a flexible filament driven by preferred curvature forcing. Our findings indicate that, compared to previous MRS simulations, the increased stability of ROS methods allows for speed-ups between twenty and two thousand times over explicit Runge-Kutta (ERK) methods. Moreover, we present approximate scaling laws for this speedup as a function of the key model parameters (bending rigidity and slenderness) at the root of numerical stiffness. Lastly, beyond the basic ROS approach, we discuss several additional strategies that further improve performance.

papers.title: A Fully Polynomial Approximation Algorithm for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Model
papers.authors: Dylan Herman, Shouvanik Chakrabarti, Junhyung Lyle Kim, Guneykan Ozgul
papers.abstract: Montanari's incremental approximate message passing (IAMP) algorithm [FOCS 2019; SIAM J. Comput., 2025] and the zero-temperature formulation of El Alaoui, Montanari and Sellke (AMS) [Ann. Probab., 2021] find a $(1-\varepsilon)$ approximation to the maximum Sherrington-Kirkpatrick (SK) energy in $C(\varepsilon)N^2$ operations for fixed accuracy, with probability tending to one as $N\to\infty$, under their respective full-support and access-model assumptions. However, it was unknown whether this approximation could be achieved with work polynomial in both $N$ and $1/\varepsilon$, together with quantitative guarantees at finite dimension. Under the same assumptions as AMS, we introduce grouped IAMP with exact Gaussian query outputs (GEG-IAMP), which is the first SK approximation algorithm with total work polynomial in $N$ and $1/\varepsilon$ and a finite-size guarantee above a dimension threshold polynomial in $1/\varepsilon$ and $\log(1/\alpha)$. More precisely, for every $\alpha\in(0,1/2)$, it returns a $(1-\varepsilon)$ approximation with probability at least $1-\alpha$ whenever $N\ge \mathsf{K}\varepsilon^{-2}\log^2(e/\varepsilon)\log(\mathsf{K}/\alpha)$, using $O(N^2/\varepsilon)$ work and $O(N^2)$ storage. GEG-IAMP replaces the Onsager correction by Reeves's coupling construction [arXiv:2508.10782] and groups Euler-Maruyama steps into $O(1/\varepsilon)$ matrix-vector products. We also prove a relative guarantee for AMS IAMP with $O(N^2\varepsilon^{-3}\log^2(e/\varepsilon))$ work but a sufficient dimension exponential in inverse accuracy. By returning a fixed configuration below its dimension threshold, GEG-IAMP also provides an asymptotic fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme (AFPRAS), with an additive error independent of dimension.

papers.title: Spectral measures and sharpness of quantum speed limits
papers.abstract: Quantum speed limits bound the time required for a given state to evolve into a given subspace of the Hilbert space under specific energy constraints. We prove that for several standard orthogonalization time bounds, the unique spectral measure associated with the initial vector that saturates the bound is a sum of two Dirac measures. Furthermore, we constrain the families of spectral measures that come arbitrarily close to these bounds and construct examples with measures which are purely absolutely continuous and purely singular continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure. As a complementary perspective, we discuss the geometric intuition behind quantum speed limits provided by the numerical range of the evolution operator.

papers.title: Raychaudhuri-Ehlers Kinematics on Quantum State-Space: Caustics and Extrinsic Quantum Geometry
papers.authors: Neellohit Karmakar, Suraj S. Hegde, Aryan Bhatia
papers.abstract: Quantum mechanics is inherently geometric in that the pure states form a curved complex manifold and the Schr\"odinger evolution defines a Hamiltonian flow on this space. Geometry identifies constraints on flows on quantum state-space that hold independently of their microscopic realization. We uncover such universal behavior in families of geodesic paths on the quantum state-space using the Raychaudhuri-Ehlers equations. We show that the complex structure leads to tidal anisotropy in the curvature, and for Hilbert space dimension $N\geq3$, complete point-emitted geodesic bundles necessarily develop shear and undergo direction-selective focusing at finite distance. We give these geometric results an information-theoretic interpretation in terms of fidelity susceptibility and quantum Fisher information. For ground-state manifolds constrained by physical parameters, we resolve the tidal curvature into Berry-curvature-dependent ambient tides and contributions from extrinsic bending within the full ambient state space. We further relate extrinsic bending to variations in the unitary generator of motion along intrinsic geodesics. We present exact many-body geometric results for the transverse-field XY spin chain. The product structure of the ground state leads to an exact cancellation of the ambient tide, including its Berry-curvature enhancement, by extrinsic curvature contributions. At the zero-field Ising point, we obtain exact results at finite size and show that the shear source for anisotropy-directed motion is entirely extrinsic relative to the full many-body state-space. For the metric in the thermodynamic limit, the geodesic families exhibit repeated $A_2$ fold catastrophes inside the ferromagnetic phase. Our framework thus separates universal state-space effects from those of physical restrictions and exposes their consequences in a paradigmatic many-body system.

papers.title: Quantum error correcting codes from quiver moduli: Grassmannians, cyclic monodromy, and argyle collision divisors
papers.abstract: Building on aspects of a recent diagrammatic field-theory programme for quantum error correction put forward by the first-named author (arXiv:2607.08911), we construct exact finite-dimensional codes from twisted cyclic and argyle quiver moduli on the projective line. A regular fibre of the node-labelled cyclic Hitchin map records the ways to distribute simple spectral zeroes among the arrows with prescribed degrees. The Hilbert space spanned by these allocations is a Young permutation module. Root monodromy acts on its Specht factors and leaves their multiplicity spaces noiseless. Resetting the Specht factor therefore recovers the encoded state for every channel in the monodromy noise model. We prove that the largest Kostka multiplicity is the optimal dimension of a subspace code correcting the full monodromy algebra, even among codes spanning several isotypic blocks. Quantizing an argyle master space recovers the cyclic sheet space as a weight sector of a tensor power, with the identification preserving monodromy. For the balanced three-cycle with $t$ zeroes per arrow, the multiplicity of a partition $(a,b,c)$ of $3t$ is $1+\min(a-b,b-c)$. The optimal logical dimension is thus $t+1$, attained uniquely by the block indexed by $(2t,t)$. At $t=1$ we give explicit codewords for a qubit on six sheets. The commuting right action generates its full logical algebra, yielding errors outside the monodromy model that leave the measured footprint statistics unchanged yet require different recoveries. We also compute collision-parity ranks, give a higher-rank Grassmannian example, and derive a conditional criterion for recovery across splitting types.

papers.title: A Unified Framework for Training-Dataset Aggregation and Exact Machine Unlearning via Gibbs Probability Measures
papers.authors: Yaiza Bermudez, Samir M. Perlaza, I\~naki Esnaola
papers.abstract: In this paper, three operations on Gibbs probability measures are studied: renormalization, normalized log-linear combination, and nesting. The resulting measures are shown to be Gibbs probability measures with explicit expressions for their objective functions, reference measures, and regularization factors. These measures are further characterized as unique solutions to optimization problems involving linear combinations of the original objective functions, subject to either relative entropy regularization or relative entropy constraints. When the reference measures are probability measures, geometric interpretations of these three operations are established involving Pythagorean identities and exponential geodesics.A central result is the equivalence between nesting and normalized log-linear combinations of Gibbs probability measures. These results are then applied to supervised machine learning with Gibbs algorithms, which are represented by Gibbs probability measures. In this context, either through nesting or log-linear combinations, Gibbs algorithms trained on local datasets are used to form new Gibbs algorithms trained upon the aggregation of all local training datasets. Interestingly, the parameters of such operations, determine the weights of each training data point on the aggregated dataset. %Operations on local Gibbs probability measures are shown to control the contributions of training data. This observation is leveraged for achieving: (a) exact machine unlearning in centralized, decentralized, and federated learning systems; and (b) centralized-equivalent performance, in the sense of producing algorithms trained on the aggregation of all local datasets in decentralized and federated learning .

papers.title: Relevance Propagation as Entropic Optimal Transport on Filippov Neural Networks: Sinkhorn Propagation and Region Relevance in Image Classifiers
papers.abstract: Relevance propagation, which redistributes a network's prediction backward through the layers, is usually treated as a heuristic. We show that it is the solution of a single variational problem: Layer-wise Relevance Propagation (LRP) is the divergence-free flow on the active computational graph of zero relative entropy to the backward transition law of the forward activation flow; for a non-negative reference, this is a relative entropy between Markov measures on backward paths. The rules LRP$_0$, LRP$_{z^+}$ and LRP$_{\alpha,\beta}$ follow from this principle by the choice of a reference, and are instances of one rule, LRPN$_{\alpha,\beta}$, whose weights may vary from node to node, for instance with the node's activity, in the spirit of Hebb's principle. The principle rests on a measure-theoretic formalization of feed-forward networks as directed acyclic graphs of Filippov operators, which covers piecewise-smooth and discontinuous architectures (e.g. hard-routed Mixture-of-Experts) with a Clarke-Filippov generalized-gradient calculus; it also characterizes backpropagation as the adjoint equation of a Lagrangian relaxation. On networks of ReLU and max-pooling nodes, LRP$_0$ is Gradient$\times$Input, with an explicit jump across a kink where LRP$_{z^+}$ stays continuous. Taking the entropy edge by edge yields a new rule, Sinkhorn Relevance Propagation. Aggregated over an input region, the flow of a non-negative reference tells, with exact accounting, which hidden units carry its evidence, the conditioned flow being a Schr\"odinger bridge. On VGG-16, the conservation identities hold to round-off, and the rules are told apart by the sign of their maps, the share of the output left to the bias nodes, faithfulness, localization and class dependence; on ConvNeXt-Tiny, LRPN$_{\alpha,\beta}$ conserves the output and its Hebbian weights give the highest ABPC of the rules tested.

papers.title: Geometric ergodicity of the block Gibbs sampler for Bayesian linear mixed models with scale mixtures of normal random effects
papers.authors: Rolando de la Cruz, Nathalie Humeniy
papers.abstract: We study a Bayesian linear mixed model whose random effects follow a scale mixture of normal distributions with an arbitrary mixing distribution, a class that contains the Student-t, slash, contaminated normal, normal-generalized inverse Gaussian and Laplace laws. Conditionally conjugate priors lead to a three-block Gibbs sampler that alternates between the variance components, the latent precision weights, and the regression coefficients together with the random effects. Using a drift function built from fractional powers, we give sufficient conditions for geometric ergodicity of this chain, which involve a moment of the mixing distribution of some order larger than 1/2 and its behaviour near the origin. An equivariance of the sampler under rescaling of the design then shows that the conditions hold for all the families above, including Student-t random effects with any degrees of freedom, for every random-effects design matrix, full rank or not, with the rank entering only the conditions on the priors of the variance components. Together with posterior moment bounds, geometric ergodicity justifies Monte Carlo standard errors and effective-sample-size stopping rules for the regression coefficients and the log-variance components. Simulations examine these procedures at practical run lengths: joint confidence regions need a correction for the number of batches, and under sequential stopping their observed coverage remains slightly below the nominal level. We illustrate the methods with longitudinal beta-HCG measurements from early pregnancies, in which the latent weights reveal larger between-subject variability among abnormal pregnancies.

papers.title: Chiral edge modes from lattice Chern-Simons theory
papers.abstract: It is shown that a level $k$ Abelian lattice Chern-Simons theory with continuum time and a spatial square lattice, which is a topological field theory on the latticized plane and torus, when quantized on a spatial cylinder reduces to chiral edge excitations, exactly localized on the two boundaries and carrying two commuting lattice versions of the level-$k$ $U(1)$ Kac-Moody algebra of opposite chirality. The algebras are represented on a Fock space in the noncompact theory and by a finite Weyl algebra in the compact one. We also observe that the theory has a natural framing of Wilson loops which exhibits the correct framing anomaly.

papers.title: Do Language Models Know Which Constraints Belong Together?
papers.authors: Junbo Jacob Lian, Kaixuan Chen, Hanzhang Qin, Huiling Chen, Chaoyu Zhang, Chung-Piaw Teo
papers.abstract: Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation strengthens the linear relaxation of a mixed-integer program by convexifying a chosen set of constraint families, and every candidate costs a column generation run. The choice is hard when families strengthen the bound only together, because a search that adds one family at a time then stops at the linear relaxation. The classical inequalities of lot sizing, network design and facility location rest on such zero-marginal groups. We prove that when each evaluation convexifies at most $s$ of $k$ families, any method that observes only bounds needs a covering number of evaluations, of order $k^w$, to find a hidden group of $w$ families, also on actual Dantzig-Wolfe relaxations. A prediction that misses $e$ members reduces the cost to $\Theta(k^e)$, through one staged search that does not need to know $e$, so the evaluations a prediction saves measure what the predictor knows. We study two sources of predictions. A one-pass lookahead at an optimal LP dual is provably blind to groups whose families share no variable, and a language model reads the names and text of the model. JointDW verifies the prediction of the language model with the staged search and interleaves it with the lookahead at a bounded loss. Groups that strengthen the bound only jointly appear in a quarter of the MIPLIB-NL models whose bound can be improved. There the strongest language models identify them about as often as the lookahead, their predictions rest on the names for textbook models, and reasoning about doubles the accuracy of the same model. On larger models with distracting families, the lookahead finds the group in one evaluation of three families. Language models given only the text seldom name it, while one reasoning model given every coefficient names it in all but one answer and then needs fewer evaluations than the lookahead for pairs of families.

papers.title: Discovering like a scientist: Literature-informed dimensionless learning for physical closure of data-driven equations
papers.authors: Hao Xu, Tianhao Wu, Dongxiao Zhang
papers.abstract: Data-driven methods can recover compact equations, yet the physical dependence of their coefficients across operating conditions often remains unresolved. Dimensionless groups can explain this variation, but selecting relevant groups from the many dimensionally admissible combinations remains challenging. Here, we introduce a knowledge-guided framework for dimensionless learning, called {\pi}-former. It learns patterns of variable association and exponent assignment from a corpus of 1,288 established dimensionless groups. Under exact dimensional constraints, the model proposes interpretable basic groups whose combinations are optimized against observations. Across seven physical problems, the framework identifies predictive dimensionless coordinates within seconds. Integration with equation discovery further expresses condition-dependent coefficients through these coordinates, recovering established physical scalings in multi-condition simulations. Applied to experimental measurements of evaporation-driven wetting, the framework discovers dimensionless coordinates and uses them to construct a unified trajectory equation. The resulting model generalizes to held-out conditions across liquids and initial volumes, outperforming existing empirical models. These results establish dimensionless learning as a transferable bridge between accumulated scientific knowledge and data-driven equation discovery, enabling artificial intelligence to uncover physically meaningful laws from observations.

papers.title: Towards the Query Complexity of Sampling under Strong Log-Concavity and Log-Sobolev Inequalities
papers.abstract:
We study the query complexity of sampling from smooth distributions on $\mathbb R^d$ using first-order oracles. For $d$-dimensional strongly log-concave targets with condition number $\kappa=2$, we prove that any randomized sampler requires $\exp({\Omega(\log^{1/3} d)})$ queries even from a constant warm start. This rules out polylogarithmic dimension dependence and strictly separates strongly log-concave sampling from Gaussian sampling. For targets with $L$-smooth potentials satisfying an $\alpha$-log-Sobolev inequality with $\kappa= L/\alpha$, we prove an $\Omega(\kappa)$ query lower bound for $d\gtrsim\log^2\kappa$. This shows that log-Sobolev sampling is strictly harder than strongly log-concave sampling.
  Our proofs construct instance-dependent tests that target samples typically pass but outputs of algorithms making few queries typically fail. For strongly log-concave targets, we embed a sequence of hidden Gaussian into high-degree tensor polynomial with smooth gates, forcing any algorithm to uncover the layers sequentially. The log-Sobolev construction hides a constant fraction of the target mass in angular caps while controlling the log-Sobolev constant via delicate estimates.

papers.title: Pathwise-Budgeted LLM Routing: Online Allocation with K-Bit Tail-Cost Learning
papers.authors: Hanzhang Qin, Sophie H. Yu, Yuewei Zhang, Zhi-Hai Zhang
papers.abstract: Firms using large language models under fixed budgets must decide which model to call and whether to retry a failed task. Because a call's charge is revealed only after completion, one long response can exhaust the remaining budget and leave later tasks unserved. Our objective is to maximize the number of tasks solved before service stops. We develop a contextual bandit policy, ADP-HT, which learns each model's task-specific success probability and constructs conservative cost estimates from coarsened response-length labels on a quantile grid with $2^K$ intervals. The policy weighs predicted success against these costs, adjusting the cost penalty to realized spending and the budget available per remaining task. Under calibration, local regularity, and grid-coverage conditions, we bound the excess allowance in the policy's conservative cost estimates. At a fixed sample size, increasing $K$ reduces the discretization term but increases the estimation allowance. At the tightest tested budgets, ADP-HT solves more than twice as many MATH500 and GPQA tasks as the best implemented baseline. It achieves the highest mean cumulative score at ten of fourteen RouterBench budgets. On LiveCodeBench, it outperforms a deployed commercial router in both default and cost-saving modes at the three lowest test budgets.

papers.title: On Convergence of Gradient Temporal-Difference Learning with Regularized Corrections and Eligibility Traces
papers.authors: Jingyi Jin, Martha White, Hao Wang
papers.abstract: Temporal-difference (TD) learning underlies many prediction and control algorithms, but can diverge when combined with off-policy learning, bootstrapping, and function approximation. TD with Regularized Corrections (TDRC) is theoretically sound and practically simple, but existing convergence theory covers only the one-step case under i.i.d. sampling, while the Huber Bellman-error formulation has not been extended to TDRC or eligibility traces. In this work, we establish convergence of constrained TDRC($\lambda$) with diminishing stepsizes and non-i.i.d. off-policy data, for state-dependent and history-dependent $\lambda$-parameters. We also propose TDRC($\lambda$)-Huber, which preserves the TDRC($\lambda$) fixed point while reducing sensitivity to large Bellman errors. For both algorithms, we apply an ODE-based weak-convergence method from stochastic approximation theory. For the nonlinear mean dynamics of TDRC($\lambda$)-Huber, we give an integral small-gain condition that guarantees uniqueness and global asymptotic stability of the target equilibrium. We then establish convergence of the constrained algorithm, derive computable sufficient conditions for convergence, and identify a regularization-based convergence mechanism shared by linear TDRC($\lambda$) and TDRC($\lambda$)-Huber. When the mean TD matrix is positive stable, both constrained algorithms converge under sufficiently strong regularization without requiring positive definiteness.

papers.title: Frequency-Frame Covariance for Reactive-Power Scalarization
papers.abstract: Measured voltage and current waveforms may be represented in a reference frame whose frequency differs from the physical fundamental frequency. Reactive-power readouts calculated from such frequency-shifted coordinates may change if their readout operators are not transformed consistently. This paper presents a frequency-frame covariance formulation for finite-spectrum, zero-mean periodic waveforms with complete harmonic information over one physical period. A necessary and sufficient covariance condition is derived, requiring the readout operator to transform consistently with the waveform representation. Consequently, frequency-dependent harmonic weights must be evaluated at physical harmonic orders rather than relative frame labels. In particular, the derivative/Iliovici readout equals a relative-derivative contribution plus an explicit reference contribution. The formulation also separates readout-operator errors from errors caused by changes in the physical components retained by waveform projections. Three analytical cases illustrate conditional carrier recovery for a memoryless resistor, physical-frequency weighting at relative zero in an RLC branch, and the possibility that an exact reactive-power scalar can coexist with a substantial waveform error after projection. The scope is deterministic calculation consistency in frequency-shifted coordinates rather than instrument measurement uncertainty.

papers.title: How Unbalanced Must a Latin Rectangle Be?
papers.abstract: We view a $k\times n$ Latin rectangle as $n$ points in the grid $[n]^k$. Each symbol gives one point, whose coordinates are the columns it occupies. The rectangle is balanced when these points are pairwise equidistant in the $\ell_1$ metric. Its imbalance measures the distance from this ideal. We study the minimum imbalance from three sides. Constructively, we use a simulated annealing that moves symbols within rows and only penalises column clashes. Against the reference table of Voboril et al. (2025), it improves 33 of the 51 non-square values for $8\le n\le 13$, by up to 39.4%, and matches the rest. A cheap invariant, the row group, certifies that none of the 33 new rectangles is isotopic to rows of a group table, so the earlier column-swapping local search cannot reach any of them. Exactly, a computer-assisted branch and bound proves that the minimum imbalance of a $3\times 9$ rectangle is $56$. D\'iaz et al. found this value, but its optimality was open. A sharper pruning bound, derived from the identity $I=2\sum(d-t)^+$, reduces the search tree by a factor of $2.4$ to $3.3$ on the instances with $k\ge3$ that we solve. Asymptotically, the minimum imbalance is $\Theta(n^3)$ for every fixed $k$. A pigeonhole argument gives a lower constant of order $k\,4^{-k}$, and random rectangles give an upper constant of order $\sqrt k$. For $k=2$, the limit of $\min I/n^3$ exists, a permuton attains it, and it lies between $4/375$ and $0.1196$. Perfect balance is an $\ell_1$-equilateral problem, so it forces $k=\Omega(n/\log n)$ rows. For $2\times n$ rectangles, single two-minute annealing runs improve five of the seven six-hour MIP upper bounds for $14\le n\le 20$. Finally, the Lean 4 kernel checks every rectangle reported in this paper against a 74-line specification that imports only Lean's core library. We also prove the pigeonhole lower bound in Lean with Mathlib.

papers.title: Attraction-Ranking Mismatch in Out-of-Distribution Detection: Theory and Evidence from Hamiltonian Feature Dynamics
papers.abstract: Attracting features toward learned in-distribution (ID) regions is an intuitive strategy for out-of-distribution (OOD) detection, but does such attraction improve detection? We investigate this question using class-conditioned Hamiltonian dynamics as a controlled testbed and identify an attraction-ranking mismatch: improving individual class-affinity scores need not improve the relative ordering of ID and OOD samples. Our analysis separates misalignment between the driving field and the detection score from ranking failure that persists even when they are aligned. An exact AUROC decomposition and a local boundary analysis identify relative score changes at the ID-OOD ranking boundary as the source of first-order AUROC change under regularity conditions. Experiments demonstrate that a score-aligned rule can improve performance on a held-out source validation split yet consistently degrade it after transfer, even without a single winning-class change. A separate perturbation study finds that near-boundary relative score changes track the direction of small AUROC changes in the tested settings. Finally, centroid approximation and shared scales connect the zero-step score to a static centroid family that includes the existing CTM detector. Together, these results explain why class attraction is insufficient to justify feature refinement and motivate evaluating its effect on the ranking boundary.

papers.title: Can a self-sustaining chemical network emerge due to just a few catalysts?
papers.abstract:
Understanding how self-sustaining chemical reaction networks can emerge from simple molecules is an important question in chemical approaches to the origin of life. Reflexively autocatalytic and food-generated (RAF) sets provide a mathematical framework for investigating this question. This line of research goes back to the early work of Kauffman on autocatalytic reaction networks and was subsequently developed through the probabilistic framework of Mossel and Steel. Further contributions by Hordijk, Steel, and collaborators extended the theory to more heterogeneous forms of catalysis, including reaction-dependent probabilities or power-law distributions of catalytic activity. We introduce a stochastic model that combines heterogeneous molecular catalytic activity with reaction-dependent molecule-reaction compatibility. By assigning random catalytic weights to molecules and incorporating compatibility through an explicit formulation of catalysis probabilities, our model provides a concrete and flexible setting that captures both sources of heterogeneity while remaining mathematically tractable.
  We establish novel and general criteria for RAF formation and nonformation. We further demonstrate that classical phase-transition criteria need not remain valid in the presence of reaction-dependent catalysis. For heavy-tailed catalytic weights, we identify and rigorously quantify an additional phase transition. In models with finite-mean catalytic weights, RAF formation and nonformation are governed by a catalytic intensity parameter. For infinite-mean weights, however, we show that RAFs may emerge with probability tending to one even when the catalytic intensity parameter tends to zero.

papers.title: CARM: Conformal Adaptive Risk Masking for Reliable Scientific Super-Resolution
papers.authors: Guangtao Zhang, Haonan Wu, Junxuan Gao, Zhengyang Liu, Zhaoxi Zeng, Zhihao Li, Jianguo Huang, Zhiqiang Liu
papers.abstract: Deep learning-based super-resolution (SR) can reconstruct fine-scale Earth-observation fields from coarse observations, but reconstruction accuracy alone does not provide a calibrated rule for identifying reliable spatial regions. Conformal Mask Calibration (CMC), built on conformal risk control, converts a spatial uncertainty score into a trust mask and controls the expected worst-case local distortion under exchangeability. However, its fixed threshold can become miscalibrated in Earth-observation streams affected by seasonality and episodic events. We propose $\textit{CARM}$ (Conformal Adaptive Risk Masking), a statistical framework for adaptive spatial risk control under temporal distribution shift. CARM maintains experts with heterogeneous update rates and aggregates their threshold proposals online using an asymmetric surrogate loss, balancing rapid adaptation to distribution changes against stability during relatively stationary periods. All updates are causal and use only mature feedback available after a fixed delay, allowing CARM to operate with any SR model that provides a spatial uncertainty score. We prove that the time-averaged mask-conditioned risk converges to at most $\alpha$ at an $O(1/T)$ rate, without distributional assumptions and for any choice of aggregation weights across experts. On a daily South China Sea chlorophyll-$\textit{a}$ SR stream, CARM reduces the empirical violation rate from $43.49\%$ to $9.38\%$ and the moving-average exceedance frequency from $47.29\%$ to $1.22\%$ at $\alpha=0.10$, while retaining a non-trivial trusted region. Experiments on ERA5 wind and OSTIA sea-surface temperature further show consistent relative improvements across multiple SR backbones.

papers.title: Separation Is a Riesz Energy: How Many Environments Does ICA Need?
papers.authors: Yuda Bi, Yubo Guo, Jiaxiao Cai, Xiaonai Li, Zhuolin Li, Vince D. Calhoun
papers.abstract: Can independent components be recovered when all of them are Gaussian? Yes, if their variances change across environments; but how many environments, and how many samples as the number of components $d$ grows? We answer both for the joint diagonalization of $K$ covariances. Each component has a signature, its variances across the environments. Separating component $j$ costs the Riesz 2-energy $E_j$ of this signature, a sum, over the other components, of inverse pairwise Fisher informations. For Gaussian sources no estimator in $O(d)$ beats $cE_j/(n+E_j)$ at any $n$ and $d$, and above an explicit sample size a spectral estimator attains $E_j/n$ up to a constant, for every mixing and without the signatures (given a lower bound on the pairwise information). Since signatures live in $K-1$ dimensions, the rate obeys a dimension law: $d^2/n$, $d\log d/n$ and $d/n$ for $K=2$, $3$ and $K\ge4$ well-spread environments. What counts is the dimension the signatures span, not their number, and $\log d$ well-designed environments make $d\log d$ samples suffice. Projecting the covariances onto one linear combination pays $d^2/n$ at first order instead. In simulations up to $d=1000$ the predictions hold and joint diagonalization with $K\ge4$ attains the rate once $n/d$ is in the hundreds; on task fMRI the energy says which components are hard to separate.

papers.title: A Polynomial Erd\H{o}s-P\'osa bound for Eulerian digraphs
papers.authors: Esther Galby, Roohani Sharma, Bart van der Steenhoven
papers.abstract:
In [Combinatorica 1996], Reed, Robertson, Seymour and Thomas proved Younger's conjecture dating back to 1973 that states that directed cycles have the Erd\H{o}s-P\'osa property. Specifically, they showed that every directed graph $D$ contains either $k$ arc-disjoint cycles or a set of at most $f(k)$ arcs that intersect every directed cycle. The function $f$, depending only on $k$, is however notoriously large--in fact, not even elementary. The first improvement on this function was only very recently provided by Hatzel, Kreutzer, Milani, and Muzi [FOCS 2024] who showed that $f$ can be taken to be an exponential tower of height $8$.
  In this work, we improve this function to $O(k^4)$ in the case where the digraph is Eulerian. This also answers an open question by Wahlstr\"om [Springer Monographs in Mathematics 2018] who asked explicitly when Eulerian digraphs have a polynomial Erd\H{o}s-P\'osa property.
  The only other known result about Erd\H{o}s-P\'osa on Eulerian digraphs is a result from Seymour [Combinatorica 1996] who showed that $f(k)=k$ when the Eulerian digraph admits a linkless embedding in 3-space, and such an equality is not possible for general Eulerian digraphs. We also complement our positive result, by showing that the result of Seymour cannot be extended to give a linear bound ($O(k)$) on general Eulerian digraphs, by showing that even on Eulerian digraphs the lower bound for the Erd\H{o}s-P\'osa property is $\Omega(k \log k)$.

papers.title: An Engineering Reading of the Bounded Halting Problem and Observable Properties of a Universal Machine
papers.abstract: The halting problem asks whether a program eventually halts, with unrestricted resources. Engineering systems instead certify bounded halting: given a program, an input, and a step budget T, decide whether the program halts within T steps. This paper studies two of its uses. First, it defines an exact finite-budget problem, placing the simulated program and the checker on the same unit-cost timescale, so the checker can be embedded in an adversarial program. A diagonal argument with explicit additive overhead shows that no fixed deterministic checker decides every instance within any fixed fraction of T below one, for large T. In the nondeterministic case, T bounds the branch depth allowed for a stable observable decision. Second, bounded-halting instances give adversarial tests for finitary universality, since a universal model must support arbitrary finite computations as T grows. The tests check resource growth with T, the absence of a fixed deliberation bound, and later access to intermediate data. They separate a fixed model with extendable external resources, a model family that grows with T, and a larger system built around a fixed component. For machine-learning systems, this identifies the resource growth a universality claim assumes and whether it fails for deployed models.

papers.title: Exact certification for conic optimization over quadratic modules: partitions of unity and recession directions
papers.authors: Didier Henrion (LAAS-POP), Alaa Ibrahim (LAAS - CNRS, UT), Victor Magron (LAAS-POP, IMT, EPE UT)
papers.abstract: We consider linear conic problems whose cone is a product of truncated quadratic modules, the sum-of-squares (SOS) side of the moment-SOS hierarchy. A floating-point solution is turned into an exact rational certificate in three steps: rounding, repair of each block residual by a constant, and absorption of the constants along a recession direction of the problem. The repair relies on strict partitions of unity in the quadratic modules. We characterize their existence, relate the canonical one to the analytic center of the dual pseudo-moment cone, Christoffel-Darboux polynomials and Pell equations, and we derive closed-form rational partitions for balls and boxes. The loss incurred by the certification is the optimal value of a recession problem, equal to a support function of the masses of the dual feasible pseudomoments. The method is illustrated on polynomial optimization, volume computation and positivity of polynomials along D-finite trajectories.

papers.title: Discrete Backbone Elasticity and Curvature-Dependent Torsion Statistics in Proteins
papers.authors: Yiquan Wang, Mingyu Bian, Jiayuan Ma
papers.abstract: Coarse-grained models of protein conformational dynamics use $\mathrm{C}_\alpha$ geometry to describe the probabilities of regular helices, ordered turns and disordered conformations. To test how much of this order arises from local chain elasticity, we connect discrete Hasimoto frame transport to neighboring bending mismatch, deriving a curvature-product torsion interaction and a six-parameter generalized von Mises density. Fitted on 194 chains from the ATLAS molecular dynamics database and tested on 1744 sequence-nonredundant proteins, this baseline reduces negative log-density loss from 1.490 to 1.160 nats, torsion-sign error from 12.26 to 2.15 percentage points, and helix-fraction error from 21.84 to 10.41 points. Ablations and circular-moment projections against reference generative models motivate extensions to anisotropic stiffness and two partition-function-weighted elastic states, further lowering test loss to 0.790 nats and helix error to 1.65 points. The fixed hierarchy also improves predictions across 72 trajectories of peptides $\mathrm{Fs}$ and $(\mathrm{AAQAA})_3$ and miniprotein $\mathrm{HP35}$ spanning varied starting conformations and force fields. Remaining angular errors in these trajectories are associated with atomic context at shared bends, as bend-matched peptide frames adopt opposite torsion signs with distinct hydrogen-bond patterns and a proline-containing $\mathrm{HP35}$ turn remains at negative torsion. Introducing a bilinearly coupled $\mathrm{C}_\alpha$--$\mathrm{N}$ orientation angle largely reparameterizes the existing bend-dependent harmonics, with an empirical $L^2$ Gram projection placing 96.7\% to 99.6\% of its added coefficient-function squared norm within the original six-function span. These results link discrete Hasimoto elasticity to statistical backbone potentials and clarify the scope and limits of local $\mathrm{C}_\alpha$ geometry.

papers.title: An Exact Poisson Mixture Representation of Siler Remaining Life Expectancy
papers.abstract: The Siler model describes mortality from birth to old age as the sum of a declining immaturity hazard, a constant background hazard, and an increasing senescence hazard. No standard closed form is available for its remaining life expectancy, which must therefore be evaluated by numerical integration. We show that Siler remaining life expectancy at age $x$ is a Poisson mixture of Gompertz-Makeham remaining life expectancies, that is, a Poisson-weighted average of life expectancies in models with only a constant background hazard and an exponentially increasing senescence hazard. All components share the senescence hazard. Their background hazards increase from one component to the next by the rate at which immaturity mortality declines. The Poisson mean is the immaturity hazard that remains to be accumulated after age $x$. This representation yields an exact series of generalized exponential integrals with a closed-form bound on the truncation error. Replacing the background hazard by its discounted counterpart also gives the Laplace transform of the remaining lifetime. The mixture bounds the life expectancy lost to immaturity mortality: up to a term below the reciprocal of $a_2+b_1$, this loss equals the probability of an immaturity death times the life expectancy with the immaturity hazard removed. In annual Siler fits to Swedish female mortality, we estimate that the loss at birth fell from 4.3 years in 1900 to less than 0.01 years in 2020, which accounts for 15% of the gain in life expectancy at birth over the period.

papers.title: From hydrological laws to catchment models: A process-based model matches deep-learning accuracy on three continents
papers.abstract: Dooge asked whether hydrology has laws at the catchment scale. We ask whether a low-dimensional system built under physical laws can match the accuracy of neural networks that outperform process-based models on the same inputs. Three laws constrain a lumped catchment model. Conservation makes it a flux-connected storage network, dissipation fixes the sign of every flux and aggregation determines how the unresolved composition enters the fluxes, through effective laws over threshold distributions and a memory of the forcing. These laws admit four kinds of refinement. A parsimonious model under them, CaRT (11 parameters per catchment), is refined in a loop assisted by AI agents. Each refinement addresses an observed deficit through a hypothesis from the literature. The result, CaRT+, has fourteen states, 35 parameters per catchment and no daily neural network. Most refinements follow from aggregation over thresholds or from variables that carry no water but modulate fluxes. On 602 British and 593 US gauged catchments, single CaRT+ models reach median Nash-Sutcliffe efficiencies of 0.863 and 0.765 in held-out years. A stateful LSTM reaches 0.869 and 0.751 and an entity-aware LSTM 0.862 and 0.754, while three-seed LSTM ensembles remain ahead of the CaRT+ ensemble by 0.003-0.012 in median paired NSE. On 505 drier Australian gauged catchments unused in development, single CaRT+ models reach 0.778 against 0.762 and 0.753 for the two LSTMs. The results suggest that catchment-scale laws exist as laws of form, with the constitutive families shared and only their parameters learned.

papers.title: Complex Martensitic Microstructures in ${\rm Ti}_{76}{\rm Nb}_{22}{\rm Al}_{2}$
papers.authors: John M. Ball, Francesco Della Porta, Tomonari Inamura
papers.abstract:
We analyze the unusual microstructure resulting from the cubic to orthorhombic phase transformation in the shape-memory alloy ${\rm Ti}_{76}{\rm Nb}_{22}{\rm Al}_{2}$. This seems to represent an approximate experimental realization of a deformation having a finite number of incompatible deformation gradients, which has been known to exist only as a theoretical possibility. Because the middle eigenvalue $\gamma$ of the transformation strain is very close to 1, the phase transformation in this alloy takes place via nucleation of exact austenite-martensite interfaces rather than, as usual for other alloys, by classical austenite-martensite interfaces separating the austenite from a finely-twinned laminate of martensite. According to the moving mask approximation of Della Porta this leads to the question whether a microstructure can be formed from the set $H$ of the twelve matrices ${\mathbf V}_i$ on the martensite energy wells that are rank-one connected to the identity, even though these matrices are mutually incompatible.
  We show that when $\gamma=1$ and the transformation is volume preserving, such a microstructure is possible that does not deform the grain boundary. This is a consequence of $H$ forming a degenerate $T_{12}$ configuration in the sense of Kirchheim. In fact there are such microstructures supported on just 8 of the 12 matrices in $H$. However there is no deformation satisfying the same boundary condition whose gradient belongs to $H$ almost everywhere. An additional prediction, confirmed experimentally, is that the macroscopic deformation gradient equals the identity everywhere. We also analyse the approximate compatibility of the ${\mathbf V}_i$. Although mutually incompatible, they are nearly compatible, with some pairs much more nearly compatible than others, these pairs corresponding to interfaces that are more frequently observed.

papers.title: OSD-JSCC: Neural Joint Source-Channel Coding with One-Step Diffusion
papers.abstract: Neural joint source-channel coding (JSCC) enables efficient image transmission over noisy channels, yet distortion-optimized approaches often produce blurry reconstructions. While diffusion priors can enhance visual fidelity, their iterative sampling incurs substantial decoding latency. To address this limitation, we propose OSD-JSCC, an SNR-adaptive JSCC framework with a single diffusion step. Specifically, OSD-JSCC transmits pretrained variational autoencoder (VAE) latents through an SNR-conditioned JSCC codec and incorporates two key designs. First, we introduce a stochastic diffusion-state interface that enables the JSCC decoder to predict a Gaussian diffusion state rather than a clean latent, while extracting image-specific semantic tokens. The sampled diffusion state preserves spatial structure and provides a good initialization for one-step refinement, whereas the semantic tokens, together with an SNR token, guide the reconstruction process. Second, we develop SNR-conditioned feature modulation and adaptive timestep selection to jointly adapt latent transmission and diffusion refinement to varying channel conditions. Furthermore, we adopt a three-stage training strategy with low-rank adaptation (LoRA) to efficiently adapt the pretrained diffusion prior to the JSCC task. Extensive experiments on Kodak and CLIC2020 demonstrate that OSD-JSCC achieves superior perceptual quality and decoding efficiency. Compared with existing diffusion-based JSCC baselines, OSD-JSCC reduces LPIPS by approximately 43% on Kodak and 53% on CLIC2020, while achieving up to a 50.6$\times$ reduction in decoding latency.

papers.title: Beyond the Gap: What Imaginary-Time Evolution Reveals About the Edge of the Continuum
papers.authors: Ruben Karapetyan, Denys Bondar, Jakub Mare\v{c}ek, Ale\v{s} Wodecki
papers.abstract: The spectral gap, the energy separating the ground state from the first excitation, governs many quantum phenomena, yet it is far harder to compute than the ground state. We propose a mathematically rigorous method for extracting the gap from imaginary-time evolution in infinite-dimensional Hamiltonians, where the first excitation typically marks the edge of a continuous spectrum. We show that a gap is not automatically detected: detection depends on how the initial state and observable couple the ground state to excitations at the bottom of the continuum. When this coupling follows a power law, the gap is recovered together with a logarithmic correction whose coefficient yields the exponent of the spectral density near the edge of the continuum, which reflects the physics of the excitations. We confirm both predictions numerically for an exactly solvable model. Our results offer a new numerical approach to many-body quantum physics, in which both the gap and the threshold exponent are obtained merely at the cost of a ground-state calculation.

papers.title: A general technique for explicit quantile representations
papers.abstract: This work proves existence of contours independent of probability level for exact quantile integrals of strictly positive real-analytic densities. Explicit constructions cover five broad distribution families and yield a finite-interval representation of Black-Scholes implied volatility using forward functions.

papers.title: Phase Locking in Oscillator Networks with Uncertain and State-Dependent Couplings
papers.authors: Iva Ba\v{c}i\'c, Philipp C. B\"ottcher, Marc Hunkem\"oller, Carsten Hartmann, David Gross, Andrea Benigni, Dirk Witthaut
papers.abstract: Phase locking in oscillator networks depends critically on the interaction strengths between coupled units. In many applications, however, these couplings are uncertain, state dependent, or time varying. We derive rigorous conditions for phase locking in Kuramoto-type networks when each coupling strength is known only within prescribed bounds. Building on a convex formulation of the nonlinear fixed-point equations, we obtain edge-wise error bounds for arbitrary feasible approximations that hold uniformly over all admissible couplings. These bounds yield sufficient conditions for the existence of phase-locked states with prescribed phase-difference limits. We illustrate the framework for AC power grids with uncertain voltage magnitudes and adaptive oscillator networks with state-dependent couplings. For the latter, the bounds can be further tightened by exploiting the state dependence of the couplings.

papers.title: A $2.81^n$ upper bound on the number of stable matchings
papers.abstract: We study the maximum number ${\rm SM}(n)$ of stable matchings in an instance with $n$ men and $n$ women. Karlin, Oveis Gharan, and Weber (STOC 2018) proved the first single-exponential upper bound; their argument gives ${\rm SM}(n)\le 2^{17n}$ for sufficiently large $n$. Palmer and P\'alv\"olgyi (FOCS 2021) improved this bound to $3.55^n+O(1)$. We prove that ${\rm SM}(n)<2.81^n$. This brings the exponential base closer to $2.28$, the base of the best known lower bound. More precisely, we bound the number of stable matchings in each instance in terms of each person's number of stable partners, where a stable partner is someone matched to that person in at least one stable matching. Our proof assigns each person a weight determined by this number and uses these weights to bound the number of stable matchings by induction.

papers.title: Constrained defined-contribution pension management: A reparameterized neural network approach
papers.abstract: This paper studies constrained defined contribution (DC) pension management under a two-factor financial market model. The pension participant is allowed to invest in cash, two nominal bonds, an inflation-linked bond, and a stock index. Moreover, they can also purchase term life insurance to manage pre-retirement death risk. Unlike traditional literature, we consider a pension member restricted to a general non-empty, closed, and convex trading constraint set that includes no short-selling, no borrowing, and portfolio-mix constraints as special cases. Such restrictions reflect common limits on pension-account trading. To solve the problem, we construct a family of unconstrained artificial markets, in which the original trading constraints are satisfied by adjusting the drift terms of the risky assets. Using a duality transformation, we derive the Lagrangian dual problem and propose a reparameterized neural network method to compute lower and upper bounds on the primal value function. We calibrate our model with U.S. data using a Kalman filter method, and find that our method produces a smaller duality gap than the benchmark methods. We also compare the constrained results with the unconstrained explicit solution and find that trading constraints substantially change wealth accumulation, portfolio strategies, and insurance demand.
